General Syndulla, please report to the briefing room.|Syndulla called into the briefing room over the Great Temple loudspeakers|}} Hera returned to the Alliance after Lothal. After the Alliance learned of the Death Star, Hera was called to the command room at [[Great Temple|Base One]]. Shortly after, Hera participated in the [[Battle of Scarif]]''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know, Updated and Expanded]]'' alongside Orrelios,{{SW|url=news/who-is-zeb|text=Who is Zeb?}} where she flew the ''Ghost'',{{HelmetCollectionCite|79|Highlights of the Saga}} and in the time before the [[Battle of Yavin]], Hera vouched for the skills of Antilles as an ace fighter pilot.{{StoryCite|story=Grounded|book=From a Certain Point of View}} She worked with Orrelios throughout the Galactic Civil War. ===Galactic Civil War=== ====Kidnapped by mercenaries==== {{Quote|I ''knew'' the general would find a way to activate her ''tracker!'' Commence attack on the kidnappers' vess—|Bini directs a rescue mission for Syndulla|}} [[File:HeraKidnapped-2016DoctorAphra17.jpg|thumb|352x352px|Hera captured by Aphra.]] Sometime after the Battle of Yavin, General Syndulla was stationed on the [[Lucrehulk-class battleship|''Lucrehulk''-class Battleship]] ''[[Lucrehulk Prime]]'' which was being used as a flight school by the Rebel Alliance. There she helped train new recruits into [[rebel pilot]]s. However, a group of mercenaries working for the [[Son-tuul Pride]], led by [[Chelli Lona Aphra|Chelli Aphra]], came to the flight school. They were first mistaken for recruits by [[Alliance officer]] [[Bini]], who gave a tour of the ship. As they got to the control center, Aphra's [[Tooka]] ran to the control terminal where Syndulla was and Syndulla killed it. When Syndulla came to them, [[Tam Posla]] said they had a proposal and she realized who they really were.[[Doctor Aphra (2016) 17|''Doctor Aphra'' (2016) 17]] Syndulla had the group detained for the time being until they managed to disable the shield encasing them in the cell. They did not go out of the cell however, and Syndulla decided to listen to their proposal. But as Posla was about to explain, his subordinate (and lover) [[Caysin Bog]] released a number of blasters set to stun out of his compartment. [[Sister Six]] used them to stun all the rebels in the room including Syndulla. They then bound and gagged Syndulla, in addition to placing a gift bow on her head, before fleeing with her captive. Their plan was to use Syndulla as a bargaining chip to get into [[Hivebase-1]], the R&D Headquarters for the [[Tarkin Initiative]]. There they hoped to find the lost memories of Son-tuul Pride's leader [[0-0-0]]. As they approached Hivebase-1, Aphra was fixing Bog's diagnostics and Posla told the crew of his hunt for [[Doctor]] [[Cornelius Evazan]]. When he tried to describe how attached he was to the case, Syndulla called him overdramatic. When Posla and Bog talked of a happy ending after they brought justice to Evazan, Syndulla told them there was no happy ending as long as they worked for Aphra and told them the rebellion would have mercy if they let her go. Aphra then revealed she had turned on the tracker on Syndulla's general's plaque. Syndulla was shocked at this and when Sister Six confirmed the ''Lucrehulk Prime''{{'s}} approach, she called Aphra a dreadful woman. The ''Lucrehulk Prime'' arrived and found itself swarmed by the [[scaraphyte]]s surrounding Hivebase-1. The ship's arrival distracted the Imperial defenses and Aphra used it as her chance to get into Hivebase-1. Once on there Posla asked what they were going to do with Syndulla, and Aphra said she did not mind as she had done her part. Syndulla was surprised to hear she wasn't really being handed over, and Aphra told her that she was only an excuse to get them into Hivebase-1.[[Doctor Aphra (2016) 18|''Doctor Aphra'' (2016) 18]] The group began searching and found a room of frozen rejected prototypes. Aphra admired them deeply and Syndulla was confused as to why. Aphra told Syndulla she was a scientist and liked "how" more than "why." She then decided to use a detached cyborg to eavesdrop on the ''Lucrehulk Prime''{{'s}} comm chatter. They heard [[officer]] Bini reporting disaster after disaster until he was knocked unconscious by an Imperial infiltrator on the ship, [[Lieutenant-Inspector]] [[Magna Tolvan]]. Tolvan contacted the command center of Hivebase-1 declaring the ''Lucrehulk Prime'' commandeered by her. Commander [[Yewl]] told her to destroy the ship but Aphra did not want that to happen and talked over the comm to convince Tolvan otherwise. Tolvan, being close to Aphra, agreed with Aphra and used an Imperial protocol to deny Yewl's order, but in doing so, revealed that Aphra and the others were in the base. Around Syndulla and the others, the prototypes defrosted and open fired on them, disabling [[Dek-Nil]]. The others took cover and Aphra demanded that Posla use his weapons to save them, but he refused, saying the prototypes had done nothing wrong. Aphra then ordered everyone to go back to their ship, and as they began to leave, Syndulla noticed Aphra pressing a button on the cyborg headset. At that moment, Bog turned around and advanced towards the prototypes, and as Posla asked what he was doing, he was gunned down. Infuriated, Posla began semi-detaching all of his robotic and cyborg limbs, revealing his complement of weapons. Syndulla asked Aphra what she had done but she butted in and prompted the others to leave as Posla fought the prototypes. Syndulla and the remaining of Aphra's crew made it to the core of Hivebase-1 where they began searching the database for 0-0-0's memories. As they did so, Posla returned asking himself why Bog would just run towards the prototypes so impulsively. Syndulla said she had a hypothesis, but Aphra told her to shut up. Syndulla then confronted Aphra about how she had programmed Bog to run to his death when she fixed his diagnostics earlier on. Aphra again told her to shut up and had Sister Six give her a gun in case they had company. Syndulla took the gun and pointed it at Aphra. However, she was zapped and the gun fell out her hands. The four turned around to see Commander Yewl with a squad of death troopers and [[Hutt clone trooper]]s. Yewl ordered Syndulla's capture and the deaths of the others, and his troopers opened fire. Syndulla used Aphra as a human shield as Sister Six returned fire. Posla remained dormant behind a terminal, still traumatized by Bog's death. Aphra gave Syndulla her gun back and she open fired on Yewl and his squad whilst Aphra tampered with the terminal.[[Doctor Aphra (2016) 19|''Doctor Aphra'' (2016) 19]] Aphra began putting her plan into action: When she chased her Tooka to the control center of ''Lucrehulk Prime'' when she first met Syndulla, she had bugged the system. She used this to her advantage and had the ''Lucrehulk Prime'' attach itself to the data core of Hivebase-1. It's tractor beam then pulled the core out and at Aphra's ship, she had a box of shrink frozen Tookas, the Tookas escaped and ran around the base. Dek-Nil sprung to life after being disabled earlier on and used a grappling hook to latch onto the data core. The Tookas then detonated at the same time and blew up Hivebase-1. Once back on ''Lucrehulk Prime'' again, Bini was keen to have Aphra and the others killed. However, Syndulla was very proud of what Aphra had done, and she had obtained the core of Hivebase-1 for them, which had data that could change the course of the war. She let them leave peacefully and Sister Six decided to stay with the rebellion. Posla told Syndulla that Tolvan was still in the vents before the rest of them set off. Syndulla sent a search party there to find her but the troopers found it was Posla himself and Tolvan had taken his armor. They then began slicing into the data core and found that Aphra had encrypted the data and ransomed it. ====Mission to obtain the decryption codes==== [[File:SyndullaStarrosHolo-2016DoctorAphra21.jpg|thumb|left|328x328px|Syndulla talks to Starros]] Aphra managed to get 0-0-0's memories back to him. However, Tolvan betrayed her and [[Second attack on the Son-tuul Pride|attacked]] the Son-tuul Pride. 0-0-0 escaped and found that Aphra had encrypted his memories as well. Aphra was captured and held in [[Accresker Jail]], where she was forced to serve a convict army called the [[Accresker Penal Legion]]. After an [[attack on an EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate]],[[Doctor Aphra (2016) 20|''Doctor Aphra'' (2016) 20]] Syndulla's people recovered a droid lost during the engagement and found the holo-image of Aphra. Desperately needing the decryption codes for the data core, she then contacted [[Sana Starros]] and offered her a job to get Aphra out of jail.[[Doctor Aphra (2016) 21|''Doctor Aphra'' (2016) 21]] Starros tracked Aphra's convict army to the scene of a [[Unidentified pirate station|pirate station]] that had been crippled of its weapons by three ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers. As Starros waited for the Accresker Penal Legion to board the space station, she spoke to Syndulla. Syndulla asked Starros what her deal with Aphra was and Starros replied by asking her if she had ever cared about someone so much that it scared her just to think about them. She then described it as a vulnerable chunk of herself walking around separate from her body where she cannot protect it, and that if it's hurt, then it's because of something that she has said or done. Then she described it further as putting all her weakness in a box and getting used to not watching it all the time until it stabbed her right in the kidney, set fire to her trust, and jumped up and down on it forever. Starros finished explaining it and asked Syndulla if she ever had that and when no reply came, she stated that love was like fireworks and flew her ship towards the pirate station as the battle began. ====Assembling a fleet==== {{Quote|Gamma group is good. Ready when you are.|Syndulla reports back to Mako-Ta Space Docks|}} [[File:RebelCouncil-2015StarWars45.jpg|thumb|right|233x233px|Syndulla attended a rebel meeting with Zeb]] Syndulla and Zeb later attended an Alliance High Command meeting at the [[Mako-Ta Space Docks]]. There, Mothma requested an update from Leia Organa about their mission to [[Mon Cala]] and Organa said it was unsuccessful. However, she revealed that she knew the location of where the Mon Calamari [[Mon Calamari monarchy|king]], [[Lee-Char]] was being held. She further proposed to go on a mission to rescue the [[king]] and inspire his people to rise against the Empire, to which Mothma agreed.[[Star Wars (2015) 45|''Star Wars'' (2015) 45]] Organa and her team were successful in inspiring the [[Mon Cala Mercantile Fleet]] to [[Mutiny on Mon Cala|rebel]], which obtained the Alliance many [[Star Cruiser]]s that were refitted at Mako-Ta with the help of [[Queen]] [[Trios]] of [[Shu-Torun]]. Hera was given command of the cruiser [[Geist (cruiser)|''Geist'']],[[Star Wars (2015) 55|''Star Wars'' (2015) 55]] as well as the other ships in [[Gamma Group]]. ====Attack on the Mako-Ta Spacedocks==== {{Quote|General Syndulla here. My cruiser's up and ready. The override codes are distributing to the rest…hey, Dodonna? What's the plan?''"
"''Wait for the remaining cruisers to reboot and then go. Everyone has their secure destinations. Finish the plan. Disperse the fleet.''"
"''You heard the man. And until then? ''Let's give the Empire a taste!''|General Syndulla and Jan Dodonna|}} During a celebration of the new ships, they prepared to scatter the fleet to keep it safe. However, when attempting to jump to hyperspace, the ships' systems failed to respond. Around the same time, [[Death Squadron]] under the command of Vader [[Battle of Mako-Ta|arrived]]. The cruisers began scrambling their starfighters, but realized the hanger doors were not opening. The ''[[Executor]]'' then destroyed General [[Vanden Huyck Willard|Vanden Willard's]] flagship ''[[Yavin's Hope]]''. It was then revealed that Queen Trios was a traitor and the Shu-Torun tech was defective. [[File:GammaGroup-2015StarWars50.png|thumb|left|293x293px|Syndulla was put in charge of Gamma Group]] Hera and the crew of the ''Geist'' could only sit defenseless and watch as Death Squadron decimated the rebel fleet, sending rebel leaders like [[Lajaie]] and [[Bob Hudsol]] to their fiery demises. Eventually, though, Leia Organa was able to retrieve the override codes and send them to the fleet.[[Star Wars (2015) 54|''Star Wars'' (2015) 54]] Hera's cruiser was one of the first to get its systems back online. Hera ordered her crew to give the Empire hell as the other cruisers were still restoring their systems. The whole fleet was able to get their systems functioning again and they jumped to hyperspace, save for General Dodonna's cruiser, which was disabled during the battle and later destroyed. ====Aftermath of Mako-Ta==== Following the devastation that occurred at Mako-Ta and the scattering of the fleet, Hera was sent reinforcements in the form of [[Clan Markona]],[[Star Wars (2015) 61|''Star Wars'' (2015) 61]] who had joined the Alliance after [[Task Force 99|SCAR Squadron]] [[Skirmish on Hubin|attacked]] their isolationist moon of [[Hubin]].[[Star Wars (2015) 60|''Star Wars'' (2015) 60]] ====Time on Hoth==== {{Quote|Your technique is not the issue, Leia. You need to see your tauntaun as a partner, not impose your command on it.''"
"''We're running out of time, Hera, and the success of this mission is crucial. I won't let it be compromised by a juvenile, stubborn—|Hera Syndulla and Leia Organa, on tauntauns|''[[Forces of Destiny—Leia]]''}} [[File:HeraHanLeiaRideTauntaunsOnHoth-FODLeia.png|thumb|right|250px|Solo, Syndulla, and Organa scout the frigid plains of Hoth for a lost Rebel ship.]] In [[3 ABY]], Hera was stationed on [[Hoth]] for a period of time, alongside other members of the Rebel Alliance, and she went on a mission to retrieve parts to repair the [[power generator]]s, just before the Empire deployed a [[viper probe droid]] to the planet. ====Unknown contact==== {{Quote|Heh. You sound like Kanan.''"
"''Is that a good thing?''"
"''Usually.|Hera Syndulla and Luke Skywalker|[[Star Wars (2020) 28|''Star Wars'' (2020) 28]]}} [[File:HerasBriefing-2020StarWars27.png|250px|thumb|left|Syndulla leads a briefing for the Rebellion.]] Following the [[Battle of Hoth]] and the [[Unity Day attack|attack]] on [[Bar'leth]] during Unity Day, Syndulla attended a meeting with Admiral Ackbar, Mothma, Organa, and [[Commodore]] [[Grek (commodore)|Grek]] during which they discussed the Alliance's surviving forces and their need to rebuild their supply lines.[[Star Wars (2020) 26|''Star Wars'' (2020) 26]] Syndulla later led a briefing to the members of the Alliance about a list of new intelligence hits they got since their last briefing. Amongst the list, Syndulla stated that the first three were promising and that she had a team running it down, while the rest were classified as too speculative. The Jedi [[Luke Skywalker]] then raised his hand and asked about "number five." Syndulla responded that it was about some people claiming to be defectors, trying to sell classified Imperial weapons data. She asked Skywalker if anything about it stood out to him, to which he responded that he had a good feeling about it.[[Star Wars (2020) 27|''Star Wars'' (2020) 27]] After the briefing, Syndulla and Skywalker continued to discuss the transmission in private, along with Commodore Grek. Unsure, Syndulla asked Skywalker whether the transmission from the defectors was something to pay attention to, adding if he sensed it through the Force. Skywalker said that he started to figure out that everything was connected through the Force, to which Syndulla remarked that the Jedi reminded her of Jarrus. Grek then ordered an officer to pull up everything about the contact. The officer told them that one of their [[relay station]]s picked up a signal from two individuals, claiming to be Imperial defectors. They wanted to exchange information about secret weapons site for safe passage and protection. The officer added that the connection was dropped after being told to wait for authorization by the rebels, showing hesitation to go further with the signal. Syndulla then asked if that was all they had. The officer tracked the defector's shuttle signature per standard procedure, revealing the ship's name, ''[[Scopium]]''. Digging further, Syndulla and the rest learned that the Imperial put up a system-wide alert on the shuttle, adding its legitimacy. The officer told them that the shuttle jumped into the [[Al'doleem system]] for a bit and quickly jumped back into hyperspace after alerting an Imperial base on [[Al'doleem]], before arriving on Coruscant. Skywalker proposed to go to Coruscant for a [[Mission to reveal the Death Star II|rescue mission]], though Grek and Syndulla fought against it. Syndulla told Skywalker that there were bounties on him throughout the galaxy, adding that he was also a valuable member of the Rebellion. Understanding the risk of the mission, the Jedi still fought for himself to go, with a confirmation from their spies that the Emperor and Vader were currently not present on Coruscant. When asked about his plan of action, Skywalker explained to Syndulla and Grek that he was going to disguise himself as an Imperial officer. Convinced by his reasoning, both Syndulla and Grek approved the Jedi's rescue mission, going to Coruscant soon after. [[File:LukeRevealsDeathStarII-2020StarWars28.png|300px|thumb|right|Syndulla learns about the existence of the second Death Star.]] Later, Skywalker returned from Coruscant back to the Rebel Alliance fleet, having successfully rescued the defectors. Syndulla, Ackbar, and Mothma met up with Skywalker for updates on what he learned from his mission. The Jedi told the three individuals that General Organa should hear what he had to say, asking for her whereabouts. Ackbar told him that she was in a different [[sector]] with another division, Mothma added that she could pass the message along instead. Skywalker then proceeded to reveal that the defectors were a family, with the parents being undercover agents of the criminal syndicate [[Crimson Dawn]]. He added that the couple, [[Bevelyn]] and [[Jon Melton]], worked as a cargo specialist and a primary [[aide]] at a [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|top-secret weapons facility]], respectively. Syndulla was shocked by the revelation and speculated that the leader of Crimson Dawn [[Lady]] [[Qi'ra]] probably had spies everywhere. Ackbar immediately tried to suggest their course of action about the Crimson Dawn spies, though Mothma interrupted the admiral, asking Skywalker what he had to tell them. The Jedi revealed that the Empire was building another Death Star, to which the whole room went silent with complete shock and uncertainty on their faces. Despite the shocking revelation, Mothma was still optimistic that the Rebel Alliance had a chance. ====Supplies on Endor==== {{Quote|I'll give you the ration sticks…if…you…say it.''"
"''What? No! I'm not gonna say it.''"
"''Okay then. Give my regards to General Organa.''"
"''Mmm, fine.''"
"''Hmm.''"
"''Ugh. The ''Ghost'' is a superior ship to the ''Falcon''.''"
"''Wow. We finally agree on something.|Hera Syndulla and Han Solo|{{FOD|An Imperial Feast}}}} [[File:Hera_and_Han.jpg|thumb|left|270px|Hera gives Han Solo and Chewbacca the ration bars for the Ewoks.]] In [[4 ABY]], the Emperor went to personally oversee the construction of the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|second Death Star]] above the [[forest]] moon of [[Endor]]. A major [[Battle of Endor|battle]] broke out above the moon and on its surface between the Rebel Alliance and the Galactic Empire. Eventually, the Empire was defeated, with the destruction of the second Death Star and the Emperor's death. After the battle, Rebels went to celebrate on the moon with the indigenous [[Ewok]]s, who helped win the battle on the surface.{{Film|VI}} Over a period of time, the Ewoks grew hungry and attempted to eat some of the stormtroopers captured on the moon. General Organa wrestled to stop them from doing so and tried to teach them how to treat the enemy fairly, though achieving little results. Organa tasked General [[Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca]] to go to [[General Syndulla's camp]] and ask Hera for [[ration bar]]s to help feed the hungry Ewoks. The two reluctantly went to Hera, but she would only give him the rations if Solo admitted that the ''Ghost'' was a better ship than the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'', which he admitted to. Hera gave them permission to take the rations and left to board her ship. Solo and Chewbacca would come back to General Organa and save the stormtroopers from the Ewoks' hunger. ====Defending Bright Tree Village==== [[File:HeraVsTIEs.png|thumb|right|300px|Hera engages TIEs in the skies of Endor.]] After running a [[comm/scan processor]] of the area, Hera alerted Chopper that Imperial TIEs had been spotted heading toward [[Bright Tree Village]]. Chopper complained about their lack of crew, but Hera subsided the inquiry and continued on with the mission, boarding the ''Ghost''. Ignoring her, Chopper looked to the Ewoks he had been practicing with and decided to bring them along for the mission. The ''Ghost'' took off from the forests of Endor, but was immediately attacked by the surviving TIEs. As the TIEs swung back around, Hera ordered Chopper to get to the guns, who then revealed his new crew of [[Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka|Kneesaa]] and another Ewok. Hera was originally reluctant to the idea of letting them man the guns, but eventually relented. As the Ewoks began to fire the guns, the TIEs began to subside and were eventually destroyed by the Ewoks. Returning to the cockpit, Hera complimented the Ewoks and brought them back to their village.{{FOD|Chopper and Friends}} Hera later attended the [[wedding of Han Solo and Leia Organa]].''[[Someone Who Loves You]]'' ====Serving the New Republic==== {{Quote|Hello, Vanguard. Welcome to the Nadiri Dockyards.|Hera Syndulla, to Vanguard Squadron|}} [[File:HeraSquadrons.png|thumb|left|227px|Hera welcoming Vanguard Squadron to the Nadiri Dockyards.]] Syndulla eventually joined the New Republic, the successor government to the Rebel Alliance, where she continued to serve as a general, leading [[Barma Battle Group]] from her new flagship ''[[Lodestar]]''. With the Republic on the verge of victory in the Galactic Civil War, Syndulla was approached by [[New Republic Intelligence]] Agent [[Caern Adan]], who wanted to station his newly assembled [[Alphabet Squadron]] on the ''Lodestar'' so they could [[Hunt for Shadow Wing|track down]] and destroy the [[204th Imperial Fighter Wing]], a mysterious and lethal force of TIE fighters who were exacting bloody and reckless vengeance in the twilight of the Empire's reign. Syndulla agreed so long as she was able to command the squadron, since it was onboard her ship. Adan agreed to help supply intelligence to guide Syndulla's efforts to destroy Shadow Wing. [[File:HeraSyndulla-SWS.png|thumb|right|227px|Hera Syndulla shortly after the Battle of Endor]] After Alphabet Squadron's [[mission to Abednedo]] went awry, Syndulla met with the squadron's leader, [[Yrica Quell]], a former Imperial TIE pilot. She told Quell that she could not expect her new comrades to fly like Imperials, and had to embrace the fact that they were creative, improvisational, and needed her to trust them. After giving Quell advice, she assigned the squadron with a supply run to a [[Unidentified moon (Harkrova I)|moon]] of the planet [[Harkrova I]] in the [[Harkrova system]]. Not only was the mission to help resupply Barma Battle Group, but Syndulla intended for the new squadron to grow closer to each other with the experience. Meanwhile, Syndulla continued to lead Barma Battle Group, who took the [[Treinhaus Citadel]] on the planet [[Argai Minor]]. When Alphabet Squadron returned successfully, Syndulla was happy to discover the squadron experienced a phenomena at the [[Unidentified temple (Harkrova system)|temple]] on the planet and had returned with greater trust and belief in each other. At some point, Syndulla and her battle group went to the Ringali Nebula for [[Project Starhawk]] and welcomed [[Vanguard Squadron]] to the [[Nadiri Dockyards]], which later came under attack from [[Titan Squadron]]. ====End of the War==== {{Quote|I've never seen them fight that way before.''"
"''We never came at them in a Star Destroyer before.|Wyl Lark and Hera Syndulla, on Shadow Wing|}} Syndulla participated in the final stretch of the Galactic Civil War, but this ultimately caused her to be separated from her son Jacen. She eventually fought in the [[Battle of Jakku]],''[[Victory's Price: An Alphabet Squadron Novel]]'' which occurred in [[5 ABY]]. She served aboard her [[flagship]] the Star Destroyer ''[[Deliverance]]'', where Syndulla gathered two corvettes and several transports and moved to escort the ground forces to the surface to begin landing troops. One TIE bomber slipped through Syndulla's defenses and attacked the ''Deliverance'', though the fighter did not do much damage, the impact had caused captain [[Nisteen Arvad]] to fall and bleed out. But after it was critically damaged by the 204th Imperial Fighter Wing and [[Palal Seedia]]'s explosive that was detonated within the starship, Hera boarded the ''Ghost'' to continue the battle. During the ensuing fighting, Syndulla had a near-death experience and thought of Jacen during what she believed to be her last moments. ===New Republic era=== ====The Hunt for Thrawn==== =====Debrief on ''Home One''===== {{Quote|General Syndulla... it's good to see you.''"
"''And you. Though I wish it were under more pleasant circumstances. I'm afraid we've lost your prisoner. I've prepared a briefing to get you caught up.|Ahsoka Tano, and Hera Syndulla|{{Ahsoka|Part One: Master and Apprentice}}}} [[File:Hera_debriefing.png|left|thumb|250x250px|Hera Syndulla met with Ahsoka Tano aboard ''Home One'']] At some point, Syndulla and Chopper ventured to [[Black Spire Outpost]]{{Twitter|starwars|status/1700216005216317539|''[[Star Wars]]''|quote=space mom has arrived Meet Hera Syndulla for a limited-time in Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge® at the @Disneyland Resort.}} on the planet''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' [[Batuu]]. In [[9 ABY]],{{AhsokaDate|1}} General Syndulla arrived on ''[[Home One]]'' to meet with Ahsoka Tano. One of the ships in the fleet's rendezvous had been boarded by two lightsaber-wielding foes, its crew slaughtered to a man. [[Morgan Elsbeth]], a prisoner that they ship had been carrying, was stolen and the ship scuttled. Her and Ahsoka met on ''Home One'' to debrief the situation. Hera recalled that it was almost like old times in the Rebellion. Both of them discussed the situation with the missing prisoner and the starmap that Ahsoka had gathered. The former Jedi explained that Thrawn's return could lead to a massive revival in military power for the [[Imperial Remnant|Imperial Remnants]] and warlords that scattered the galaxy. System after system could fall to a fresh Imperial counterattack led by one of the greatest military minds to ever exist. Hera suggested that she seek out Sabine Wren on Lothal for a possible apprenticeship and to help her track down Ezra Bridger. =====Speaking with Tano===== {{Quote|I just wish she had changed a little. But she's still just as stubborn and bullish as ever.''"
"''She's Mandalorian. You knew what you were getting into.''"
"''I thought I did.|Ahsoka Tano and Hera Syndulla|{{Ahsoka|Part One: Master and Apprentice}}}} Ahsoka contacted her after meeting with Sabine Wren several days later, concerned that this was maybe a mistake. Sabine had run off with the starmap after the former Jedi had explicitly told her not to leave. Hera insisted on Sabine's behalf, saying that if anyone knew how to find Ezra, it would be Sabine. Hera would be proved right shortly after. However, Sabine was shortly attacked by several [[HK-87 assassin droid]]s and a dark side force user. In the ensuing melee, Sabine was heavily wounded and the starmap lost. Hera was notified via hologram about the stolen map. =====Corellian Shipyard Investigation===== {{Quote|What a mess? How can they still be loyal to the Empire?''"
"''It's not loyalty. It's greed.|Hera Syndulla and Ahsoka Tano|{{Ahsoka|Part Two: Toil and Trouble}} }} [[File:AhsokaChopperHera-Ahsoka-PartTwo.png|thumb|right|250px|Hera and Chopper met with Ahsoka on Corellia]] Ahsoka Tano went on a mission after Sabine had managed to activate the memory circuit of one of the assassin droids. Hera and Ahsoka left for [[Corellia]]'s [[Facility 301G|shipyards]] after realizing that Morgan Elsbeth had owned manufacturing plants there. Hera met with one of the Regional Supervisors, [[Myn Weaver]], to discuss possible Imperial remnant activity. Weaver stated that he was particularly busy at the moment, but Syndulla pressed him, stating that this would be a far more formal investigation if she could not do so immediately. Weaver took them on a [[REV-2K personnel carrier]] through the production plant, telling them the insides of his operation. During the ride, he was questioned on the loyalty of his workers (most of them had been employed by the Empire) to which he replied that average workers did not care about galactic politics. After this, Hera suggested that Tano take Sabine back on as an apprentice. Tano replied that neither of them was ready for that. Still, Hera believed it would be good for both of them, saying that Wren needed some structure in her life and so did Tano. Once Myn Weaver showed them into the control center, Tano asked about the purpose and clients of the manufacturing center. While Weaver was explaining the priority given to shareholders, Hera spotted a massive hyperdrive core. Weaver explained that it had been extracted from a [[Super Star Destroyer]]. Hera was befuddled since the New Republic had not been constructing anything of that size. Weaver checked the logs and explained that it was of a classified nature and that it needed approval before he could unseal it. The supervisor asked for the protocol droid [[C1-D1]] to explain the regulation surrounding it. Tano questioned him on the other types of droids in use, but the protocol droid interjected by stating that she had been interrupted by an HK earlier. The protocol droid stated that it was on the transport about to leave with the massive hyperspace core. Hera ordered the flight crew to stop the ship from leaving the planet, but the crew, and even Myn Weaver, had actually been Imperial loyalists the entire time. Several drew pistols in an attempt to kill the general, but Tano's lightning-fast reflexes had dispatched all of them in seconds. Hera rushed to the ''Phantom II'' to stop the transport as soon as possible. Tano leaped out of the window, sprinting towards the rapidly ascending transport, but an assassin droid and a former Imperial Inquisitor named [[Marrok]], who was working for Elsbeth as a mercenary, stood in her way. Meanwhile, Chopper and Hera had launched the ship and ordered the transport to stand down. The transport crew was not particularly excited about this news, as they instantly opened fire. Hera could not simply shoot the ship down and crash it into the city below, but she also could not simply let it escape either. Hera sped the ''Phantom II'' straight toward the escaping transport, and Chopper chucked a tracking device onto it right before it launched into hyperspace. Tano had dueled the two Imperials, destroying the HK droid and forcing the Force wielder to escape onto a shuttle that had almost blasted the former Jedi to death. After this, both of them watched over as dozens of Imperial spies and Weaver were arrested by New Republic security forces. Tano stated that it wasn't simply loyalty that drove them, it was greed. Hera stayed back on Corellia as Tano took her ship back to Lothal to meet up with Sabine. Then, the new apprentice joined her master in tracking the Imperials. ====Meeting with the Chancellor==== [[File:HamatoZiono-RFGE.png|thumb|left|250px|Syndulla had an antagonistic relationship with Senator Hamato Xiono.]] {{Quote|Did you ever fight in the war senator?|Hera Syndulla, to Xiono|{{Ahsoka|Part Three: Time to Fly}}}} After the events on Corellia, Syndulla returned to Home One for a discussion with New Republic Senators, leaving her son, Jacen, to play with Chopper. Chancellor Mothma greeted the general, but Senator Hamato Xiono interrupted Syndulla's response, stating that they should begin immediately due to a lack of time. Syndulla reported the events on Corellia and linked them to the rumors regarding Thrawn's return. A surprised Mothma questioned the possibility, before Xiono suggested that Syndulla was wasting resources to give in to her personal feelings. The two exchanged subtle insults before Syndulla publicly questioned Xionos' integrity for being absent throughout the war. As a result, her request was denied, which she reported back to Tano. ====Unauthorized mission to Seatos==== Knowing full well that Ahsoka and Wren would not endanger themselves chasing mere rumors, Hera took the ''Ghost,'' Jacen, Chopper, and a squadron of X-Wings with her to Seatos to ascertain the truth herself. [[Carson Teva]] joined her on the mission. By the time they arrived to the system, they witnessed the ''[[Eye of Sion]]'' about to jump to hyperspace, right in front of them. Unable to stop the hyperspace ring in time, the squadron took evasive action, but a few of them were destroyed as the Eye jumped.{{Ahsoka|Part Four: Fallen Jedi}} Landing on the surface of an altar, Hera was able to determine that a battle had taken place there, but both Ahsoka and Wren were nowhere to be seen. The only things she was able to recover were the remains of the Star Map and Wren's helmet. However, Jacen was able to hear something in the waves. He called out to Hera to listen as well. At first, Hera heard nothing, but as Jacen insisted, he heard lightsaber crackling. Hera listened more closely and also heard it faintly. She ordered Carson to sweep the nearby area and the ocean. After multiple sweeps, the squadron still found nothing until Hera told Chopper to scan. Chopper was eventually able to pick up something with Jacen's direction, and eventually, Hera was able to extract Ahsoka from the ocean, injured but alive. After Ahsoka recovered, she briefed Hera about what had happened; she and Wren attempted to stop Morgan Elsbeth, but as she tried to grab the map, her hand was burned, and Baylan Skoll pushed her down from the cliff. She had urged Wren to destroy the map, but apparently she did not, which allowed the ''Eye of Sion'' to leave. Both women believed that Sabine is alive, but they had no way to follow her, until Ahsoka came up with the idea to ask purrgils to follow the Eye. Hera and Jacen watched as Ahsoka talked with purrgils with the Force. Just then, the New Republic fleet arrived to investigate Hera's actions. Hera told Carson to stall them until Ahsoka can get the purrgils to take her. This worked and purrgils began to head towards the coordinates, where the Eye had jumped earlier. The fleet was forced to move out of the way. Hera wished Ahsoka good luck as she promised to find Sabine and Ezra. [[File:ThreepioTevaSyndullaCourt-Ahsoka-PartSeven.png|thumb|right|250px|On behalf of Leia Organa, C-3PO acquitted Hera of her charges in court]] Following Seatos, Hera was brought to Coruscant,{{Ahsoka|Part Seven: Dreams and Madness}} the governmental center for the New Republic,''[[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]'' to answer for her actions in front of a court headed by Mon Mothma and Senator Xiono. Xiono was more than willing to strip Hera of command and imprison her. Even Carson Teva's claim that the Imperial Remnants were up to something based on Moff Gideon's actions on Mandalore was ignored. But thanks to C-3PO, who interceded on behalf of Senator Leia Organa, Hera was acquitted of all charges. Mon Mothma then talked with Hera and asked how real the return of Thrawn was. Hera said they must hope for the best and prepare for the worst. ====Reuniting with an old friend==== Some time after the trial, Hera was back at Home One when a shuttle was escorted into its hangar. Gathering an armed welcoming party, the shuttle's bay door opened, and from it, a single stormtrooper emerged with his hands up. Hera and her party raised their weapons towards the trooper, but Chopper noticed something familiar about the trooper. He went to him, and the trooper placed his hand on the droid. The trooper then took off his helmet and revealed himself to be Ezra Bridger in disguise. Hera was utterly shocked to see him again after so long.{{Ahsoka|Part Eight: The Jedi, the Witch, and the Warlord}} ===Legacy=== {{Quote|The Hera Syndulla? If only they had known where she'd end up.|Leia Organa|}} [[File:Spectres_painting.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Spectres depicted by Sabine's mural]] Sometime after the Battle of Endor, Sabine Wren painted a mural depicting Hera and the other Spectres flanked by loth-wolves and loth-cats to honor their role in the Rebellion. When ''[[The Rebel Files]]'' were [[Excavation on Durkteel|recovered]] by the [[Resistance]] in [[34 ABY]],''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]'' establishes that ''[[The Rebel Files]]'' were [[Bombardment of Durkteel|buried]] on [[Durkteel]] at the same [[time]] as the [[Battle of Endor]], which ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates to [[4 ABY]]. As the book also states that the files had not been seen for thirty [[Standard year|years]] prior to their recovery, the [[excavation on Durkteel]] and the case's journey from Durkteel to [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] must have taken place in [[34 ABY]]. Leia Organa, now a general in the Resistance, came across Ahsoka Tano's message to General [[Davits Draven]] following the Spectres' action at Mustafar. In the message, Tano informed Draven that Syndulla had received an Alliance officer's commission in the aftermath of the mission. Organa left a note asking if it referred to the Hera Syndulla, before she added if only Tano and Draven had known as the time where Syndulla would end up, a general in the New Republic. ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|There's enough darkness in the galaxy right now. Let me know if you want to spread a little light.|Hera Syndulla|[[Star Wars: Outer Rim|''Star Wars'': Outer Rim]]}} [[File:HeraSyndulla1-Fathead.png|thumb|left|344x344px|Hera Syndulla and her blaster.]] Hera's personality was somewhat two-sided; while she exuded a no-nonsense style of command, she was also known for being a very warm and compassionate individual. As a highly capable pilot and captain, Hera took good care of her ship, as well as her crew. Upon meeting Ezra, Hera developed a sort of motherly bond with the boy as she had with the other crew members. She was a true believer in the rebel cause and inspired hope in the rest of the crew. She was also the only other crew member aware of Kanan's test after Ezra stole the latter's [[holocron]]. Hera was also in love with Kanan,{{WebCite|url=http://www.comingsoon.net/tv/features/620441-star-wars-rebels-cast-and-crew-talk-season-2-and-clone-wars-connections|text=Star Wars Rebels Cast and Crew Talk Season 2 and Clone Wars Connections|author=Busch, Jenna|date=2015-10-07|quote=Though Hera loves him very much, she knows she can't allow that part of him to step in front of that Galactic obligation she has to people everywhere.|archivedate=20170711093531}} she usually confided in him and frequently called him "love." She was more than capable of putting her foot down when she saw conflict within the crew, such as sending Ezra and Zeb out on an errand together when the two had been fighting. While an adept fighter, Hera also cared for her crew and knew how to motivate them to reach a common goal. A smart, tactful, and highly observant individual, Hera could quickly detect a threat. As Lando Calrissian successfully played her crew members off one another to his own ends, Hera caught on to his trickery and put the con-man in his place. Her skills of deduction proved invaluable when her suspicions of Gall Trayvis allowed her to expose the man as an Imperial agent. She also remembered when the Jedi and clones fought in the Clone Wars, at one point being saved from death by them, and encouraged Kanan to trust Captain Rex and put aside his past animosity towards clones. As with other Twi'lek females, many considered her attractive, particularly Kanan but also less savory characters as well, including Okadiah Garson, Azmorigan, and Lando Calrissian. She knew how to use her natural charm and beauty to her advantage when necessary, as seen when she manipulated the gangster Azmorigan in order to escape his ship. Due to her negative experiences with the criminals Azmorigan and Hondo, Hera was reluctant to work with them until Hondo convinced her that doing so would benefit the rebellion's interests. She despised their company to the extent that she ordered them to leave the ship once both parties had achieved their objectives. Despite her love for Kanan, Hera was deeply committed to the rebel cause. Her pragmatism led her to accede to Ahsoka Tano's advice that they not rescue him in order to avoid exposing the rebellion to the Empire, and was a key organizer of the early Alliance, whose original goal was to seek a diplomatic solution.''[[Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy]]'' While Hera was angered that her crew had disobeyed her orders by embarking on a search for Kanan, she was mollified when Ezra revealed that he had a plan. She also viewed the rebel struggle as a larger galactic-wide struggle that went beyond the planet Lothal. Her concern for the galaxy put her at odds with her father, who was solely focused on achieving Ryloth's freedom. Despite their differences, she managed to convince her father and his rebel cell to help her crew to steal an Imperial fighter-carrier. [[File:HeraSyndullaWantedPoster-SWCT.png|thumb|right|220px|Hera's Imperial wanted poster]] Hera also had a love for flying which resonated well with her leadership aspirations in the rebellion. Due to her role in obtaining a prototype [[A/SF-01 B-wing starfighter|B-wing starfighter]], Hera was promoted to Phoenix Leader. While Hera regarded the space-faring purrgil as a pest for endangering interstellar travel, she came to respect them after the purrgil helped the Spectres to raid a Mining Guild refueling station. Something visibly seen by the fact that she wore her flight jacket during her days as a general, Syndulla would never forget her roots as a pilot.{{InsiderCite|223|Launchpad}} Hera also had a relationship with the astromech droid Chopper which dated back to the Clone Wars. She adopted the droid after rescuing him from a downed Y-wing fighter. Hera cared for Chopper and looked after the outdated astromech droid. She understood [[binary]] and regarded Chopper as an indispensable member of her crew. While Hera was angry with Chopper for allowing himself to be distracted during a raid on a fuel depot, she was mollified after Chopper and his new-found friend AP-5 helped find the rebellion the site for a new base on the planet Atollon. Hera was also skilled at undercover work. She could also change her accent in order to conceal her identity. Hera also displayed considerable fortitude and defiance when being interrogated by Grand Admiral Thrawn. Her courage and willingness to infiltrate her former home to recover a family heirloom the Kalikori gained Thrawn's respect. Despite losing the Kalikori to Thrawn, Hera came to realize that her crew and her father were her family and more important than old heirlooms. Hera was willing to let go of the past if it meant furthering the rebel cause. Cognizant of the Empire's military capabilities, Hera tried unsuccessfully to convince Mart Mattin and his Iron Squadron to accompany them back to the rebel fleet. Later, Hera led a successful mission to rescue Mart from the Empire. Despite the disillusioned Imperial Agent Kallus' help in obtaining plans for Thrawn's TIE Defender initiative, Hera still distrusted the Imperial. She cautioned her comrades to be careful with him until they could verify his trustworthiness. Hera also cared for her rebel crew and held a maternal role in the group, becoming its "Space Mom." She was both tough and loving towards her fellow rebels, with Wren and Bridger both coming to her for advice, encouragement, and training.{{InsiderCite|221|Space Moms}} Jarrus and Syndulla raised Bridger from a young troublemaker into the man he became.{{SW|url=news/ahsoka-part-8-the-jedi-the-witch-and-the-warlord-highlights|text=''Ahsoka'' Analyzed: 7 Highlights from "Part Eight: The Jedi, the Witch, and the Warlord"}} She displayed maternal instincts when Ezra was tormented by Maul's visions. Hera wanted to abort her recon mission to Lothal but Kanan managed to convince her to proceed with the mission. Due to her close rapport with Sabine, Hera was privy to Sabine's doubts, fears, and troubled relationship with her family. Knowing that Sabine was a fearsome warrior and strong leader, Hera counseled Kanan not to hold back her training but to let her fully embrace the Darksaber's power. As a rebel leader, Hera was aware of Saw Gerrera's harsh methods; which caused her not to trust him fully. Still, she regarded him as being better than the Empire. Hera typically spoke in a colloquial [[The galaxy|Galactic]] accent but occasionally reverted to her native Rylothian accent. Hera was a brave and creative pilot who was willing to undertake difficult challenges including smuggling the rebel leader Mon Mothma through the dangerous Archeon pass. Hera also had a deep respect for Mon Mothma and the two women became friends. Hera respected Mothma for her outspoken criticism of the Empire and her long-term strategic vision for the rebellion. Mothma in return complimented Hera for her willingness to take dangerous risks and courageous leadership. [[File:Herra_and_C1-10P_Ally_Pack_art.png|thumb|left|250px|Hera shared a strong bond with Chopper.]] Hera had a strong bond with Chopper and sought revenge on the Imperial intelligence officers who had reprogrammed her droid into a double agent. This led her to destroy an entire IGV-55 surveillance vessel with all hands aboard. Hera was distraught when she thought that she had lost Chopper and expressed elation when he rebooted. Hera was a courageous and skilled military commander who cared for the well-being of the rebellion and had a good working relationship with her fellow commanders Sato and Dodonna. She was not intimidated by Grand Admiral Thrawn and refused to surrender. Hera loved Kanan and pleaded with him to come back safely after his unsuccessful mission to solicit Bendu's help against the Empire. At times, Hera's devotion to the rebellion led her to regard the Spectres as important assets of the Rebel Alliance. She regarded Kanan as her partner and companion. Hera distrusted Saw Gerrera for his aggressive and violent methods and expressed concern when Saw enlisted Ezra, Sabine, and Chopper on one of his operations. Like Ezra, Hera believed the Spectres had a special connection with Lothal and was willing to accept a dangerous mission there. Hera's romantic feelings for Kanan led them to share a passionate embrace while on an undercover mission on Lothal. As a passionate rebel leader, Hera successfully lobbied for the Rebel Alliance to take out the TIE/D Defender factories on Lothal and to aid the people of Lothal, who were suffering under Imperial oppression. Hera's fearlessness and devotion to the rebel cause led her to lead a strike attempt on Lothal's Imperial factories. Hera also cared for her subordinates and was willing to risk capture in order to ensure that her underlings Chopper and Mart Mattin escaped Imperial forces. Hera's iron resolve and fighting spirit enabled her to hold out against both Governor Pryce and Grand Admiral Thrawn during interrogation. After Kanan rescued her, Hera confided her feelings for Kanan. Hera was devastated by the death of her partner Kanan and initially blamed herself. However, Chopper helped her to realize the significance of Kanan's sacrifice. To honor his memory, she attached a piece of his Jedi holocron to her family heirloom, the Kalikori. Kanan's death led Hera to be more careful about the lives of her rebel cell members. Though Hera was frightened that the Emperor had taken an interest in the Lothal Jedi Temple, Zeb convinced her to persevere with the mission. Despite Kanan's death, Hera could still sense his comforting presence. Hera also used her persuasive communications skills to recruit several old friends of Ezra including Gregor, Wolffe, Hondo, Melch, and Ketsu Onyo into helping Ezra to liberate his homeworld of Lothal. Despite her initial misgivings about Hondo, she decided to trust his plan to latch onto an Imperial cargo ship in order to get the ''Ghost'' through the Imperial blockade above Lothal. As a result, Hera came to trust Hondo. After Ezra helped trap Governor Pryce, Hera praised Ezra for his victory. Respecting her as a leader and mother figure, Ezra recognized her and the other rebels' contributions to their victory. During the Liberation of Lothal, Hera showed leadership and resolve. She endorsed Sabine's plan to send rebel teams to reactivate the shield generators. Hera also respected Ezra's decision to leave and confront Grand Admiral Thrawn alone. Out of respect for Hera's leadership and motherly role, Ezra left a meiloorun fruit for her before departing into uncharted space with Thrawn. ==Skills and abilities== {{Quote|That was one of your better crashes.''"
"''Kanan Jarrus, you know I never crash. I have very—''"
"''Very exciting landings. Thanks for reminding me.|Kanan Jarrus and Hera Syndulla|}} [[File:Hera_Syndulla_EaW.png|thumb|right|250px|Hera's love of flying was evident in her skill as a pilot]] Besides being an able and effective leader, Hera was also an exceptionally skilled pilot. Hera first honed her skills as a rebel pilot during a relief mission to Ryloth following the failed assassination attempt on the Emperor and Lord Vader. She was able to fly various ships including the ''Ghost'', the ''Phantom'', a prototype B-wing starfighter, and a T-65B X-wing starfighter. Hera was also familiar with physical combat and once assaulted the gangster Azmorigan and one of his men. Later, she knocked out the Imperial agent Gall Trayvis in physical combat after tricking him into holding an unloaded blaster. As a seasoned rebel operative, Hera could tell when a blaster was unloaded. [[File:Hera_Syndulla-FA.png|thumb|left|200px|Captain Hera Syndulla]] While Hera was a capable fighter who could come up with ingenious escape plans, she was no match for the Force powers of the former Sith Lord Maul. Despite her strong will-power, Hera could not stop Maul from retrieving information on the location of Kanan Jarrus' holocron from her mind. As a seasoned rebel commander, Hera was familiar with various Imperial strategies and traps. Hera was also tech-savvy enough to close the ''Ghost''{{'s}} cargo hatch manually. She also used Chopper as a conduit to send reverse data feed to destroy an Imperial surveillance vessel. As a military commander, Hera knew how to study battle maps in order to devise strategies. Her skills as a pilot also allowed her to lead from the front in space battles. As a skilled pilot, Hera was able to evade Imperial fighters including TIE/D Defenders. She later used her engineering skills to help Sabine install a hyperdrive aboard Ryder Azadi's U-wing. On another occasion, she was able to escape Thrawn's forces by jumping into hyperspace while flying through an Imperial construction module. Hera later used her dogfighting skills to take out a TIE/D Defender Elite and an Imperial light cruiser. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|There are certain issues that I care very much about in my life, in terms of equality and representation and fighting for those who are marginalized, and speaking up for those who may have no voice. This character seemed to do that. There's also a part of me that loves to bring people together.|Vanessa Marshall on Hera Syndulla|{{SW|url=news/vanessa-marshall-interview-star-wars-the-bad-batch|text=Hera Flies Again: Vanessa Marshall on Returning as the High-Flying Pilot in ''Star Wars: The Bad Batch''}}}} Hera Syndulla was created for the animated series ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' where she was voiced by [[Vanessa Marshall]].{{SWYouTube|RzopG0SGJYI|Meet Hera, the Pilot | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/star-wars-rebels-meet-hera-the-pilot}} She was first revealed at the [[January]] [[2014]] [[Wikipedia:Nuremberg International Toy Fair|Nuremberg International Toy Fair]], where the character was included on the packaging of a [[LEGO Star Wars|LEGO ''Star Wars'']] ''Rebels'' set.{{WebCite|url=http://www.groovebricks.com/lego-star-wars-rebels-sets-at-the-nuremberg-germany-toy-fair|text=LEGO Star Wars Rebels Sets At The Nuremberg Germany Toy Fair -- Groove Bricks|author=Tomás|date=2014-01-28|work=[http://www.groovebricks.com Groove Bricks]|archivedate=20181007012014}} A video properly introducing the character was released on [[February 20]], 2014. Prior to the series' debut episode "[[Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion|Spark of Rebellion]]" on [[September 26]], [[2014]],{{SW|url=news/star-wars-rebels-spark-of-rebellion-to-debut-early-on-watch-disney-xd|text=Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion to Debut Early on WATCH Disney XD}} she appeared in the prequel novel ''[[A New Dawn (novel)|A New Dawn]]'' by [[John Jackson Miller]]{{SW|url=news/sdcc-2014-star-wars-a-new-dawn-panel-liveblog|text=SDCC 2014: ''Star Wars: A New Dawn'' Panel – Liveblog}} and other media.''[[Chopper Saves the Day]]''''[[Rise of the Rebels]]'' ===Design=== The character was envisioned as the skilled pilot and a norturing heart of the team and like their mother. The design phase for ''Rebels'' began in early [[2013]]. According to [[Kilian Plunkett]], she was envisioned "from the beginning" as a Twi'lek wearing a flight suit. Various differnt designs of female Twi'lek, all adult with either green or blue skin,''[[The Art of Star Wars Rebels]]''{{SW|url=news/wondercon-2014-star-wars-rebels-panel-report|text=WonderCon 2014: ''Star Wars Rebels'' Panel Report}} were designed by [[Chris Glenn]] and [[Amy Beth Christenson]] and one design of a blue skinned younger Twi'lek girl was also designed. All of the designs featured her wearing flight goggles, which series creator [[Dave Filoni]] compared to those used during [[Wikipedia:World War II|World War II]].{{SW|url=news/star-wars-rebels-costuming-101-hera-syndulla|text=''Star Wars Rebels'' Costuming 101: Hera Syndulla}} Her final model was designed by Kilian Plunkett and finished on [[April 11]], [[2013]]. It used bright warm colors and the markings on her lekku head tails were meant to set her apart from other Twi'lek characters. A series of facial studies for her final design was also drawn by Plunkett and a maquette of her final head was created by [[Darren Marshall]].{{WebCite|url=https://dmarshallart.com/star-wars-rebels-season-1|text=Star Wars Rebels - Season 1|work=[[Darren Marshall]]'s website|archivedate=20251211062553}} According to the [[StarWars.com]] blogger [[James Burns]], Hera Syndulla was named after the ancient Greek goddess [[Wikipedia: Hera|Hera]], whose name means "protector." Hera was the wife and the sister of the Greek god [[Wikipedia:Zeus|Zeus]] and was the goddess of women, childbirth, and marriage. [[Simon Kinberg]] and [[Dave Filoni]] also confirmed that Hera and several other characters in the television series were named after historical and Biblical characters in order to give their names a sense of purpose and meaning that would reflect their characters.{{SW|url=news/star-wars-rebels-whats-in-a-name|text=''Star Wars Rebels'': What's in a Name?|nolive=1}} Hera shares a surname with Cham Syndulla, a Twi'lek character from the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series. Cham Syndulla was revealed to be her father on [[February 23]], [[2015]].{{RebelsRecon|AATSzoxTC1g|#1.13: Inside "Rebel Resolve" | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/rebels-recon-inside-rebel-resolve}} ===Concept art gallery=== {{Gallery |source=''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' |storyboards= |concept= File:HeraBlue-ConceptArt.png|Early concept art of Hera Syndulla File:Hera-ConceptArt-ABC2.png|Concept art of Hera Syndulla by Amy Beth Christenson File:Hera-ConceptArt-ChrisGlenn.png|Concept art of Hera Syndulla by Chris Glenn File:Hera-ConceptArt-ABC.png|Concept art of Hera Syndulla by Amy Beth Christenson File:RebelsCrew-EarlierConceptArt-ArtofRebels.png|Concept art of the ''Ghost'' crew including of Hera Syndulla by Amy Beth Christenson File:Hera-FacialStudies-KilianPlunkett.png|Facial studies of Hera Syndulla by Kilian Plunkett |digital= |in-progress= }} ===Portrayal=== {{Quote|Initally, I auditioned for a secret project entitled 'Wolf.' I earned a call back where I met Dave Filoni for the first time, and then my life changed when I got the news that I was going to play Hera! She was described as a 'nurturing yet fierce leader,' who assembles a chosen family to fight for the cause.|Vanessa Marshall|{{InsiderCite|219|Day Wanna Wanga - The Tale of the Twi'leks}}}} [[File:VanessaMarshall.jpg|thumb|right|175px|Vanessa Marshall, Hera's voice actress]] Vanessa Marshall was originally called in for a voiceover audition for a project just called "Wolf". Based on the script's content she already suspected that it could be ''[[Star Wars]]'', but was only confirmed when she got a call back and saw a picture of a Twi'lek on the wall. She originally imagined that Hera would look more like actor [[Sigourney Weaver]], but was "thrilled" that she was a Twi'lek, especially because she wanted to fight the perception that the species were all mostly slave [[dancer]]s.{{InsiderCite|151|Hera: A New Breed of Hero|reprint=1}} The voice cast recorded their scripts as a group before the animation phase and had only seen mockups of their characters' designs. Videos of their recording sessions were used to inform the character's facial expressions and Sabine Wren's voice actor [[Tiya Sircar]] thought that Syndulla looked "an awful lot" like Marshall.{{InsiderCite|152|Mandalorian Graffiti: Tiya Sircar is Sabine Wren|reprint=1}} Hera did not speak with a Twi'lek ([[Wikipedia:French language|French]]) accent until the [[Star Wars Rebels Season Two|Season Two]] episode "[[Homecoming]]," in the scene where she argues with her father. When she auditioned for the role, Vanessa Marshall read Hera's dialogue with her own accent, before being asked if she could do it in a French accent. Marshall, who is fluent in French, responded she would, but the topic did not come up again, presumably as it was decided it would be hard for viewers to understand. Eventually, Dave Filoni emailed her asking if she ever thought Hera would use a Twi'lek accent if she returned to her homeworld: Marshall replied "Only if she was angry." She later likened it to "someone from [[Wikipedia:Tennessee|Tennessee]] or [[Wikipedia:Texas|Texas]], or something like that, when they get into an argument with their father, all of a sudden, they're a [[Wikipedia:Southern belle|Southern belle]]. It demonstrates a kind of vulnerability that goes straight to the core of who she is. Even in that moment, she can't undo that accent. But I think that's how much she loves him and yearns to connect with him, that she even lets that guard down to speak in their shared accent."{{WebCite|url=http://www.hypable.com/star-wars-rebels-2x16-vanessa-marshall-clip|text=''Star Wars Rebels'' 2×16: Vanessa Marshall previews Hera's "Homecoming" – plus exclusive clip!|author=Schick, Michal|date=2016-02-17|work=Hypable|archivedate=20170528184640}} ===Further appearances=== {{Quote|We had a blast dialing in the exact right amount of youth and accent for little Hera. It was a dream come true to finally explore her relationship with her mother. I also loved planting the seeds for her dreams and goals for her future.|Marshall on returning for ''The Bad Batch''|}} General Syndulla is name-dropped as an [[Easter egg (virtual)|easter egg]] in the [[2016]] live-action film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'', which Dave Filoni clarified was meant to be Hera (as opposed to her father), a reference to a forthcoming storyline.{{WebCite|url=http://ew.com/movies/rogue-one-rebels-references/rogue-one-and-rebels-6|text=See the 'Star Wars: Rebels' References in 'Rogue One'|author=Breznican, Anthony|date=2016-12-20|work=Entertainment Weekly|archivedate=20161222184651}} Marshall returned to portray the character in the [[2020]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Squadrons]]'', developed by [[Motive Studios]], where she also provided [[Wikipedia:Motion capture|motion capture]] work for the character.{{Twitter|vanmarshall|status/1312156766176571393|[[Vanessa Marshall]]|date=2020-10-03|quote=Grateful to confirm that I am voicing Hera in #StarWarsSquadrons! My first motion capture gig!}} A teenaged Hera Syndulla later appeared in the [[The Bad Batch Season 1|first season]] of the animated series ''[[Star Wars: The Bad Batch]]'' in [[2021]], where she was again voiced by Marshall. Hera's model for the series was designed by [[Chris Madden]] and finished on [[February 11]], [[2020]].{{SW|url=series/the-bad-batch/devils-deal-episode-guide|text="Devil's Deal" Episode Guide | The Bad Batch}} Marshall was first approached by the series' producers over email and asked if she wanted to return, but was only later further informed about the series. She then recorded her lines in either late 2020 or early 2021.{{WebCite|url=https://www.cnet.com/culture/entertainment/hera-syndulla-voice-in-star-wars-the-bad-batch-was-inspired-by-marvel|text=Hera Syndulla's voice in Star Wars: The Bad Batch was inspired by Marvel|author=Sean Keane|date=2021-07-15|work=''[[Wikipedia:CNET|CNET]]''|archivedate=20220527011044}} Marshall said that she highly enjoyed figuring out the "right amount" of youthfulness and French accent for Hera's voice and that it was "a dream come true" to explore Hera's relationship with her mother and that she loved to establish the basis for Hera's future dreams and goals. Marshall was also inspired by her earlier role as the [[Marvel Comics]]' character [[Wikipedia:Mary Jane Watson|Mary Jane Watson]] in the animated series ''[[Wikipedia:The Spectacular Spider-Man (TV series)|The Spectacular Spider-Man]]''. ===''Ahsoka''=== [[File:MaryElizabethWinstead.png|thumb|left|190px|Mary Elizabeth Winstead portrays Hera in the ''Ahsoka'' television series.]] [[Mary Elizabeth Winstead]] portrays Hera Syndulla in the [[2023]] television series ''[[Star Wars: Ahsoka]]''.{{SW|url=news/swce-2023-ahsoka-panel|text=SWCE 2023: 10 Things We Learned from the ''Ahsoka'' Panel}} The casting of Winstead was first reported in December 2022 and was formally confirmed at [[Celebration|''Star Wars'' Celebration]] in April 2023.{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/ahsoka-series-hera-syndulla-mary-elizabeth-winstead-cast|text=Mary Elizabeth Winstead Reportedly Cast as Hera Syndulla in 'Ahsoka' Series|author=Arezou Amin|date=2023-12-23|work=''[[Wikipedia:Collider (website)|Collider]]''|archivedate=20221224224936}} Concept art of Winstead as Syndulla was created by [[Brian Matyas]] in [[2021]][[Ahsoka 2|''Ahsoka'' 2]] Ahead of [[Ahsoka Season 2|''Ahsoka'' Season 2]], Winstead stated that she recieved more play within the season and remarked that was very fun.{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/ahsoka-season-2-update-mary-elizabeth-winstead|text=‘Ahsoka’ Star Drops Action-Packed Season 2 Update on the Hit Star Wars Series [Exclusive]|author=McPherson, Chris|date=2025-10-17|work=Collider|archivedate=20251019172915}} ===Non-canon history=== {{Quote|No, General Syndulla.|[[Rowan Freemaker/LEGO|Rowan Freemaker]] expresses surprise as he spots Hera Syndulla|{{FreemakerAdventures|Trouble on Tibalt}}}} [[File:Alliance_leadership_Freemakers.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Hera and members of the Rebel Alliance in ''LEGO Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures Season Two'']] Hera Syndulla appears in ''[[Angry Birds Star Wars II]]''. At one point, she and Sabine Wren rescued the street orphan Ezra Bridger from stormtroopers. They escaped from Agent Kallus, and Hera let Ezra join her crew aboard the ''Ghost''.''[[Angry Birds Star Wars II]]'' In the [[LEGO Star Wars Movie Short|''LEGO Star Wars Rebels Movie Shorts'']], Hera, Kanan, and Zeb were drinking in the [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina|Mos Eisley Cantina]] when Ezra called for a rescue from a Star Destroyer. The three left aboard the ''Ghost'' and managed to rescue him. Ezra then suggested they charge the Star Destroyer's bridge and hide behind it, and eventually the warship jumped to hyperspace.{{LegoMiniMovie|RUZ2y3uRaW8|Saving The Phantom}} At another time, the ''Ghost'' was damaged by a Star Destroyer, forcing it to go to a space station for repairs. The rest of the crew was separated, and Hera went to a space station to make repairs. She avoided Imperials while she and Chopper collected parts. The rest of the crew arrived in time to finish repairs to their starship.{{LegoMiniMovie|w53MYjyUPWI|Ghost Story}} Hera Syndulla also appeared in the [[LEGO Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures Season Two|second season]] of ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures]]'', which debuted in the Summer of 2017.{{SW|url=news/lego-star-wars-the-freemaker-adventures-season-2-coming-this-summer|text=''LEGO Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures'' Season 2 Coming This Summer}} Vanessa Marshall reprised her role as Hera.{{WebCite|url=http://deadline.com/2017/04/lego-star-wars-the-freemaker-adventures-renewed-season-2-disney-xd-1202059900|text='Lego Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures' Renewed For Season 2 By Disney XD|author=Petski, Denise|date=2014-04-03|archivedate=20170713160657}} She made a cameo appearance as a General in the Alliance Fleet in the episode "[[Trouble on Tibalt]]," which was released on [[June 17]], [[2017]], and more throughout the season, including her being at the Battle of Endor and the subsequent celebration in Bright Tree Village.{{FreemakerAdventures|Return of the That you will face your demons and save the universe.|Qui-Gon Jinn and Anakin Skywalker|audio=QuiGonAnakinMortis.flac|{{TCW|Ghosts of Mortis}}}} '''Anakin Skywalker''' was a legendary [[Force-sensitive]] [[human]] [[Gender|male]] who was a [[Jedi Knight]] of the [[Galactic Republic]] and the prophesied [[Chosen One]] of the [[Jedi Order]], destined to bring balance to [[the Force]]. Also known as "'''Ani'''" during his childhood, Skywalker earned the moniker "[[Hero With No Fear]]" from his accomplishments in the [[Clone Wars]]. His alter ego, '''Darth Vader''', the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]], was created when Skywalker turned to the [[dark side of the Force]], pledging his allegiance to the [[Sith Lord]] [[Darth Sidious]] at the end of the [[Republic Era]]. A [[vergence]] in the Force, Anakin Skywalker was [[Reproduction|born]] on the [[desert]] [[planet]] of [[Tatooine]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories]] in [[41 BBY]]. He was the son of [[Shmi Skywalker Lars|Shmi Skywalker]], a [[Slavery|slave]] who conceived a [[Youngling|child]] without a [[Parent|father]]. His [[blood]] contained over twenty-thousand [[midi-chlorian]]s, surpassing [[Grand Master]] [[Yoda]] and all other [[Jedi]] in [[the galaxy]]. [[Qui-Gon Jinn]], the [[Jedi Master]] who discovered Skywalker on Tatooine in [[32 BBY]], theorized that Skywalker was conceived by the midi-chlorians. Following the [[Battle of Naboo]], the [[Jedi High Council]] admitted Anakin Skywalker into the Order as the [[Padawan]] of Jedi Knight [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] despite feeling that he was too old and emotional to adhere to the [[Jedi Code]]. Skywalker remained a Padawan through the beginning of the Clone Wars, instigated by events set in motion by [[Count]] [[Dooku]]. Although Jedi [[Religion|doctrine]] prohibited romantic relationships, Anakin Skywalker had a secret [[Marriage|wife]], [[Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]] of [[Naboo]]. During the early [[Standard day|days]] of the Clone Wars, Skywalker served as a [[Jedi General]] in the [[Grand Army of the Republic]], commanding the [[clone trooper]]s of the elite [[501st Legion]] against the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. After receiving his knighthood, Skywalker oversaw the [[Jedi training]] of his own apprentice, [[Ahsoka Tano]]. By [[19 BBY]], when Tano walked away from the Jedi Order, Skywalker began to struggle with feelings of failure towards his apprentice and the Order itself. Following the [[death]] of Count Dooku during the [[Battle of Coruscant]], Anakin Skywalker's faith in the Jedi was further shaken when he was put on the Jedi Council without the rank of master. He also learned that [[Supreme Chancellor]] Sheev Palpatine was [[Darth]] Sidious, the elusive Dark [[Lord]] of the [[Sith]] who orchestrated the war in order to take over the [[galaxy]]. Manipulated into believing that the Jedi had failed him and coupled with his fear of losing Amidala in childbirth, Skywalker betrayed and turned against the Jedi Order, believing Sidious had the knowledge to [[Immortality|cheat]] death. Consumed by the persona of Darth Vader, the fallen Jedi Knight marched his [[legion]] on the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] of [[Coruscant]] where they executed its inhabitants, including [[Jedi Initiate|Jedi younglings]], as part of [[Order 66]] and the [[Great Jedi Purge]]. Vader was then sent to [[Mustafar]] to [[Mission to Mustafar|exterminate]] the [[Executive Separatist Council|Separatist Council]] at the behest of his [[Sith Master]], who became the [[Proclamation of the New Order|self-proclaimed]] [[Galactic Emperor]]. Vader subsequently sustained severe injuries in his [[Duel on Mustafar|duel]] with Kenobi, and was [[Cybernetics|rebuilt]] as an [[Darth Vader's armor|armored]] [[cyborg]] while his wife died of a broken [[heart]], though not before giving birth to the [[twin]]s [[Luke Skywalker]] and [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] who were hidden from their father and the [[Emperor]] as the [[Galactic Empire]] rose to power. Being the [[Emperor's Fist]] and later being elevated to the position of [[supreme commander of the Imperial fleet]], Vader enforced the rule of the [[New Order]] as the Emperor's [[Sith apprentice]] throughout most of the [[Imperial Era]] and was thus seen as ''de facto'' [[Commander-in-Chief]] of the entire [[Imperial Military]]. In the aftermath of killing Kenobi in a [[Rescue of Princess Leia|duel aboard the Death Star]] and the subsequent [[Battle of Yavin]], he discovered the existence of his son and was determined to turn Luke to the dark side. Luke sought to become a Jedi, like his father before him, and believed that Vader had the potential to turn back to the [[light side of the Force]]. Vader was defeated by Luke during the [[Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY]], but the young Jedi refused to strike down his father in anger, causing the Emperor to [[torture]] Luke with [[Force lightning]]. The pain inflicted on his son awakened the part of Vader that was still Anakin, resulting in a redeemed Skywalker killing Sidious at the cost of his own life. Having destroyed the Sith and fulfilled his [[destiny]] as the Chosen One, Skywalker made peace with his son and became [[Force spirit|one with the Force]]. Anakin Skywalker was one of the most powerful Jedi and Sith in [[Timeline of galactic history|galactic history]]. The Force was especially strong in the [[Skywalker family|Skywalker bloodline]], which culminated in Anakin's grandson, [[Ben Solo]], Organa's son who was born by the [[Galactic Concordance|end]] of the [[Galactic Civil War]] in [[5 ABY]]. Solo would turn to the dark side as well, becoming the [[Knights of Ren|dark warrior]] Kylo Ren during the [[New Republic Era|rise]] of the [[First Order]]. Like his grandfather, however, Solo found redemption by sacrificing his life for the love of another—the Jedi apprentice [[Rey Skywalker|Rey]], who heard Skywalker's voice telling her to restore the balance, as he once had, during the [[Battle of Exegol]] in [[35 ABY]]. Solo's death ended the Skywalker bloodline, although Rey, the [[Palpatine family|granddaughter]] of Sidious, rejected her true heritage and took their surname to honor their legacy. ==Biography== ===Early life=== ====Childhood on Tatooine==== {{Quote|Had he been born in the Republic, we would have identified him early. The Force is unusually strong with him, that much is clear. Who was his father?''"
"''There was no father. I carried him, I gave birth, I raised him, I can't explain what happened.|Qui-Gon Jinn and Shmi Skywalker|audio=ThereWasNoFather.flac|}} [[File:Baby_Ani.png|thumb|left|210px|Shmi Skywalker and her baby, Anakin Skywalker]] Believed to have been conceived by the [[midi-chlorian]]s,{{Databank|anakin-skywalker-biography-gallery|Anakin Skywalker Biography Gallery}} Anakin Skywalker was [[Reproduction|born]] to the [[Slavery|slave]] [[Shmi Skywalker Lars|Shmi Skywalker]]. Although Skywalker was listed as being born on the [[desert]] [[planet]] of [[Tatooine]] in some sources, confusion existed as to where Skywalker was actually born; whereas some records reported his birthplace as Tatooine, others claimed he moved to the planet with his mother at a very young age. Regardless, Tatooine was Skywalker's homeworld. While living on Tatooine, Skywalker and his [[Parent|mother]] were originally owned by [[Gardulla Besadii the Elder|Gardulla]] the [[Hutt]] until she lost them to the [[Toydarian]] [[Watto]] in a [[podracing]] bet when Skywalker was around age 3. Affectionately nicknamed "Ani," he worked in [[Watto's junkshop|his master's shop]], located in [[Mos Espa]]. Even at a young age, Skywalker exhibited exceptional [[pilot]]ing skills, and built the [[protocol droid]] [[C-3PO]], specially modified to withstand Tatooine's sand and heat''[[Return of the Jedi: Beware the Power of the Dark Side!]]'' for his mother. Once, while he was working in Watto's scrapyard, he found a broken [[servomotor]] which he thought he could repair and use on the droid that he was building and asked his master for it. With a glance, Watto saw that it was worthless and grunted that he could, but as Skywalker walked away, Watto told him nothing was free and had him work harder the next day. On one occasion, Skywalker and his mother were lost in a sandstorm, but the boy refused to listen to her when she demanded he return home if he could see it. Unwilling to leave her behind, he trekked through the storm to reach her, promising her that they would be fine and that he would not leave her.[[Darth Vader (2020) 26|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 26]] [[File:AnakinGetsThreepioPhotoreceptors-Ashcan.png|thumb|right|200px|Skywalker used salvaged parts to rebuild a protocol droid for household duties and to help his mother.]] Skywalker got the [[photoreceptor]]s for the droid at a [[Mos Espa Market|market]] in Mos Espa. Though a [[Gran]] wanted them too and chased him through the market, Skywalker escaped by destroying an [[Ithorian]]'s stall and blocking the Gran's pursuit.[[Star Wars Adventures Ashcan|''Star Wars Adventures'' Ashcan]] Before he had even turned nine, Skywalker's work had ensured 3PO was operational.{{EncyclopediaCite|Anakin Skywalker}} He was close friends with fellow slaves [[Kitster Banai]] and [[Wald]], as well as the elderly [[Jira]]. He also built [[Anakin Skywalker's Podracer|his own podracer]], which would eventually help him win a podracing contest. Over the course of his life on Tatooine, Skywalker never saw it rain.{{StoryCite|story=There Is Always Another|book=From a Certain Point of View: The Empire Strikes Back}} At some point, Watto told Anakin to go and throw away some scrap. When looking at it, Anakin found an ultra power cell, just what he needed for his pod. Suddenly, a swoop gang with a [[Devaronian]] member attacked the streets and shot the generator for the medical center. When Anakin examined it to see if he could repair the generator he saw that it needed a power cell. So, he took his power cell and saved the medical center. A week later, Anakin participated in a pod race with [[Sebulba]] who made him lose by cheating. Anakin stated that if he would have used the power cell on his own pod, he would have won but it was more important for the medical center to receive it.{{IDWAdventuresCite-2017|issue=6|story=Tales from Wild Space: Podracer's Rescue}} On hard nights, Anakin's mother would tell him the story of the [[sun-dragon]]. Generations of Tatooine dwellers told of the sun-dragon myth with their own personal significance, but only Shmi's held the most feeling. The sun-dragon was a creature that lived inside the core of a [[star]]. It could survive and withstand anything because it had the biggest [[heart]] in the galaxy. It guarded everything it loved and treasured, through fire and flame. Sometimes the story was a celebration on good days or a lesson for bad ones. Anakin normally heard it on days where Watto was exceptionally cruel. Her intent was always clear, however. To Shmi, Anakin ''was'' the sun-dragon. He had the strongest heart in the galaxy and it would always guide him to do what he needed, so long as he trust in it. It was a story Anakin kept extremely close to his heart and shared with very few other people. ====Helping a Tusken slave==== [[File:JediAnakinDream-TPM25th.png|thumb|left|250px|Skywalker dreamed of becoming a Jedi from a very young age.]] One day, Anakin dreamed he was a [[Jedi]], saving his mother from slavery. He was awoken from his dream by his mother, who told him that there were no Jedi in the Outer Rim. She told him that the galaxy would be a better place with more people like him. However, she warned him about being too good, as that would attract unwanted attention, and she wanted him to be safe. Then an [[Otoga-222 maintenance droid]] came in and warned them both of the work Watto wanted them to do while he was gone. The Toydarian needed young Skywalker to go to [[Mos Eisley]] [[spaceport]] to pick up a shipment. [[Unidentified Otoga-222 maintenance droid|The droid]] reminded them of the [[transmitter chip]] inside their bodies that would blow up if they tried to run.[[The Phantom Menace 25th Anniversary Special 1|''The Phantom Menace'' 25th Anniversary Special 1]] Skywalker went to the spaceport, but could only pay the person delivering the shipment on credit. Just then a [[landspeeder]] with a trio of [[Enslaver|slavers]] arrived with their new [[Unidentified Tusken Raider (Anakin Skywalker)|Tusken slave]]. Skywalker overheard [[Unidentified Kajain'sa'Nikto (Mos Eisley)|one of the slavers]] mention that he hadn't put a transmitter chip in the slave yet, so he messed with the wiring of the speeder causing the speeder to fly away on its own. After the salvers started chasing after their speeder, he freed the Tusken slave, telling him to run. When the [[Kajain'sa'Nikto|Nikto]] slaver asked Skywalker where the slave went, he pointed them in the wrong direction. Skywalker walked home that day, happy that he was able to save someone.
