An obsession with the glory gathered in war, he valued bravery in combat above all else throughout his life and began gathering [[weapon]]s as trophies. Sheelal became an honorable, proud,{{TCW|Lair of Grievous}} and revered warrior''[[Star Wars: Alien Archive]]'' and one of the greatest military leaders, and the Kaleesh grew to regard him as a legendary figure. At that [[time]], Sheelal also began to develop a deep hatred for the [[Galactic Republic]]. He soon came to the realization that the [[Jedi Knight]]s of the [[Jedi Order]], the protectors of the Republic,{{Film|II}} were nearly undefeatable in [[Unarmed combat|hand-to-hand combat]] through their possession of [[Force power|supernatural abilities]] originating from a mystical energy field known as [[the Force]],{{Film|IV}} and he despised them for their skill. Sheelal had demonstrated his abilities and earned a bloody reputation as a warlord on his homeworld, with many adversaries, and eventually adopted the moniker "Grievous," whose name alone brought fear to his enemies. Over his years of battle, Grievous traveled and battled alongside Kalee's best warriors, the [[Izvoshra]]. He would assemble them into his elite{{ShipsandVehiclesCite|55|History of the Ship}} [[bodyguard]]s, with each a [[khan]] in command of troops of their own. Seemingly always alongside their warlord leader, the courageous Izvoshra shared in his victories and love of battle alike. =====Beyond Kalee===== {{Quote|I have toppled nations, I have slain kings, I have murdered legends!|Grievous on his several victories|audio=IHaveToppleNationsIHaveSlainKingsIHaveMurderLegends-BFII.flac|}} [[File:Pre-robo_grievous.png|thumb|right|295x295px|A statue of Grievous holding an enemy's severed head, a member of the Skrilling species.]] Accompanied by his Izvoshra, Grievous turned his attention to the [[star]]s to continue his conquests. Over the course of his exploits, Grievous came to topple nations, slay [[king]]s, and murder legends. At some point, he encountered a [[Wookiee warrior]]''[[Star Wars Battlefront II]]'' and decapitated a member of the [[Skrilling]] species. Grievous then went to war against the Yam'rii with increased vigor and determination while on the offensive. Fortunately for Grievous, his reputation had drawn the attention of the [[Sith]]—[[Dooku|Darth Tyranus]], also known as [[Count]] Dooku, who discovered Grievous{{Topps|set=2015 Topps Star Wars Chrome Perspectives|subset=Sith Information Guide|cardname=General Grievous|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/114595/cid/8022691/2015-Topps-Chrome-Star-Wars-Perspectives-Jedi-vs.-Sith-37-S-General-Grievous}} for the Sith, and his [[Sith Master]], [[Darth Sidious]], secretly the Republic [[Politics|politician]] Sheev Palpatine—both of them saw his potential as he led his people in a brutal campaign against the Yam'rii. Legend claimed that they specifically were interested in his strength, power, and will to succeed.{{StoryCite|story=The Droid with a Heart|book=Myths & Fables}} The Sith had been recruiting minions who possessed unique skills and a deep hatred of the Jedi, both of which Grievous had in abundance. As per the plan for the [[Cloning|Clone]] Wars, the Sith needed to recruit someone to lead a droid [[army]].''[[The Star Wars Book]]'' In particular, Grievous's hatred for the Jedi pushed him to near-madness and made him easily exploitable. In time, the Kaleesh forces successfully drove the Yam'rii from their world. Grievous launched a series of devastating campaigns on Huk itself, sweeping across the Huk worlds, where he relied on the help of his bodyguards. However, the Yam'rii took an unexpected turn and sought assistance from the Republic. The Galactic Republic and the Jedi Order intervened, siding with the Yam'rii against the invaders. The Kaleesh faced punishment; embargos and penalties were enforced, resulting in hundreds of thousands of deaths from starvation. At the time, Grievous's hatred only deepened, and he developed a personal vendetta against the Republic and the Jedi for their assistance to the Yam'rii. After their catastrophic intervention, he swore to exact terrible vengeance against the Republic and the Jedi for his people's suffering. Perhaps due to that animosity, Grievous decided to associate with the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan]] and joined its ranks as an [[Enforcer (occupation)|enforcer]]. However, when he demanded that his loyal Izvoshra remain by his side, the request was denied, and he was forbidden from continuing to utilize their services. Instead, Grievous was assigned leadership of the IGBC's [[droid]] army, which he despised. After requesting a more [[Sentience|intelligent]] personal guard and consulting with Count Dooku, [[Holowan Laboratories]]' [[engineer]]s were then authorized to construct a specific series of droids to fulfill Grievous's exacting standards. Thus, the [[IG-100 MagnaGuard|IG-100 series MagnaGuard]] [[Battle droid|combat droids]], or the prototype of autonomous combat with heuristic programming, were created. At the time of their creation, various fighting techniques were implanted in their memory, but Grievous insisted on having them erased of all knowledge{{HelmetCollectionCite|24|Helmets}} so that he could train them himself. He ordered and made certain that the MagnaGuards who served under him were outfitted with [[cloak]]s and half-hoods from his homeworld, in honor of his original faithful Izvoshra bodyguards, as well as an homage to the traditions worn on his homeworld. Grievous was tremendously successful, making him one of the IGBC's more vulnerable resources. By this time, not only Count Dooku but Darth Sidious himself had already taken notice of his exploits and had important intentions for him. =====Becoming a cyborg===== {{Quote|Sometimes I wonder why you submitted to the changes.''"
"''Improvements! I submit to no one! I chose them!|EV-A4-D and Grievous|audio=ISubmitToNoOne-LoG.flac|}} [[File:Sidious_Tyranus.png|thumb|left|295x295px|Count Dooku and his Sith Master, Darth Sidious.]] Grievous chose to become a [[cyborg]], receiving his enhancements over time, after the Sith gave him an unquestionable chance. They had been looking to test technologically advanced beings, and Grievous agreed to take on the tests. On Dooku's invitation, the Kaleesh fighter sacrificed practically all of his physical body to increase his skills, strength, and speed in combat to even rival a [[Jedi Master]]{{BuildXWingCite|47|Starfighter Aces}} through extreme [[Cybernetics|cybernetic]] upgrades to make himself an even more threatening and powerful warrior.''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]'' These augmentations turned an already capable warrior into a nearly unstoppable killing machine on the battlefield, giving him capabilities beyond those of a normal soldier. His transformation occurred over a period of time; Grievous gradually traded many of his biological parts for upgraded mechanical ones to become a murderous cyborg with one obsession: killing Jedi. By the time of his choice, Grievous had grown psychotic and thus saw his enhancements as a logical development. With his living Kaleesh flesh traded for cyborg implants, Grievous claimed that his changes were improvements he chose to celebrate. As recounted in one legend, Grievous's transformation had been over time, he initially only made simple enhancements before moving on to more extreme changes. The legend said Grievous transformed himself because he admired the logic of droids and wanted to mirror their infallibility, strength, and power. As for Grievous's mental state, however, the augmentations did little to settle his mind and led to increased anger, lashing out at all those he perceived as weak, often destroying the droids placed under his care and leadership, for in some ways they reminded him of his own weaknesses. One [[Standard day|day]], Grievous was fatally injured in a [[Sabotage of Grievous' shuttle|sabotaged]] [[Grievous' shuttle|shuttle]] crash during an [[assassin]]ation attempt ordered by [[San Hill]],{{Topps|set=2019 Topps Star Wars Masterwork|cardname=General Grievous}} [[Chairman]] of the InterGalactic Banking Clan, nearly killing him''[[Star Wars: A Galaxy at War]]'' and destroying most of what remained of his original body. As his [[troop carrier]] crashed, Grievous was thrown out of the wreckage{{HelmetCollectionCite|8|Helmets}} (German edition) and was taken from his homeworld and given a rare opportunity to become a living weapon. Rumors would later be spread that the crash was orchestrated by Dooku, which was indeed the case. Following the horrific shuttle crash that nearly took his life, the Kaleesh warlord regained consciousness in a [[bacta tank]] and discovered that [[FX-series medical assistant droid|surgical FX droids]] had nearly totally gutted and deformed him.{{BuildXWingCite|47|Starfighter Aces}} (German edition) Dooku claimed that the sabotage was carried out by a Jedi, since then fueling Grievous's deep and violent hatred for them. Betrayed and abused, with his sanity broken and mind fractured, Grievous accepted the offer of life-saving surgery and reconstruction and to return to military service, motivated by his hatred for the Republic and the Yam'rii. [[File:BountyHunters16-50yearstextless.png|thumb|right|300px|General Grievous, the cybernetic apprentice and servant of Count Dooku]] Even though Dooku was directly responsible for the shuttle crash that resulted in Grievous's injuries and subsequent transformation, Grievous was obviously psychologically confused with his final appearance. No evidence, at the end of the day, existed that Grievous was a victim in someone's grand design: despite Dooku's actions, Grievous had already decided to become a cyborg and was in that process no matter the Count's actions. Later historical work even disregarded the idea that Dooku was involved in the general's reconstruction as a shadowy manipulator due to evidence from Grievous's own life: it had been Grievous himself who wanted to be changed into a cyborg, no matter what role Dooku played in the final steps. Separatist [[Cyberneticist|cybernetic experts]] and [[Geonosian]] [[biotechnician]]s surgically reconstructed Grievous with the assistance of [[medical droid]]s, including the [[FX-9 surgical assistant]] [[FX-6]], under the supervision of Count Dooku and Darth Sidious. Along with the repairs and improvements performed by the Geonosian biotechs, some areas of Grievous's [[brain]] were altered without his knowledge. These modifications included the installation of [[heuristic combat programming]], which was intended to make him a smarter and faster fighter.''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]'' Furthermore, his demeanor was made more aggressive, his memory centers were modified to suppress recollections of his past and improve his concentration, and areas of his brain responsible for coordination were altered to make it easier for him to control his cyborg body. Circuitry was grafted onto his brain tissue, while wiring transmitted the brain's electrical impulses throughout the rest of his body. Many critical decisions were made regarding which parts of his original body should be preserved. By the time Grievous had been rebuilt, very little remained of his original form. These surviving structures consisted largely of portions of his brain, much of his spinal cord and spinal column, parts of his head, including his [[eye]]s, and a few other vital organs, such as his [[heart]], a pair of damaged [[lung]]s, his [[liver]], and the portions of his digestive system necessary to sustain his remaining organic elements. His lungs were given cybernetic implants as well. [[Scientist]]s transplanted his brain and eyes into a [[duranium]]-alloy body hidden beneath external [[armor]] plates, many of which were designed to resemble bone rather than [[metal]], with his remaining organs protected inside a pressurized [[synthskin]] gut-sack behind his armored [[rib]]s. Grievous would, in his new form, be able to survive in the [[vacuum]] of [[Realspace|space]] without a [[Environment suit|spacesuit]]. [[File:GrievousBrain-RotSVD.jpg|thumb|left|220px|A cut-away of Grievous's head.]] Grievous's armor, made of [[durasteel]] composite and duranium, was significantly easier to make and maintain than [[Mandalorian]] [[beskar]], although it was not as impenetrable. A head unit held parts of his skull and some of his brain, and was equipped with two [[antenna]]s[[Star Wars: Complete Vehicles (2018)|''Star Wars: Complete Vehicles'' (2018)]] and an [[Audio sensor|audio receptor]]. It could be opened for repairs or replacement of electronics, as well as for further surgery. Although Grievous's spinal cord carried signals to and from his robotic [[limb]]s and body, as well as the organ contents of his gutsack, millions of pinpoint [[electrode]]s were inserted into his brain from the lining of his [[helmet]] to [[Computer monitor|monitor]] brain activity and increase the timeliness of nerve signals. Adding to his already remarkable physical control, additional processors improved his agility and response times. Grievous's designers utilized [[crystal]] circuitry to improve his reaction times as much as the technology allowed, while keeping the circuitry safely protected behind duranium plate armor. The technology used for Grievous's conversion into a cyborg was not perfect; his heart and lungs were weakened, with his lungs irritated by their implants. This gave him a persistent cough for the rest of his life and, eventually, difficulty breathing. This information was kept in the Sith's possession in case they had additional candidates for conversion in the future. Due to his already compromised lungs, his speech occasionally degraded into a rasp, followed by random coughing fits. Even so, his enhancements allowed him to survive without food, water, or air- including underwater or in a vacuum- and made him immune to [[poison]]s and toxins. [[File:Kaleesh_statues2.png|thumb|right|270px|Statues of Grievous' transformation.]] While he claimed his old form was no more than weak flesh, Grievous would find himself disgusted with his cyborg body despite having wanted to exist in that very state for so long. Indeed, he retained several reminders of his past life. As a cyborg, Grievous frequently wore a [[Kaleesh cloak]], which was a vestige of his past identity, as well as a fearsome mask that was often worn by Kaleesh warriors. By the time he owned his [[Grievous's fortress|fortress]] on [[Vassek 3]], Grievous had several [[Statues of Grievous|statues]] he earned lining the halls of the privacy of his inner sanctuary that depicted his progression from his organic life into that of a cyborg.{{SW|url=video/behind-the-scenes-lair-of-grievous|text=Behind the Scenes: Lair of Grievous}} As evidenced by the statues, some accounts claimed he was already a cyborg when Count Dooku recruited him to lead the droid army. Ironically, Grievous despised his completely mechanical [[militia]], possibly revealing deeper thoughts about his own drastic transformation. Motivated''[[Star Wars: Book of Lists]]'' by his quest to become the greatest warrior in the galaxy,''[[Knights of Fate]]'' the once widely feared''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]'' Kaleesh warrior chose to be rebuilt as a cyborg in order to increase his power, extend his life, and gain an advantage when facing Jedi.{{Topps|set=2015 Topps Star Wars Chrome Perspectives|subset=Jedi Temple Archives|cardname=General Grievous|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/114595/cid/8022641/2015-Topps-Star-Wars-Chrome-Perspectives:-Jedi-Vs.-Sith-37-J-General-Grievous}} He even boasted about how drastically he had changed. Regardless of how he came to be, whether this was true or not, the former Kaleesh warlord went through numerous more operations to become soon-to-be General Grievous, the towering monster that stalked the galaxy. The cyborg's body was purposefully designed to resemble Grievous's original Kaleesh physique and warlord armor.{{BuildR2Cite|53|Droid Directory}} His arms were constructed to mimic the limbs he had been born with, while his faceplate paid homage to his previous life, mirroring the mask he had once worn and evoking the culture of his people.[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars – The Official Collector's Edition|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' – The Official Collector's Edition]] The engraved lines above the mask and on the chest plate resembled the patterns of karabbac-blood war paint. Additionally, the overall outline of the mask echoed the shape of his snub nose, while the duranium teeth resembled those of the karabbac beast as well as the bony protrusions on his chin. An [[ultrasonic vocabulator]], located behind the duranium teeth where his [[mouth]] would have been, generated and amplified Grievous's harsh, powerful voice, reproducing it almost perfectly. Though the cyborg's [[Skeleton|skeletal]] structure retained various echoes of his Kaleesh heritage, nearly all resemblance to other Kaleesh had been erased. He still had the characteristic [[snake]]-like [[Color|golden]] eyes with slit pupils eyelids, flat [[nose]], and elongated [[ear]]s of his species. At first sight, the only feature that belied his cyborg nature were the [[Reptile|reptilian]] eyes and a small amount of dark, tortured red Kaleesh flesh that could still be seen around his eyes and extended upward somewhat beneath the forehead of his faceplate. It was believed that only his eyes resembled the man he once was, and looking into them was like seeing into the gaping mouth of a [[black hole]]. =====Trained by Count Dooku===== [[File:CountDookuDeviousStrategist-SWDA.png|thumb|left|250px|Grievous was taught the Jedi arts by Count Dooku, a Jedi-turned-Sith Lord renowned for his swordsmanship.]] Grievous was initially given a [[Grievous' first lightsaber|Jedi weapon]] that had belonged to a [[Unidentified Jedi (Dooku)|long-deceased Jedi]] by Dooku, and he subsequently continued to add other weapons to the [[Collector|collection]] he had started while still a warlord on Kalee. Furious that his body had been entirely replaced with that of the droids he hated despite it being his own wish to become a cyborg that put him down such a path, Grievous immediately slaughtered all the guards present at his resurrection. Disgusted by his cyborg body, Grievous reluctantly accepted the job of Supreme Commander of the Separatist Droid Armies. He spent [[Standard hour|hours]] on end watching [[holovid]]s of Jedi in combat and reading every training manual his master could provide. When it came to dealing death, Grievous was a voracious learner, and to him, the various lightsaber forms were simply additional military techniques to master. He was eventually selected for [[Lightsaber combat|lightsaber training]] by none other than Count Dooku, the [[Jedi]]-turned-[[Sith Lord|Sith-Lord]] who was regarded as a legendary swordsman. Through a combination of Dooku's instruction and combat programs, Grievous mastered several of the classical Jedi lightsaber forms and developed his own impressive, highly effective fighting style. While Dooku trained Grievous in Jedi martial arts, Grievous, in turn, passed everything he had learned on to his IG-100 MagnaGuards to improve their effectiveness in combat. He later employed them as sparring partners to keep his own skills sharp. Grievous received a modified [[EV-series medical droid]], [[EV-A4-D]], as a gift to serve as his [[Doctor|surgeon]] and cybernetics [[Technician|mechanic]]. With access to all of Grievous's medical and cybernetic records and substantially increased intelligence, the fairly caustic and sometimes sadistic droid became the perfect foil for both Grievous and his doctor. A4-D's continued indispensability gave him an inflated sense of self-worth, as well as the distinction of being one of the few beings in the galaxy who understood his master's secrets. Although his caustic humor often irritated Grievous, A4-D was allowed to survive so long as he continued to perform his duties. Grievous owned a massive [[roggwart]] named [[Gor]], whom he kept in his [[fortress]] as both a pet and a guard [[dog]],{{BuildFalconCite|65|Guide to the Galaxy}} and for whom he expressed genuine affection. Grievous modified and improved his cybernetic body, with EV-A4-D helping to create and install the new components he requested. In this regard, his claim that he chose his own modifications could be considered true from a certain twisted perspective as well as literally. Grievous also had A4-D enhance Gor by attaching four cybernetic limbs to his back, a battle-armor [[Exoskeleton/Canon|exoskeleton]] over his body, and, just as he had, a chest plate and helmet to protect his vital organs and braincase. ===The Clone Wars=== ====Early efforts==== =====General of the Confederacy===== {{Quote|The droid general, Grievous, has our forces spread thin.|Mace Windu|[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]]}} Beyond receiving cybernetic enhancements, Grievous was trained in lightsaber combat by Dooku, who invited him to join his [[Separatist Crisis|Separatist movement]]. Grievous accepted the invitation{{HelmetCollectionCite|21|Databank A-Z}} and allied himself with other members of the Confederacy{{EncyclopediaCite|Darth Maul and Other Followers of the Dark Side}} and its leading [[Executive Separatist Council]]. One member of the group was San Hill, the same Muun who was, unbeknownst to Grievous, secretly behind the assassination attempt. All of them entrusted to him and Dooku their invaluable resources and large droid armies.{{ShipsandVehiclesCite|42|Starships and Vehicles}} Grievous was in direct opposition of the Galactic Republic and the Jedi Order, whom he had long regarded as mortal enemies. According to Legends, although Grievous had the outward appearance of a machine, he was pleased, for he alone understood his true potential and knew that he still retained some of what made him a living, breathing man. He believed this set him apart from the rest of the Separatists, droids and organics alike. However, neither droids nor organics felt comfortable in his company. [[File:GalaxyofHeroes-Droid-Army.png|right|thumb|300px|General Grievous was at the head of vast and powerful armies of battle droids.]] The CIS and Republic were soon launched into opposite warring sides of the [[The galaxy|galactic]] conflict known as the Clone Wars with the [[First Battle of Geonosis|Battle of Geonosis]], which Grievous secretly took part in, though he was not seen. While it was entirely by accident, Grievous's first clash against members of the Jedi Order came during the battle. He was positioned within the [[Stalgasin hive]] [[Geonosian catacombs|catacombs]] on [[Geonosis]] when the battle began, and while retreating, the cyborg ended up dueling a number of Jedi who incidentally wandered into the tunnels in the midst of the battle. Grievous prevented the Jedi and the [[clone trooper]]s from reaching the Separatist Council and escaped through the hive tunnels beneath Geonosis, leaving none of the [[Force-sensitive]]s he encountered alive to speak of his existence.''[[Star Wars: Battles that Changed the Galaxy]]'' As such, his involvement in the war's opening battle was not discovered by the Republic until much later. Grievous was quickly granted the rank of [[General]] in the [[Confederacy military]] and took upon the title of [[Supreme Martial Commander of the Separatist Droid Armies]], with which he acted as [[Commander-in-Chief]] and absolute leader of the [[Separatist Droid Army]].''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'' In the early weeks of the war, he publicly emerged onto the scene as a major Separatist leader[[Brotherhood (novel)|''Brotherhood'']] and soon became one of the Separatists' most important generals. As the war progressed, he evolved into Dooku's most powerful enforcer, serving as his best general and foremost battlefield commander. Renowned as one of the Separatists' military minds, Grievous was also among their most dangerous''[[Star Wars: The Secrets of the Clone Troopers]]'' and important leaders,[[Star Wars Day-at-a-Time Calendar 2021|''Star Wars'' Day-at-a-Time Calendar 2021]] as well as their most fearsome warrior,{{Topps|set=2020 Topps Star Wars Holocron Series|cardname=General Grievous}} in their effort to overthrow the Galactic Republic.{{Shatterpoint|set=Appetite for Destruction Squad Pack}} As later proclaimed in the legend he made for himself, Grievous swiftly distinguished himself during his tenure, rising through the ranks as a result of the many campaigns he fought on behalf of his masters and claiming victory after victory. He earned a name for himself among the powerful figures leading the Separatist movement, in part because of his sheer commitment to being the best soldier he could be. The legend stated that it was soon afterward that Grievous was promoted to the rank of general and given command of vast armies and fleets. [[File:Displate-GrievousDarkSide.png|thumb|left|300px|General Grievous expanded his lightsaber collection over the course of the Clone Wars by killing and defeating various Jedi.]] During the early [[standard week|weeks]] of the war, Grievous had an encounter with Jedi Master [[Ki-Adi-Mundi]], wounding the [[Cerean]]''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' and leaving him with scars across his cheek that took time to heal. Grievous brought a new wave of fear, with its threat came the possibility of panic and chaos across the [[galaxy]]. The war expanded faster than the Republic could comprehend, and there was now a very real chance of losing.[[Obi-Wan 3|''Obi-Wan'' 3]] The news of his abilities and subsequent victories sowed doubt within the Republic's military ranks and inspired outright fear in the hearts of his enemies. Quickly earning a reputation as both a savage, merciless warrior and a tactical genius, Grievous led the Confederacy{{Topps|set=2015 Topps Star Wars Masterwork|subset=Scum & Villainy|cardname=General Grievous}} to victory in many battles over the course of the Clone Wars,{{Topps|set=2025 Topps Star Wars Chrome|subset=Double Vision|cardname=DV-12 General Grievous|link=https://www.ebay.com/itm/306602524721}} at one point enjoying a straight string of victories. Grievous became a famous figure, although it was also the case that his IG-100 MagnaGuards played a major role in uplifting his terrifying reputation. As the Clone War proceeded to spread throughout the galaxy, Grievous and his forces engaged the [[Grand Army of the Republic]], and, under his command, the Separatist Droid Army attacked and conquered numerous Republic planets.{{Databank|confederacy-of-independent-systems|Confederacy of Independent Systems}} As the Separatist Army's imposing leader, Grievous and the tales of his brutality and victories would strike fear throughout the Republic,{{Databank|general-grievous|General Grievous}} although the Confederate populace were not told the stories of the general's bloody onslaughts.{{SWE|characters|minabonteri|Mina Bonteri}} Ultimately, many Republic citizens—as well as some citizens in CIS territory—came to see Grievous as the face of the Confederacy despite Dooku's status as its official leader. Those who knew the Kaleesh warrior's true nature saw this face as a brutal and terrifying one.{{Databank|url=confederacy-of-independent-systems-history-gallery|text=Confederacy of Independent Systems History Gallery}} {{C|Image 9 caption}} Few knew of his life before the Clone Wars, but during the conflict his name became infamous, synonymous with the worst excesses of brutality, slaughter, and ruthless warfare due to his devastating battlefield tactics. Grievous also shared his name with [[The Grievous Legion]], a [[battle group]] that included at least one [[Vulture-class starfighter|vulture droid]].[[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']] [[File:Clone-War-battlefront.png|thumb|right|270px|Grievous led one of his armies against the Republic.]] During the war, the clone troopers of the [[Republic Military]],{{TCW|Shadow of Malevolence|Shadow of ''Malevolence''}} having nicknamed the Confederacy's battle droids "[[clanker]]s,"{{TCW|Ambush}} accordingly nicknamed Grievous the "head clanker;" Grievous was also referred to within the Republic as the "droid general." While the war against the Yam'rii had given Grievous a vendetta against the Republic, the Clone Wars had changed him; indifferent to the Republic and the politics of the war as a whole, his only goal was to see the extermination of the Jedi Order, which led to him escalating the war as his quest to wipe out the Jedi once and for all carried on. Only Grievous' hatred of the Jedi and his unwavering confidence in his own abilities gave those who stood against him even the slightest chance of survival. Grievous fought against numerous Jedi during the war, relying on his lifetime of experience and with the advantages offered by his mechanical body, defeating and killing many of the Order's members. This enabled the general to collect [[lightsaber]]s and other trophies from bested opponents, resulting in a morbid collection of lightsabers as a renowned{{InsiderCite|230|A Certain Point of View}} and feared [[Jedi hunter]]. Grievous often maintained a strategy of elusiveness, difficult for the Republic's forces to locate him despite it being one of their primary objectives. Defiant by temperament, he never hesitated to challenge his opponents and frequently masterminded intricate, audacious plans that left the Republic's troops embarrassed. With four arms, four lightsabers, and an entire army behind him, Grievous had wreaked havoc on the Republic and caused immense suffering across the galaxy, earning a reputation as an unstoppable force.''[[Inquisitor: Rise of the Red Blade]]'' Most beings observing the warlord walking alongside his battle droids would find it difficult to accept that he was anything other than a machine.{{AtomicMassGames|url=transmission/databank-download-general-grievous|text=Databank Download: General Grievous|date=2023-05-30}} According to Jedi Knight [[Thirteenth Sister|Iskat Akaris]], Grievous was among the greatest fighters the galaxy had ever seen and had likely been responsible for more Jedi deaths during the conflict than anyone else. Akaris also noted that, although she had not yet encountered Grievous in person, little was known about whether he possessed any connection to the Force. She knew he was largely a cyborg and had been trained by Dooku, suggesting that he might be more difficult to sense or locate than others. [[File:GrievousCommandoDroid-GrievousIntrigue.png|thumb|left|300px|Grievous found himself personally invested in the development of the new BX-series droid commando.]] Early in the war,{{GermanFanCite|123|Database}} Grievous commissioned over twenty-six thousand [[B1-series battle droid]]s for deployment to [[Hakara]]. [[C-5DS]], Grievous' [[service droid]], contacted [[Poreni]], the [[chief supervisor]] of the [[Akiva production plant|droid factory]] on the Outer Rim planet [[Akiva]], regarding [[batch 4652-A]], which had failed to meet the expected combat performance. In response to the poor performance, Poreni apologized for the shortcomings and offered a twenty percent discount on the next batch of B1s, while also promising to improve the performance.''[[Star Wars Outlaws]]'' Around the same time, the Akiva production plant had demonstrated the new [[BX-series droid commando]] to Grievous, which convinced him of the droids capabilities. C-5DS accepted Poreni's discount and made an advance order of twelve thousand BX-series droid commando units,''[[Star Wars Outlaws]]'' as Grievous was personally interested in the new [[commando]]s. =====Duels with Kenobi===== {{Quote|I was told the Jedi was restrained.''"
"''Terribly sorry to disappoint you. I'm going to need you to release Senator Yarua and his daughter.''"
"''It's ''my'' turn to disappoint ''you.|Grievous duels Obi-Wan Kenobi|[[Hyperspace Stories 1|''Hyperspace Stories'' 1]]}} During the war, Grievous came to duel Jedi Master [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] numerous times, developing a history between them that made it so Grievous would choose to engage Kenobi over others. Grievous harbored a deep hatred for Kenobi.{{Topps|set=2019 Topps Star Wars Chrome Legacy|cardname=Specializing in Sith Lords}} Their confrontation turned the two into mortal adversaries, and their immense abilities were evenly matched.{{Topps|set=2015 Topps Star Wars Chrome Perspectives|subset=Sith Fugitives|cardname=General Grievous|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/117731/cid/8023186/2015-Topps-Chrome-Star-Wars-Perspectives-Jedi-vs.-Sith---Sith-Fugitives-4-General-Grievous}} Each time was inconclusive, but both realized that this could not always be the case. Kenobi's apprentice, [[Jedi]] [[Anakin Skywalker]], considered him a monster that needed to be stopped, even making it a personal mission to find Grievous. However, Grievous and Skywalker would not meet face-to-face until the war had nearly reached its conclusion. [[File:ObiWanKenobiJediKnight-SWCT.png|thumb|right|250px|Obi-Wan Kenobi, Grievous' nemesis]] As Kenobi, his then-[[Padawan]] Skywalker, and Senator Amidala were on a [[Unidentified secret mission|secret mission]] to meet with the [[Rodian]] [[The Ambassador|ambassador]] on an unknown [[Unidentified planet (Clone Wars)|planet]], Grievous had dispatched several B1 battle droids and a [[Unidentified MSE droid (Grievous)|modified]] [[MSE series|MSE droid]] to infiltrate their [[Consular-class light cruiser|''Consular''-class space cruiser]]. Then, Grievous appeared on their screen to reveal that everything was proceeding as planned, and that Kenobi was correct to assume he was involved. Grievous ordered his droids to attack, as he knew that the facilities were defeasible. Grievous successfully reprogrammed their ship's [[flight computer]], irreversibly directing them into the [[star|sun]].[[Star Wars: My First Comic Reader 1|''Star Wars: My First Comic Reader'' 1]] Grievous explained to Padmé that, while they were busy dealing with the battle droids, a little droid had snuck into their ship. While Anakin instructed Obi-Wan to remain in command, Padme assured him that they would handle the droid, but Grievous reminded them that they could not stop his droid in the same way they could not change the direction of the ship before ordering the droid to eliminate the Senator and the two Jedi. However, Kenobi and Skywalker took back control of the ship by having the mouse droid shoot at the control panel, and then the two Jedi destroyed the mouse droid, leaving only Grievous to admit defeat. Towards the beginning of the war, Grievous led a fleet of [[Providence-class Dreadnought|''Providence''-class Dreadnoughts]] to the [[Moon of Staggec]] with the aim of taking a [[Unidentified Jedi artifact|valuable item]] from Republic Senator [[Yarua]]. There, he and his droid forces [[Mission to the moon of Staggec|captured]] Yarua, [[Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]], and their associates. Shortly after, the droids also captured Yarua's daughter [[Viiveenn]] and Kenobi. Once Kenobi was restrained, Grievous interrogated Yarua and Viiveenn about their hidden item. Just then, Kenobi appeared behind Grievous and asked for Yarua and Viiveenn to be released. Grievous responded by drawing his lightsabers and engaging the Jedi in combat. [[Force push]]ed by Kenobi, Grievous immediately took Viiveenn hostage, only for Yarua to tackle him into space, sacrificing himself and allowing his daughter to escape along with the Jedi. While successfully escaping from the Separatists, Kenobi assumed Grievous was dead, but Yoda warned him not to underestimate him. =====Victories and defeats===== [[File:ADAndGrievous-JOTRMaceWindu3.png|thumb|left|300px|Grievous and AD-W4.]] Shortly into the war, Grievous met in person with the droid [[mercenary]] [[AD-W4]] to hire him to oversee the Separatists' operations on the planet [[Hissrich]]. Grievous admitted that he would have liked to fill this role himself, but could not as he had the entire Separatist Droid Army to command. AD-W4 was skeptical, but after seeing the [[Currency|payment]] available, left to fulfill the job. AD-W4 served as [[commander]] of the droids on the planet and [[Operation on Hissrich|battled]] with Jedi Master [[Mace Windu]] and his [[Mace Windu's squad|Jedi squad]]. Grievous later checked in via [[hologram]] to see the progress of AD-W4, and the droid falsely claimed to have killed Windu; however Grievous demanded the [[Mace Windu's lightsaber|Jedi's lightsaber]] as evidence, which was not presented.[[Jedi of the Republic – Mace Windu 3|''Jedi of the Republic – Mace Windu'' 3]] Ultimately, the droid was defeated and Hissrich was lost to the Republic.[[Jedi of the Republic – Mace Windu 5|''Jedi of the Republic – Mace Windu'' 5]] A while later, around the time of an [[Mission to Cato Neimoidia (Kenobi and Skywalker)|incident]] on [[Cato Neimoidia]], Grievous [[Strike on key supply chains for war munitions|struck on key supply chains for war munitions]]. Early in the war, Grievous launched an assault that failed to [[Attempt to capture Outpost 716|capture]] [[Outpost 716]], forcing Count Dooku to dispatch his personal [[Sith assassin|assassin]] and [[Sith apprentice|apprentice]], [[Asajj Ventress]], in [[Capture of Outpost 716|another attempt to capture]] the outpost. Darth Sidious doubts Dooku's faith in his two students, however, Ventress successfully captured Outpost 716. Soon after [[Ambush on the moon of Staggec|surviving an ambushed]], Ventress informs Dooku that it appears someone slipped information to Chancellor Palpatine that she would be returning to clean up Grievous's mess.[[Hyperspace Stories 5|''Hyperspace Stories'' 5]] In the [[Battle of Parein II 4|battle]] on the [[Parein II 4|fourth moon]] of [[Parein II]] saw the first real test of the IG-100 MagnaGuards, and on the battlefield, Grievous used a new weapon for the first time: the [[TSMEU-6 personal wheel bike]].{{EncyclopediaCite|Miscellaneous Ships and Vehicles (2)}} With Grievous in command and leading his troops at the front, the Republic forces led by Jedi General [[Sannen]]{{EncyclopediaCite|Battle Droids and Other Droids of War}} (English version) were utterly crushed. Sannen bravely tried to confront the cyborg directly, but the Jedi was instead stabbed in the [[throat]] with an [[electrostaff]]-wielding MagnaGuard. The MagnaGuards quickly became as feared as their master and shared his fearsome reputation. According to legend, early in the Clone Wars, Grievous was tasked with a critical mission: to travel to the distant [[Water|ice]] planet [[Alamass]] and deploy his droid army in an [[Battle of Alamass|assault]] that would destroy a strategic enemy [[Republic stronghold|stronghold]]. The operation was both dangerous and difficult, and it ultimately ended in failure after his [[Unidentified T-series tactical droid (Alamass)|tactical droid]] betrayed him. Despite knowing that transporting his forces to Alamass would cost him nearly a third of his droids along the way, Grievous accepted the risk. As he prepared to launch the invasion, however, his tactical droid defied its programming by altering the battle plan Grievous had devised, one that would have led to a Separatist victory. Eventually, Grievous was forced to admit defeat to his Sith masters, marking the first major loss of his military career. At some point, Grievous and Jedi Knight [[Pablo-Jill]] had a [[Duel over Duro|duel]] over the world of [[Duro]] in a [[Unidentified satellite city|collapsing satellite city]]. Jill was left injured and lost his blue-[[Plasma|bladed]] [[Pablo-Jill's lightsaber|lightsaber]] to Grievous.''[[Star Wars Lightsabers: A Guide to Weapons of the Force]]'' At some point, Grievous killed Jedi Master [[Jmmaar]] and took his green-bladed [[Jmmaar's lightsaber|lightsaber]] in order to add to his own collection.[[Star Wars: Complete Vehicles (2018)|''Star Wars: Complete Vehicles'' (2018)]] =====Venture to the Haven===== {{Quote|This negotiation is over.''"
"''Good. I tire of diplomacy. You will be destroyed, but at least I can make use of your ''parts''.|Telemak and Grievous|[[Bounty Hunters 38|''Bounty Hunters'' 38]]}} [[File:GrievousDestroysDroids-BountyHunters38.png|thumb|right|235px|Grievous destroyed numerous droids on The Haven.]] With the coordinates from [[Tarr Kligson]], a member of the [[Kligson clan]] who operated as a [[bounty hunter]],[[Bounty Hunters 37|''Bounty Hunters'' 37]] Grievous [[Skirmish on The Haven|traveled]] with two IG-100 MagnaGuards and several B1 battle droids to a large [[space station]], [[Haven (droid outpost)|the Haven]], orbiting [[Kligson's Moon]] in a [[Grohl sector|sector]].[[Revelations (2022) 1|''Revelations'' (2022) 1]] Grievous arrived to offer [[Telemak]], the station's protector, the protection of the Confederacy of Independent Systems, but Telemak, knowing what Grievous wanted—more droids to join the Separatist Droid Army—interrupted him before he could finish and insulted him, suggesting that he couldn't beat the Galactic Republic with those he currently "enslaves." Grievous was dissatisfied that they would stay here and deteriorate, waiting for their leader, [[Ajax Sigma]], to come back rather than seizing the chance he provided them to [[Battle on Kligson's Moon|inflict revenge on the Jedi Order that had destroyed him]]. Before his next statement, Telemak declared that they do not serve organics, concluded the discussions, and surrounded him with droids. Grievous happily accepts and, tired of diplomacy, attacks Telemak and its droid army. Grievous destroyed numerous droids, but he lost all battle droids and may have overestimated the droids' capabilities since they wanted to be "free" and thought it would be pointless to utilize them for the Separatists. One of his MagnaGuards was then destroyed, and Grievous moved to deal with Telemak directly, who continued to ridicule him, but several droids seized him. He defeated them all, proving they couldn't compete with him. Telemak informed the general that many of them were willing to sacrifice themselves and asked if he would like to test how many he could defeat. Grievous realized he had no time dealing with Telemak's droids and called in his [[Sheathipede-class transport shuttle|''Sheathipede''-class transport shuttle]], jumped on board, promised to return to wrap up the conversation once the Republic fall and Telemak could keep its army since the Separatists could build more since droids are disposable, and left the station. =====Skirmish on Caliban===== {{Quote|You belong to me, Kenobi. And you will do as I say… Or you will ''die''.|Grievous after capturing Kenobi|[[Star Wars Adventures: The Clone Wars – Battle Tales 5|''Star Wars Adventures: The Clone Wars – Battle Tales'' 5]]}} [[File:GrievousAndKenobiInTheSnow-TCWBattleTales5.jpg|thumb|left|290px|Grievous and Kenobi duel on the frozen moon of Caliban.]] Grievous [[Battle on Caliban|attacked]] the frozen moon of [[Caliban]] after he [[Invasion of Caliban|invaded]] the moon and destroyed a [[Lunar ice bridge|lunar bridge]] in the procession. He also [[Prisoner|captured]] Jedi General Kenobi and [[Clone Marshal Commander]] [[Cody]], along with their [[squad]] of clone troopers and ordered them to rebuild the bridge, to allow him to freely move weapons and battle droids across the moon. Kenobi, however, answered that he and the clones would not have to work for Grievous, since according to the [[Galactic Accord of Systems]], no war prisoner could be forced into manual labor. The Separatist general smacked Kenobi to the ground and threatened him with death if he would not follow his orders. Kenobi and the clones started constructing the bridge, but, during the operation, Grievous was distracted by a group of native [[Qubey]]s, in league with Kenobi, who piled on top of him and managed to steal back [[Obi-Wan Kenobi's third lightsaber|Kenobi's lightsaber]], which had been tucked into Grievous's cloak, without the cyborg noticing. Although the bridge was completed sometime later, Grievous ordered the battle droids to execute Kenobi and his men, but the Qubeys ambushed the droids, allowing Kenobi to engage Grievous while the clones reclaimed their [[blaster]]s. In the ensuing battle, Grievous overwhelmed Kenobi, but when he was right where the Master wanted him, Kenobi used the Force to cause an avalanche, burying Grievous and his droids. Kenobi and the clones escaped on a [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry]] [[gunship]], realizing that staying to capture Grievous would put the Qubey further in danger, and they destroyed the bridge before Separatist reinforcements could arrive. ====Attack on the ''Stellar Rise''==== {{Quote|Tell me about the hilt you have found. I have been monitoring your mission here in the Outer Rim to collect rare Jedi artifacts from the High Republic Era.|Grievous, to Anap Ree-Di|{{InsiderCite|210|Galactic Tales: Saber Truth}}}} [[File:SaberTruthCover.png|thumb|right|264px|Grievous was on the search for Jedi artifacts from the High Republic Era.]] At some point during the Clone Wars, aboard the [[Arquitens-class light cruiser|''Arquitens''-class light cruiser]] ''[[Stellar Rise]]'', clone trooper [[Checkbox]] was inspecting five mysterious crates that had been recovered near the [[Kazlin system]] when he heard something moving inside one. As he approached, a blue lightsaber sliced through the crate, and through him. Grievous emerged, followed by four IG-100 MagnaGuards. They had secretly [[Infiltration of the Stellar Rise|boarded]] the ship to search for a rare [[Jedi artifact|artifacts]]. After quickly taking the bridge, Grievous confronted [[Captain]] [[Lozz Beraf]], who revealed through his reaction that a Jedi was aboard. Jedi Knight [[Anap Ree-Di]] appeared and boldly ordered Grievous to leave. Instead, Grievous unleashed his four lightsabers and sent the MagnaGuards after her. Anap led them through the ship, eventually separating herself from the others and engaging Grievous alone. During their duel, Grievous revealed that he knew Anap was transporting ancient [[High Republic Era|High Republic-era]] artifacts to the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant]]. He demanded the location of a valuable Jedi [[Lightsaber hilt|hilt]], hoping to add it to his collection. Anap appeared cornered and even threw her lightsaber away. When Grievous moved to claim it, she used the Force to pull it back, kicked him into an [[Escape pod|escape-pod]] corridor, and sealed the door behind him. She warned that cutting through the door would expose him to the vacuum of space. Grievous reluctantly lowered his weapon as Anap revealed a second, older lightsaber. Anap launched the escape pod, leaving Grievous stranded as the ''Stellar Rise'' jumped to [[lightspeed]]. Alone, he remembered Count Dooku’s warning not to let his obsession with Jedi weapons cloud his judgment. ====The ''Malevolence'' campaign==== {{Quote|General Kenobi. Did you really think I would leave the hyperdrive unguarded?''"
"''Anything is possible. You haven't exactly impressed ''me'' today.|Grievous and Obi-Wan Kenobi|{{TCW|Destroy Malevolence|Destroy ''Malevolence''}}}} [[File:Grievous_on_Malevolence_bridge.png|thumb|left|300px|Grievous giving orders on the ''Malevolence'' bridge.]] Around the time of the [[Battle of Christophsis]], Grievous had spread Republic forces thin, which hampered Republic efforts to locate [[Rotta]] the [[Hutt]] after he was secretly kidnapped by the CIS. After its victories on [[Christophsis]] and [[Dantooine]] made the war seem like it was swinging in the Republic's direction, Grievous took command at [[Hypori]] and led a brutal [[Battle of Hypori|slaughter]] of clone troopers and Jedi. During the battle, a group of Jedi Knights were taken by surprise. After the battle, the wreckage of an [[Acclamator-class transgalactic military assault ship|''Acclamator''-class cruiser]] that crashed earlier on Hypori remained as a grim memorial.''[[Catalyst: A Rogue One Novel]]'' Grievous was also known to lead [[Navy|starfleets]] within the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems Navy|Confederate Navy]] to further his conquest of Republic planets, with his ships leaving the worlds wrecked and [[fire|burned]]. As he was leading the Separatist forces in the Clone Wars, Grievous was given the [[Subjugator-class heavy cruiser|''Subjugator''-class heavy cruiser]] ''[[Malevolence]]{{TCW|Rising Malevolence|Rising ''Malevolence''}}'' as his [[flagship]]. From the ''Malevolence''{{'s}} [[Bridge (starship)|bridge]], Grievous could command millions of battle droids, and he used his new [[warship]] in the [[Malevolence Campaign|''Malevolence'' Campaign]],{{Databank|battle-droid|Battle Droid}} wherein he executed attacks on [[Republic Navy|Republic fleets]] that left no survivors. Grievous simply gradually unveiled the capabilities of his new ship. For weeks, he tore through Republic [[Merchant|shipping]], destroying cargo vessels and their escorts, like he had done with his own abilities. For [[Standard month|month]], rumors circulated of a terrifying new Separatist weapon alongside widespread concern over the cyborg general. Once such attack came with the [[Battle of the Phu system]], where the ''Malevolence'' wiped out three [[Venator-class Star Destroyer|''Venator''-class Star Destroyers]]{{BuildFalconCite|43|Starship Fact File}} under the command of Jedi Master [[Ares Nune]].{{BuildFalconCite|43|Starship Fact File}} (German edition) Following that victory, while stationed in the [[Abregado system]] with Count Dooku aboard, a [[Plo Koon's fleet|Republic fleet]] led by Jedi Master [[Plo Koon]] and [[Clone Commander]] [[Wolffe]] aboard the Venator ''[[Triumphant]]'' arrived in the system to [[Battle of Abregado|engage]] the warship. The [[mega-ion cannon]]s of the ''Malevolence'' disabled the Republic [[fleet]]'s [[deflector shield]]s, and fired on the defenseless [[Star Destroyer]]s. The entire fleet was destroyed, although a few individuals managed to survive by launching away from the vessels inside escape pods. General Plo Koon, Commander Wolffe, [[Clone Sergeant]] [[Sinker]], and clone trooper [[Boost]] were the only survivors, having been eventually rescued by Anakin Skywalker and his Padawan [[Ahsoka Tano]] aboard the [[G9 Rigger-class light freighter]] ''[[Twilight]]''. As a result of the escape of survivors, Dooku's trust in Grievous was shaken, and the Sith Lord left to discuss the matter with his master, Darth Sidious. [[File:General_Grievous_XW2.png|thumb|right|250px|Grievous flees the critically-damaged ''Malevolence'' aboard ''Soulless One''.]] After later [[Battle of the Ryndellia system|destroying]] a Republic [[convoy]] in the [[Ryndellia system]], Grievous, as instructed by Dooku via hologram, took the ''Malevolence'' to [[Battle of the Kaliida Nebula|destroy]] a Republic medical facility that was treating over 60,000 wounded clones. In order to reach the target, the ''Malevolence'' had to navigate around the [[Kaliida Nebula]], a time-consuming journey that frustrated Grievous. Upon arriving at its destination, the [[ion cannon]]s of the ''Malevolence'' were disabled by a small strike force of fighters led by General Skywalker. After this, a Republic [[Obi-Wan Kenobi's taskforce|fleet]] led by Obi-Wan Kenobi aboard his flagship the ''[[Negotiator]]'' arrived and attacked Grievous's crippled ship. Grievous was forced to retreat, but Dooku came up with a new plan; taking Senator Amidala hostage. After Amidala's ship was captured, the Republic fleet stopped firing, and a rescue team was sent to board the ''Malevolence'' led by Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker aboard the ''Twilight''. Grievous fought Obi-Wan Kenobi briefly and overpowered him but as he prepared to kill the Jedi, Kenobi jumped onto another vehicle, saluting the general as he left, and the two Jedi managed to escape with Padmé and her [[protocol droid]] [[C-3PO]]. Grievous ordered the ''Malevolence'' to retreat to [[hyperspace]], arranging to meet his warship at a Separatist base in [[Sector Four (Confederacy)|Sector Four]]. Grievous pursued ''Twilight'' in his personal [[starfighter]], the ''[[Soulless One]]'', with a [[squadron]] of Vulture droids, but Skywalker had sabotaged the navigation system of the Malevolence so that when the ship engaged its hyperdrive, it crashed directly into the nearby [[Dead Moon of Antar]]. Grievous escaped in his starfighter, ''Soulless One'', but he had personally disconnected a transmission with a questioning Count Dooku. While Grievous escaped, the Separatist effort suffered a blow. The ship's loss was undoubtedly a blow to Darth Sidious's plans and the Separatist movement, as well as a poor return on such a large investment of time and resources. In addition, the absence of the Malevolence kept the arrogant Grievous at bay. Only a few months after this session, Grievous would face [[Luminara Unduli]] in person at [[Nadiem]] in the Outer Rim.{{EncyclopediaCite|Mace Windu and Other Users of the Force}} ====Attack on Rishi Station==== {{Quote|All the preparations for your invasion are in order.''"
"''Good. Our fleet is approaching the system. We are almost at the rendezvous point.''"
"''Very good, my lord. I will await your arrival.''"
"''The destruction of Kamino will stop their production of clones for good.|Asajj Ventress informs Grievous that the preparations for his invasion of Kamino are in order|{{TCW|Rookies (episode)}}}} The Republic would make efforts to locate Grievous, but, even after [[Clone Intelligence]] spotted him in the [[Balmorra system]], the general remained out of the Republic's sight. Several standard weeks after his sighting in the Balmorra system, Anakin Skywalker was losing sleep while searching for the cyborg, but he denied himself his needed rest until Grievous was found. While Obi-Wan Kenobi believed that they would know if Grievous entered their current quadrant, the general was currently preparing to launch an attack on [[Kamino]]. Under the Separatist invasion plan, Grievous would be able to remain undetectable, as he was to take over the [[Rishi Station]]. Seizing the listening outpost would enable the Separatists to keep its all-clear signal broadcasting; Republic forces would assume Kamino was still secure, meaning Grievous's fleet could launch a surprise assault on the planet. [[File:Grievous_Rookies.png|thumb|left|300px|Grievous speaks with Ventress via hologram aboard his warship.]] Grievous, determined to stop the clone production on Kamino, sent a team of BX-series droid commandos to [[Defense of Rishi Station|seize]] [[Rishi]] Station from the clone troopers stationed there. After the commando droids had taken control of the station, Grievous was contacted by their [[Sparky|captain]] aboard his [[Munificent-class star frigate|''Munificent''-class star frigate]], who informed him that the outpost was secure, and that they managed to disable the alarm and activate the all-clear signal. Grievous ordered him to keep the signal activated, so as not to draw the Republic's attention and lose the element of surprise. After ending the transmission, a battle droid informed the general that their [[spy]] on Kamino, Asajj Ventress, was contacting him. Ventress assured Grievous that everything was ready for their invasion. Pleased, the general informed her that he had almost reached their rendezvous point. However, the station was soon visited by [[Clone Captain]] [[Rex]] and Clone Commander Cody, who were inspecting the station as part of a security checkup. The two [[Clone trooper officer|clone officers]] soon discovered the outpost had been taken, and met with the survivors and retook the station from the commando droids. When communication with the droids was abruptly cut off, Grievous sent a [[battalion]] of B1-series battle droids to inspect the station and was informed that there were clones in the station. One of the clone troopers, [[Hevy]], sacrificed himself to destroy the base, which angered Grievous as he believed that the droids had blown it up instead. The base's destruction ended the all-clear signal and alerted the Republic [[Skywalker's fleet|fleet]] to Grievous's location. Upon the Republic's arrival, the Kaleesh cyborg immediately realized that his forces were heavily outgunned, and ordered his fleet to make a full retreat out of the system, therefore postponing the Kamino invasion. Knowing that Kamino will be targeted again, a 'dead or alive' warrant was issued for General Grievous by the [[Galactic Senate]]. The Republic discovered a hidden [[Separatist weapons factory (Abrion Major)|Separatist weapons factory]] beneath a granary complex on [[Abrion Major]] that would produce the new mega-ion cannon for Count Dooku and General Grievous, capable of immobilizing an entire fleet. Later on, Kenobi led the 212th Assault Battalion on the [[Battle of Abrion Bridge|assault]] at [[Abrion Bridge]] and successfully captured the plans but suffered heavy losses. ====Skytop Station campaign==== =====Fighting in the Outer and Mid Rim===== {{Quote|Our intelligence has confirmed that Grievous's spies have been intercepting our transmissions.''"
"''He must have some sort of secret listening post out there somewhere.''"
"''That would explain how he's been able to ambush our fleets.|Obi-Wan Kenobi, Ahsoka Tano, and Anakin Skywalker|audio=InterceptedTransmissions-DoaD.flac|{{TCW|Downfall of a Droid}}}} [[File:General_Grievous_duing_the_Outer_Rim_Campaign.png|thumb|right|242x242px|General Grievous during his campaign in the Outer Rim.]] Only a short time after the ''Malevolence'' offensive,{{EncyclopediaCite|Anakin Skywalker}} Grievous launched another [[Skytop Station campaign|campaign]], targeting Republic fleets in the galaxy's [[Outer Rim Territories]] by using the newly created [[Skytop Station]], a Separatist [[battlesphere]] that served as a [[listening post]]. Able to locate and ambush Republic fleets without warning, Grievous moved his forces against the Republic's forces in the Outer Rim, and, due to the victories he gained, the Republic's foothold in the Outer Rim began to slip from their disastrous losses.{{TCW|Duel of the Droids}} Despite suffering a few serious setbacks, Grievous continued on his march, leading the Separatists to numerous triumphs and proving himself a nearly indestructible opponent for both the Jedi and the Republic, leaving a trail of conquest and destruction across the galaxy. All within a single month, he invaded several planets and [[Outer Rim blockades|blockaded]] several important [[hyperspace route]]s leading to [[Bespin]], [[Kessel]], and [[Mon Cala]]mari. Anakin Skywalker and his battle group fought against Grievous's forces in the campaign, but failed to stop Grievous's advance. His next move was to capture [[Bothawui]], the [[Bothan]] homeworld and a vital intelligence planet for the Republic. However, Grievous pulled the Republic fleet out of hyperspace and engaged the Jedi and their clone troopers before they could reach Bothawui. Grievous reconsidered his decision to stop pursuing Skywalker's fleet in order to help coordinate [[Battle of Falleen|attacks against Republic forces]] stationed near the planet [[Falleen]]. With the help of Count Dooku and Asajj Ventress, Grievous led an agile fleet to attack Falleen and captured the planet for the Separatists before preparing to take the planet of Bothawui in the [[Mid Rim Territories]]''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: The Visual Dictionary]]'' to [[Battle of Bothawui|attack]] Skywalker's fleet with information from his spies. After the [[Falleen battle group|Republic battle group]] at Falleen was wiped out, the fleet under the command of Grievous continued on to Bothawui, which was of high strategic value and was currently being protected by Skywalker and a weary fleet of Republic cruisers. Realizing that attacking from above would put them at a disadvantage, Grievous moved the fleet through the [[asteroid]] field to engage Skywalker's fleet, knowing that the asteroids would protect him from any surprise attacks. Before Skywalker led Gold Squadron the engagement, this tactic allowed Grievous to damage the Republic cruiser. [[File:Grievous_Battle_of_Bothawui.png|thumb|left|300px|General Grievous at the Battle of Bothawui.]] Skywalker then deployed into the [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gold Squadron]] from his flagship, the ''[[Resolute]]'', to try and draw out the general. As Grievous's fleet exited the asteroid field, it was able to severely damage one the Republic [[cruiser]]s, but was quickly outflanked by [[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer]]s hidden on the asteroids. Grievous was shocked and angered that Skywalker knew what he was planning to do, and ordered an immediate retreat. However, the battle droid commander was dumbfounded as to where to go, so Grievous abandoned his [[Grievous's frigate|flagship]] and the droids in annoyance. He quickly fled in his personal starfighter, ''Soulless One'', rather than risk destruction or capture. He fled, leaving the Separatist fleet to be destroyed. Both actions were indicative: Skywalker frequently chose bold, maneuvers, while Grievous fled as soon as he realized a battle was not in his favor. He was soon spotted by Skywalker, who attempted to pursue him in his [[Delta-7B Aethersprite-class light interceptor|Delta-7B ''Aethersprite''-class interceptor]] but was soon sent spinning out of control as a result of the damage his fighter had sustained earlier in the fight. Meanwhile, Grievous had managed to power up the ''Soulless One''{{'s}} hyperdrive, allowing him to jump into hyperspace. The rest of Grievous' fleet, however, was destroyed. However, Grievous' victory over Falleen helped offset his first unsuccessful invasion on Kamino, as well as his attack on Bothawui. Following his loss at Bothawui, Grievous contacted the [[Trandoshan]] [[Scavenger|salvager]] [[Gha Nachkt]], and requested that he search the debris field for an [[R2-D2|astromech droid]], telling him to rendezvous at Skytop Station on [[Ruusan]]'s [[moon]] once the droid was located. The droid in question was R2-D2, the astromech droid of General Skywalker, with Grievous suspecting that he held vital military secrets within his memory banks that could aid the Separatists. =====Trapping Skywalker===== {{Quote|Ah! There's our Jedi tracking beacon. Skywalker, now you have fallen into ''my'' trap.|Grievous after R3-S6 activated the tracking beacon on Skywalker's Jedi Starfighter|audio=JediTrackingBeacon-DoaD.flac|}} [[File:Between_those_tin_cans.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Grievous's ''Munificent''-class star frigates attempts to block the ''Twilight''{{'s}} escape.]] Later, Grievous was contacted by Nachkt, who informed him that he had the droid in his possession and was en route to their rendezvous point. He also revealed that Skywalker had boarded his [[Vulture's Claw|ship]] looking for it, and believing it to be valuable, requested more money than they had previously agreed upon. However, Grievous threatened him, telling Nachkt to not anger him and to arrive as fast as he could, or else there would be consequences. Not soon after, Grievous detected Skywalker's fighter's beacon, which had been activated by [[R3-S6]], Skywalker's replacement astromech droid, who in reality was a Separatist spy. Having fallen into his trap, Grievous aboard his new [[Grievous's Munificent-class star frigate (suspected Confederate space)|command ship]] suddenly dropped out of hyperspace and [[Mission to suspected Confederate space|attacked]], destroying his [[hyperspace transport ring]], preventing his escape, proceeding to launch an entire squadron of vulture droids to kill the Jedi, and ordered his cruisers to move in. However, Skywalker was rescued by the timely arrival of his apprentice Ahsoka Tano and the ''Twilight'', Skywalker's freighter. The general then ordered his ships to prevent their escape, but the ''Twilight'' was able to navigate between the two battleships, causing them to collide with each other, destroying the vulture droids. The Jedi's ship then jumped to hyperspace. In his anger, Grievous physically decapitated an unfortunate battle droid who had pointed out to him that the Jedi had escaped. =====Encounter on Skytop Station===== {{Quote|Sorry to interrupt your playtime, ''grumpy'', but wouldn't you prefer a ''challenge?
"''That wouldn't be you!|Ahsoka Tano and Grievous after the latter attempts to kill the unconscious Captain Rex|audio=InteruptPlaytime-DotD.flac|}} [[File:Ahsoka_vs_Grievous.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Grievous duels Ahsoka Tano aboard Skytop Station.]] Nachkt soon arrived at Skytop Station with R2-D2, and proceeded to disassemble the astromech droid and sift through his memory banks for any vital information. Grievous listened as Nachkt revealed that the data within the astromech had never been erased and contained a wealth of information that they could exploit. Trying to use this to his advantage, Nachkt demanded double the agreed price, but Grievous, having grown tired of his incompetence, proceeded to impale him with his lightsaber, killing him with Grievous cackling in his death. He was then informed by the spy R3-S6 that the Jedi had infiltrated the station in order to rescue the droid. Grievous ordered R3 to distract them until he arrived, and tasked his IG-100 MagnaGuards with taking care of the astromech while he confronted the Jedi. Grievous then arrived to confront the Republic forces outside the [[reactor]] room and attacked Skywalker's apprentice, Ahsoka Tano; the two exchanged lightsaber blows, and Tano was knocked against a wall and rendered unconscious. The clones attempted to defend themselves with blaster fire as the cyborg general approached them, and Grievous eliminated all of them except for Rex and [[Denal]]. He prepared to kill Rex, but Tano regained consciousness and blocked the blow, saving the clone captain. Grievous doubted that Ahsoka would be a challenge and activated another lightsaber and continued to duel her. Knowing that she couldn't defeat Grievous by herself, she successfully evaded his attacks and drew him away from the clones and then escaped with R3-S6 into a storage room. While searching one of abandoned spare parts rooms for her, Grievous was informed that Skywalker had gone to rescue his astromech. He then had R3 go to the hangar and ensure that Skywalker would not escape. Hanging from the ceiling, Grievous found Tano and clamped a metal hand around the Padawan's throat, examining her fallen lightsaber with his free hand. Believing he had won, Grievous taunted his prisoner, saying Skywalker would be next after he eliminated her. Despite Tano's claims that her Master would destroy Skytop Station, Grievous believed otherwise. However, Tano's beliefs proved true when the Republic squad detonated the explosives in the reactor room, crippling the listening post's [[repulsorlift]] systems. As the station shook from the impact, Tano managed to use her lightsaber to [[Dismemberment|sever]] the hand clamped around her throat. Although Grievous attempted to slash her with one of his lightsabers, Tano retrieved her weapon and escaped through an air duct. Their objective complete and R2-D2 safely back with Skywalker, the Jedi made their escape. Grievous then retreated aboard the ''Soulless One'' as the station collapsed around him. ====Various advancements==== {{Quote|More machine than alive, though more dangerous for it.|[[Jedi Master]] Yoda on Grievous|}} [[File:InvisibleHandStarboard-FF.png|thumb|right|234x234px|The ''Invisible Hand'', as seen from starboard.]] With the loss of the ''Malevolence'', Grievous suffered not only the loss of a vessel, but also a significant loss of face, and he wouldn't be trusted with a vessel worthy for his position as Supreme Commander of the Separatist Droid Armies.{{BuildFalconCite|75|Starship Fact File}} The [[Neimoidian]] [[Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray]], who detested the general for giving the beast preferential treatment from Count Dooku, had found slight sense of joy. In turn, Grievous hated the cowardly, pretentious, and foolish Gunray.{{EncyclopediaCite|Republic and Separatist Ships (1)}} For a time, Grievous had been forced to command ''Munificent''-class star frigates as his flag ships. Eventually, Grievous decided he instead wanted the ''Providence''-class Dreadnought ''[[Invisible Hand]]'' to fill the role of his flagship, demanding the vessel from Gunray, something he finds cruelly amusing but clearly insisted on by none other than Darth Sidious himself. The ship was indeed turned over to Grievous, who used it throughout the conflict in addition to other flagships.{{TCW|ARC Troopers (episode)}} and could utilize it, at least, to further solidify his terrible image for ruthless excess and the flagship's great effect. The ''Invisible Hand'' became well-known and feared throughout the Republic and was a constant threat in battles for key Republic worlds. Like on the ''Malevolence'' before it, Grievous could command millions of droids from the bridge of the ''Invisible Hand''. At some point prior to the discovery of his lair by the Jedi-led Republic team, Jedi Master [[Neebo]] was on the moons of [[Sanjin]]. Neebo was [[Mission to the moons of Sanjin|attempting]] to protect [[refugee]]s on the moons, but she was presumed missing.{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode010.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Lair of Grievous}} However, Jedi Master [[Kit Fisto]] and his former apprentice [[Nahdar Vebb]] later found [[Neebo's lightsaber|her lightsaber]] among the trophies of the Jedi Grievous had murdered, and Vebb believed that what was in the room were trophies from the Jedi Grievous had killed. There were rumors that Grievous had [[Grievous' laboratory|built]] a [[laboratory]] on [[Belsus]], the moon of [[Gentes]].''[[Star Wars: Uprising]]''—Crew Run: "Laboratory of Grievous" During the war, Grievous ravaged the homeworld of a loathsome rascal named [[Ralakili]], leaving the man with a hate for droids that culminated in him running droid fighting pits in [[the Lodge]] on the planet [[Vandor]].''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide]]'' ====Proving his competence==== {{Quote|You might have been a proud warrior once, but now you are just a pawn in Dooku's game!''"
"''I wield great power, Jedi fool!''"
"''That power will only consume you.|Kit Fisto and Grievous|audio=ProudWarrior-LoG.flac|}} [[File:Vebb_Grievous_Fisto.jpg|thumb|left|250x250px|Grievous activates two more of his lightsabers during combat with the Jedi.]] While Grievous had some successes, he made enough mistakes that Count Dooku wanted to hold the cyborg general accountable for them. The Republic had been searching for Trade Federation Nute Gunray, who had just been [[Rescue_on_the_Tranquility|rescued]] by Asajj Ventress,{{TCW|Cloak of Darkness}} and Dooku had deactivated his bodyguards and [[Mission to Grievous's castle|lured]] the Republic into Grievous's fortress on Vassek's third moon, hoping to test Grievous and leave him alive or dead if necessary.{{EncyclopediaCite|Scarif and Other Planets in the Outer Rim}} Upon entering his home, Grievous found that his MagnaGuards had been deactivated. He was swiftly surprised by Kit Fisto and Nahdar Vebb, along with a [[Fil's Squad|squad]] of clones led by Commander [[Fil]]. Fisto mockingly welcomed him upon his return and requested him to surrender so that the Senate could show him more mercy. Grievous replied that Fisto would be the one pleading for mercy as he ignited his two lightsabers and fought the two Jedi, holding them off and then separating two more blades. While Grievous was fighting Fisto and Vebb, the clone troopers pulled the [[ascension cable]]s attached to his legs. Fisto then cut off Grievous's lower legs, but he immediately jumped to the ceiling using his four limbs, which gave the cyborg a lot of mobility. After being pulled down, he continued to retreat and blocked Vebb's attack and spun one of his lightsabers and threw it directly at his master. He rushed back up and pulled the cords to grab one of the clone troopers and use them as a shield and threw them at Vebb, causing him to fall to the ground. Grievous returned to the ground, then to the ceiling, where he was struck in the face by a blaster, and engaged the clones. He then entered a hidden door and trapped the surviving Jedi and clones. In his control room, Grievous ordered EV-A4-D to proceed with repairs, and he reactivated the remotely deactivated MagnaGuards, locked down the fortress, and set off a trap that killed another clone. The group then attempted to leave the castle, but before they could, they were locked in. Grievous then ordered his MagnaGuards to destroy their shuttle outside. Grievous then appeared on a hologram, and proceeded to taunt the remaining group. Fisto fired back, asking Grievous to come out of hiding. He replied that while they wait, they should experience all that his home had to offer. As his hologram flickered off, the floor beneath disappeared. Fisto and Vebb were able to easily jump back onto the floor still remaining, however one clone trooper fell to his death. Clone Commander Fil dispersed his cable, and was pulled back up by the Jedi. A short while after recovering from what had just happened, Grievous unleashed his pet roggwart Gor, in an attempt to finally finish them off. Fisto warns Vebb and Fill that they are about to encounter something considerably more dangerous than the general. After repairs had been completed, Grievous checked on the Jedi to see whether they had been killed, but he discovered that the Jedi had killed his beloved pet instead. Grievous was enraged by Gor's death, who had paid a high price for his life, and promised vengeance, adding to his hatred of the Jedi. However, Dooku interrupted Grievous, informing him that he had invited the Jedi into his lair to reassess his usefulness following his recent setbacks at the hands of the Jedi. An enraged Grievous resolved to seek down and kill Fisto and Vebb. Upon leaving his command center, A4-D alerted Grievous that the Jedi were about to enter the control room and separated them. Grievous then engaged Padawan Nahdar Vebb in a fierce duel; due to his multiple limbs, Grievous easily killed Vebb with a dirty, but well-timed blaster shot. The general then added [[Nahdar Vebb's lightsaber|Vebb's lightsaber]] to his collection. Fisto saw the duel and his former apprentice's death on video, along with Grievous threatening and intimidating him. Having eliminated Vebb, Grievous then followed and chased after Fisto, forcing the Jedi onto the castle's outer platform and emerging before him, climbing from below the platform. [[File:FistovsGrievous.png|thumb|right|220x220px|Grievous and Fisto engage in battle.]] As the two fought, Fisto [[Kit Fisto's lightsaber|deactivated his lightsaber]] and snuck up on Grievous, taking advantage of the dense fog that surrounded the castle. Grievous positioned his four lightsabers in front of him to defend himself, but Fisto attacked him from behind, nearly taking him by surprise as he perfectly timed Fisto's attack. The two continued their fierce lightsaber duel, and despite Grievous' superior lightsaber skill, Fisto gained the upper hand{{HelmetCollectionCite|64|Databank A-Z}} and managed to sever one of Grievous' hands holding Vebb's lightsaber, reclaiming the weapon in respect of his fallen comrade. Fisto pushed him with the Force, causing him to lose his balance, but he recovered quickly and continued the duel with renewed vigor. Suddenly, three MagnaGuards arrived and joined Grievous in battle to support their leader's attack, and Fisto was quickly surrounded and outnumbered. Grievous ordered Fisto to surrender, but the Jedi managed to escape when his ship appeared, jumped into its open cockpit, and returned to Coruscant, knowing where the general's hideout was. The test highlighted Grievous' capabilities: he could be a great match for a Jedi master in hand-to-hand combat; however, it also demonstrated the weaknesses in the Jedi Order that had been evident since the Clone Wars begun. Shortly thereafter, Grievous contacted Dooku and told him that he had defeated the Jedi, but that Fisto had escaped. Dooku congratulated Grievous on his victory but stated that he could have done better and that there was still room for improvement before leaving the cyborg to ruminate on his failures. Grievous barely survived, but he knew the cost of failing the Sith again. Grievous' hatred for Dooku became stronger as he sensed treachery; it was a betrayal he was unwilling to forgive. Immediately, on the general's order, EV-A4-D was recovered and rebuilt, and continued to serve the cyborg until the conclusion of the war.{{BuildR2Cite|53|Droid Directory}} With the Republic having discovered his lair, however, Grievous was forced to abandon Vassek 3 and relocated his base of operations. In the near future, Grievous would manage to find a way to enact his revenge upon Dooku for leaking the location of his lair. Meanwhile, Fisto's victory over Grievous became a legend spread across the galaxy as a testament to the Jedi Master's skill.''[[Star Wars: The Secrets of the Jedi]]'' ====Battle of Felucia==== Later in the war, Grievous led a [[Felucia blockade|blockade]] of the planet [[Felucia]]{{EncyclopediaCite|Geonosis and Other Planets in the Outer Rim}} with at least four ''Munificent''-class frigates.{{TCW|Holocron Heist}} The Separatists and Republic struggled for control over Felucia and the neighboring [[Perlemian Trade Route|trade route]].''[[Collapse of the Republic]]'' The planet was also strategically valued because of its agricultural productivity of [[Nysillin|nysillim]], an [[plant|herb]] with healing properties. Kenobi, Skywalker, and Tano were dispatched to break the blockade and take part in the ground battle, but the [[First Battle of Felucia]], as it came to be known, devolved into a loss for the Republic, entrapping Kenobi and Skywalker's forces as B1 and [[B2-series super battle droid|B2 battle droids]], [[DSD1 dwarf spider droid|dwarf spider droids]], vulture droids, and [[Armored Assault Tank Mk I|armored assault tanks]] descended upon the Republic's position and held them at bay. Immediately to the east of their position, Ahsoka Tano refused to withdraw and launched a courageous but reckless counterattack, believing the battle droids were on the run in the nearby [[jungle]], but they were regrouping and were about to overrun her position if she kept pushing them back. The two Jedi and some AT-TEs formed a defensive circle to defend themselves against the droid forces. Jedi General Plo Koon led several LAAT/i gunships and an escorting squadron of [[V-19 Torrent starfighter]]s to evacuate the troops on Felucia. Republic cruisers were ordered to breach the Separatist planetary [[blockade]] in orbit as part of a hurried rescue operation, and rescue gunships were sent to the surface to evacuate the survivors. Plo Koon personally led the assault, clearing a route through droid starfighter defenses, and upon reaching the surface, Koon saw a dire scenario on the ground, as Kenobi and Skywalker had set up a defensive cordon around their dwindling armored forces. Through sheer numbers, the Separatists secured the strategic planet, nearly ending in disaster for the Republic forces, forcing them to withdraw from the world.
