Forced out of the Core Worlds and spreading across the galaxy, the Jedi helped their beleaguered clones in an effort to defend against Grievous's attacks in what would amount to be the war's desperate, final hours. At one point during the sieges, Grievous was aboard the bridge of a starship, observing six Providence-class Dreadnoughts [[Battle between a Republic and Separatist fleet|attack]] a Republic fleet of at least six Venator-class Star Destroyers. Grievous was rumored to be [[Mission to Frong|possibly present]] on [[Frong]], one of the many planets in the Outer Rim that were under siege, and if he were, the general should be captured, and despite the Jedi Council's lack of evidence, it's clear that the Separatists are engaging in some sort of activity, and must find out what. ====Battle of Coruscant==== {{Quote|Your lightsabers will make a fine addition to my collection.|General Grievous|}} [[File:Grievous_on_Invisible_Hand.png|thumb|left|300px|Grievous aboard the ''Invisible Hand''.]] With the Republic Military and Jedi busy with the Outer Rim Sieges raging across the galaxy's spiral arms, Coruscant was left with fewer defenses. With Republic strategists unworried, Sidious,{{Databank|palpatine-biography-gallery|Palpatine Biography Gallery}} {{C|Image 19 caption}} via Dooku, arranged for Grievous to launch a [[Battle of Coruscant|massive assault]] and carried out ground raid{{BustCollectionCite|37|Star Wars Universe}} to capture his own alter ego, [[Supreme Chancellor]] Sheev Palpatine as prisoner of war. The cyborg was charged with kidnapping the Chancellor and keeping him safe until the Jedi arrived to rescue him. Grievous, however, was entirely unaware of Palpatine's real identity. He took a dozen MagnaGuards as part of a large force to distract any Jedi during his escape. Dooku had earlier relocated his command post to Grievous's flagship, the ''Invisible Hand'', allowing him to be close to Grievous and ensure his orders were carried out, but even though a creature like the cyborg general posed no threat to the Sith Master, Sidious did not want any setbacks to his plans.{{EncyclopediaCite|Emperor Palpatine}} Grievous and his forces emerged from hyperspace with hundreds upon hundreds of C-9979 landing craft and thousands upon thousands of their Vulture droid and [[Droid tri-fighter]] escorts swept past toward the planet's surface and opened fire on the fleet of ships guarding Coruscant, wreaking destruction on the planet. The [[Coruscant Home Defense Fleet]] was caught off guard, and, with the chaos and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems Navy|Confederacy navy]] providing cover, Grievous and a strike team could land on Coruscant's surface. Within minutes, a significant number of Republic Star Destroyers protecting the [[Ecumenopolis|cityworld]] were reduced to fiery rubble, with the ''Invisible Hand'' accounting for a large percentage of the deaths. In space, Droid tri-fighters quickly decimated Republic [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter|ARC-170 fighter]] squadrons, while droid fighters flying to the battle on the surface supported the battle droids with their passes, spraying enemies on the ground with fire, immobilizing Jedi Masters Yoda and Mace Windu long enough for Grievous to act. Amidst the chaos and panic, Grievous flew down to the planet and landed in the [[Federal District|Executive District]], leading an armed team, as a shocked Republic wasn't quick enough to stop him, while Dooku stayed in orbit and commanded the aerial attack on Coruscant. Grievous then appeared, accompanied by his electrostaff-equipped MagnaGuards, and ambushed Palpatine in [[Palpatine's apartment|his apartment]]. Despite Shaak Ti and Corobb's best efforts to get Palpatine to safety, Grievous fought his way through layers of Republic security forces, including clone troopers and Jedi protectors, to secure Palpatine, eliminating everyone either by subduing or killing them, killing Jedi Master [[Roron Corobb]], whose lightsaber he claimed, during his hunt for Palpatine. During the defense, Kit Fisto attempted to defend the Chancellor from Grievous. Last but not least, he also incapacitated Ti using electrified cables, knocking her unconscious and claiming her weapon as well. He then took a single, but invaluable prisoner, the Chancellor, and carried him away{{EncyclopediaCite|Padmé Amidala}} aboard his flagship, the ''Invisible Hand'', leading him to the still-waiting Dooku in [[Conning tower|Communications tower]], where Dooku took charge of keeping Palpatine captive. Grievous was also warned by Dooku that the Jedi would stage a rescue mission. Grievous had already captured Palpatine and returned to his flagship by the time the Coruscant Home Fleet had finally established assault positions. Before Grievous could escape into hyperspace with the captured Chancellor, Republic reinforcements arrived into the battle with the ''Invisible Hand'' as their main target. While the Home Fleet moved to prevent Grievous from reaching a jump point from which the Separatist leaders could escape, thus keeping the ''Invisible Hands'' in the midst of the battle, a rescue squad under Kenobi and Skywalker, who had rushed to Coruscant from the planet [[Yerbana]] upon learning of Grievous's attack, raced to board the ''Invisible Hand'' while Commander [[Honor Salima]] of the Home Fleet rallied her vessels to stop the Separatists from escaping or disengaging. Amid the slugging match that the battle devolved into, Kenobi, Skywalker, and [[Clone Flight Squad Seven]] raced forward despite squadrons of droid fighters confronting them, resulting in many of the clone pilots being shot down. However, the two Jedi managed to board the ''Invisible Hand'' and race toward its Conning tower to save Palpatine. Upon returning to the bridge, Grievous was informed of the Jedi incursion by his Neimoidian captain [[Lushros Dofine]], but the cyborg merely laughed at how Dooku's prediction had come true. [[File:FirstDate-ROTS.png|thumb|right|300px|Much to Grievous's delight, he was met face-to-face with a captured Anakin Skywalker and his old enemy Obi-Wan Kenobi.]] Fighting past the battle droids who tried to stop them, the two Jedi, accompanied by R2-D2, made it to the [[Observation deck|observation platform]] atop the towering spire where Palpatine was being held, and upon their arrival, rather than Grievous, they were confronted by Dooku, whose presence proved to be fortunate for the Republic; the two clashed with Dooku until Skywalker bested the Separatist Head of State and killed on Palpatine's orders. His death was a major blow to the CIS. Meanwhile, the ''Invisible Hand'' was surrounded by [[Home Fleet Strike Group Five]] under [[Lieutenant Commander]] [[Lorth Needa]] and demanded the Kaleesh surrender. Needa did not believe Grievous's claims that Palpatine was a prisoner on board. Although he gave the cyborg ten minutes to prove himself before his ships opened fire, Grievous did not surrender.{{BuildFalconCite|52|Starship Fact File}} Informed by one of his OOM pilots that they had located the Jedi in [[Hallway 328]], Grievous had them trapped within a [[ray shield]] and escorted to the bridge by droids. In a moment that filled Grievous with satisfaction, Obi-Wan and Anakin were marched onto his bridge in [[Stuncuffs|electrobonds]]. The ''Invisible Hand'' began to weaken to the punishment it was receiving as Grievous captured Obi-Wan, Skywalker, and Palpatine. An [[OOM command battle droid]] handed Kenobi and [[Skywalker lightsaber|Skywalker's lightsabers]] to Grievous, who took them and weighed them in his metal claws. According to the Jedi, constructing their own lightsaber was not simply a weapon but also a piece of art that perfectly reflected its owner. A comprehensive analysis of the lightsaber could reveal much about the Jedi who made it, but there would be time for that later. Turning to face his prisoners, Grievous expanded to his full height. He enjoyed looking down on them, the terror in their eyes as they wondered what awful weapons were behind his long cloak, and the fear as they stared up at his expressionless metal face. Nonetheless, the Jedi appeared underwhelmed; Grievous would change that. Grievous and Anakin Skywalker finally meet face-to-face, both mocking one another, with Skywalker angering him in the process due to being shorter than the younger Jedi expected. He swept his [[cape]] back, revealing the lightsabers hanging in its lining, boasting that their lightsabers would make an excellent addition to his collection. [[File:Grievous-is-surrounded.png|thumb|left|250px|Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi corner Grievous who prepares to shatter the viewport before him to escape.]] Not knowing yet that Dooku was dead on the observation deck, Grievous was thrilled to have captured both his old adversary, Kenobi, and the legendary Skywalker. His gloating would end abruptly. Obi-Wan couldn't help but do the same as Anakin signaled his droid to set up their trap. As Grievous celebrated his victory and secretly delighted in having total control, he was briefly distracted by Skywalker's droid, R2-D2, for the Jedi to break free from their restraints and attack him and his guards. Activating his fire extinguishers and overloading his arc welder and electropica, R2-D2 stunned nearby droids, giving Kenobi time to retrieve his lightsaber from Anakin. He stepped away from the free Jedi, placing his bodyguards in his way. Standing back-to-back, the two Jedi deflected blaster fire from the surrounding droids. Some of his crew members had been struck by blaster shots, and he wasn't about to suffer the same fate. Thus, he let the droids exhaust the Jedi and approached one of the ship's pilots and ordered them not to deal with them and to keep the ship in orbit. The chancellor was dragged to safety by the battle droids, as the Jedi took on the task of dealing with the general's bodyguards. Obi-Wan and Anakin, now accustomed to dealing with even [[phrik]] alloy electrostaff-wielding MagnaGuards, destroyed [[IG-101]] and [[IG-102]], leaving them free to corner Grievous. The ship's [[Artificial gravity generator|gravity grids]] altered, and suddenly the ceiling was below. Most of the battle droids fell to the ceiling with the Jedi, but few of them reacted in time to stick to the floor. With that, the Jedi destroyed a handful of them. A Neimoidian pilot, in terror, announces that the ship is disaggregating. Grievous saw that staying to win this fight was pointless, therefore letting the Jedi dissolve with the ship. The [[gravity]] unexpectedly returns to normal as the Jedi fall back to the ground and sprint in the direction of the Kaleesh general. Almost all of the droids were out of order. The Supreme Chancellor was quickly saved for the second time, and Grievous was trapped on his own bridge. With his leader dead and bodyguards gone, Grievous knew the odds were against him. The Jedi clearly had the upper hand and managed to hurt the general. Reconsidering his plan, the general declared that Kenobi had lost and shattered the front window of the cruiser with an electrostaff. The cyborg was dragged into space as the compressed air inside the ship rushed into the vacuum, while Obi-Wan and Anakin fought not to follow him. Kenobi, Skywalker and the Chancellor managed to stay in the ship, but Grievous was sucked into space. Using a [[grappling hook]] built into his arm and his clawed feet to latch onto the hull of the ship, Grievous climbed back onboard the ship to reach the escape pods. As he moved along the smooth metal, he remarked to himself how easy it was to have a droid body. [[File:Grievous_escape_pod.png|thumb|right|250px|With his ship lost, Grievous was forced to escape to save his life, using one of the escape pods.]] Leaving everyone on board, the Separatist commander launched all of the escape pods, took off in one, and rapidly moved away from the remnant of his flagship. Grievous usually finds himself an escape route, but as the Battle of Coruscant took place, he was alone without the ''Soulless One''. He would have lost it along with his flagship, the ''Invisible Hand'', if this had happened. By that time, the starfighter had been on a small landing platform on Utapau for several months. Anakin and Obi-Wan discovered that he had survived by doubling back by this. The Trade Federation shuttles were close enough to pick him up, and the clone fighters were too preoccupied with battling his droids to pay him any attention. Grievous's escape pod was recovered by the [[Lucrehulk-class battleship|''Lucrehulk-class Battleship'']] ''[[Profusion]]'', and rejoined his fleet. With Palpatine out of his grasp, Grievous ordered his forces to flee and led the two-thirds of his armada capable of fleeing into hyperspace. ====Retreat to Utapau==== {{Quote|The end of the war is near, general.''"
"''But the loss of Count Dooku?''"
"''His death was a necessary loss. Soon I will have a new apprentice, one far younger and more powerful.|Sidious and Grievous|}} With a full third of the Separatist fleet used in the battle over Coruscant having suffered major damages, much of the navy was decimated and could not follow Grievous to safety. In the aftermath, Republic military officers analyzed the battle's footage in an attempt to identify the Separatist strategy and the reason they had remained in the system for so long after capturing Palpatine. Unaware that Dooku's escape was never his intention; Palpatine used the battle entirely as bait to bring Anakin Skywalker back to Coruscant, eliminate Dooku, and prepare the Republic for its dying days. Following Dooku's unexpected death,{{Topps|set=2017 Topps Journey to Star Wars: The Last Jedi|cardname=Confronting General Grievous}} which struck a major blow to the Separatist cause and the Separatists' hopes, Grievous succeeded him as [[Head of State]], turning the Supreme Commander into the leader of the entire Separatist Alliance. While Grievous had always been in command of the droid army,''[[Skywalker: A Family at War]]'' his promotion left him with complete control over Separatist forces as both the military and political head. Despite the usefulness of such a promotion, Grievous remained subservient to Sidious, whom he continued to loyally serve. After the Jedi Knights foiled his plan to kidnap Chancellor Palpatine, Grievous fled to the Outer Rim and ordered a brutal, but clearly desperate, counterattack across several star systems, including Kaller,{{TBB|Aftermath (episode)}} even though the CIS had largely been forced on the defensive as the Outer Rim Sieges continued. Despite being used in his counterattack, the legions of battle droids Grievous could command were severely depleted, whereas the Republic was securing more and more victories across the galaxy. Grievous, ever the faithful servant to Sidious, was now ordered to return to Utapau in the Outer Rim and safeguard the security the increasingly irrelevant Separatist Council. In reality, Sidious had other plans for Grievous, who failed to realize he was being tricked again. The cyborg had one role left to play in the Sith Lord's schemes: to act as bait to draw Kenobi away from Coruscant and Anakin Skywalker. With his Grand Plan to bring down the Republic and Jedi Order in motion, Darth Sidious did not care if Grievous or Kenobi lived or died. [[File:Grievous-speaks-to-Sidious.png|thumb|left|254px|Grievous was assured by Darth Sidious that the war was coming to an end and that the Separatists would be victorious.]] Grievous particularly disliked Utapau, a planet where he had been humiliated by Kenobi and Skywalker during the kyber crystal endeavor, and regarded its people as wretched worms.''[[Revenge of the Sith - The Film Novel]]'' All the same, Grievous had returned to the planet aboard his personal{{BuildFalconCite|54|Starship Fact File}} [[Unidentified Sheathipede-class transport shuttle (Grievous)|''Sheathipede''-class transport shuttle]] for his meeting with the Separatist Council in some force, deriving some satisfaction from taking the Pau'un leaders hostage and beginning to transform their capital into a droid factory. Grievous seized control of a sizeable portion of the city, holding its population hostage under the threat of destruction if they revealed his presence there. When Grievous arrived, his droids informed him that the planet is under his command. Uninterested and instead focusing on his mission to speak to the Separatist Council, the cyborg did not have to wait long for Sidious to reach out to him.{{StoryCite|story=The Cyborg and the Jedi|book=The Prequel Trilogy Stories}} One of his MagnaGuards informed him that someone was trying to contact him. Grievous hurriedly bowed to the hologram of the hooded figure who had appeared. Under the direct order of Sidious, Grievous was to relocate the Council to the [[Volcano|volcanic]] planet [[Mustafar]], with Sidious further promising Grievous that the end of the war was near. Wondering if Sidious, despite his greatness, realized what the useless raid on Coruscant had cost their cause, the general asked Sidious if Dooku's death impacted the coming end, but Sidious seemed unconcerned, reassuring Grievous that his death was a necessary loss and that he would soon have a new, younger and more powerful apprentice. Sidious also told him to remain on Utapau until the new apprentice had joined their cause since he didn't want to waste any time before finding a replacement. However, after the end of the communication, he remained immersed in his thoughts for some minutes. Had Grievous knew Sidious's plans, he would have an easier time sharing his confidence. Unaware of his superior's true plans,{{BustCollectionCite|68|Star Wars Universe}} Grievous remained uncertain about his new role and waited for further orders. After years of seemingly unstoppable terror, the general's murderous streak were finally set to end when Sidious revealed his whereabouts to the Jedi, intending to close a loose end. Unaware of his master's treachery, Grievous had no idea that Sidious had secretly informed the Republic of his location and allowed Republic intelligence to track him down. ====Final duel with Kenobi==== {{Quote|Army or not, you must realize you are doomed.''"
"''Oh I don't think so…|Grievous and Obi-Wan Kenobi|audio=ArmyOrNot-ROTS.flac|}} [[File:Speaks-to-the-council.png|thumb|right|275px|Grievous addresses the Separatist Council on Utapau.]] In light of Dooku's recent demise and the Republic's other significant victories, the task of capturing or killing Grievous had a new sense of urgency. Although such a mission had been attempted before, the end of Grievous looked like it could be the key to crippling the CIS military and finally end the war. With the General hiding in the Outer Rim, the Jedi Council scoured the Republic's systems but found no sign of Grievous. Despite having few ships available, they recommended expanding the search to the outlying systems. In the days after the Battle of Coruscant, the Republic received word that Grievous was hiding on Utapau, with Sidious, under his alter-ego of Chancellor Palpatine, claiming to Skywalker that Clone Intelligence located the general. With the war coming to its close, Sidious no longer needed Grievous as his pawn as the cyborg had played his role: all of Grievous's campaigns had served to distract the Jedi Order from learning of the Sith conspiracy unfolding around them on Coruscant. Furthermore, the general had spread fear across the Republic and been featured as a figure of evil in Republic propaganda.''[[Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy]]'' The fear and death spread across the galaxy during the war helped ensure Palpatine's [[Galactic Empire]] would be welcomed by the population.''[[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]'' Although Palpatine advised the Jedi Council to send Skywalker to challenge Grievous, they felt a Jedi Master with more experience was needed to finally defeat the cyborg warrior, with the Council also judging Skywalker as little more than Palpatine's puppet, so Kenobi was sent to [[Battle of Utapau|confront him]]. After Obi-Wan had discussed his plan with Cody and other members of the 212th combat personnel, they both recognized that finding Grievous on Utapau was a great chance to deal a major, if not fatal, blow to the Separatist Army.{{EncyclopediaCite|The Grand Army of the Republic}} Promising to notify Cody as soon as he learned of Grievous's presence, Kenobi arrived on Utapau, where he was immediately met by Tion Medon, a senior member of the Utapaun government who was under significant pressure despite his preternaturally calm demeanor; while a core ship was not an unusual sight, even as far out as Utapau, Medon whispered that Grievous was present and holding the populace hostage with numerous battle droids, further declaring that Grievous was a force to be reckoned with.''[[Force Collector]]'' Kenobi's arrival was watched by a MagnaGuard and two B1 battle droids, but Kenobi sent his starfighter away under [[R4-G9]]'s control to trick the Separatists into thinking he had departed. Meanwhile on Level 10, Grievous found himself at the back of a room, watching the Separatist Council members with disgust. Unknowingly watched by Kenobi, Grievous directed the Council to safety on Mustafar with a little annoyance and rebuffed Gunray, whom he threatened when the Viceroy openly doubted his ability to keep them safe. With the Council departing and having earned a degree of satisfaction from demonstrating Gunray's weakness, Grievous waited for his insufferable Jedi enemy to arrive, hoping he would not have to wait long, while speaking to a B1 battle droid. Suddenly, however, Kenobi revealed himself by simply jumping into the middle of the room and greeting the general. With his MagnaGuards and other battle droids around him, Grievous exuded a gloating sense of confidence. Applauding Kenobi's audacity, Grievous ordered his bodyguards to kill the Jedi Master, who instead handily defeated all four MagnaGuards. Grievous's droid army then moved to fire on Kenobi but were called off by the general, who decided to engage Kenobi himself to wash away the shame of their previous confrontation and prove his value to Sidious. Grievous thought he was the better fighter, but his presumption would prove wrong. [[File:Kenobi_faces_Grievous_ROTS.png|thumb|left|264px|On Utapau, Grievous faces Obi-Wan Kenobi, his great adversary, for the last time.]] Unknowingly, however, Grievous had played directly into Kenobi's hands as the Jedi General waited for Cody and the 212th to arrive. Due to their many prior clashes, Kenobi was well prepared for the duel and determined to prevent him from escaping in a fight that was clearly not going to be easy. Given permission by Kenobi to make the first move, Grievous unveiled four lightsabers—all of which were obtained from previously defeated Jedi—and laughed. Kenobi refused to let Grievous do the same with his lightsaber,{{StoryCite|story=The Duel for Peace|book=5-Minute Star Wars Stories Strike Back}} and thus began a duel along a walkway suspended above the [[hangar 10]]'s lower levels. Grievous stomped forward, spinning two of the lightsabers above his head, utilizing a spectacular combat maneuver to produce a lethal [[circular saw|laser-saw]] effect, and scorching the floor beneath him. At the same time, he dragged the remaining two along the ground, sending sparks hurtling toward Obi-Wan. Delighting in the chance to engage Kenobi in what both intended to be their final battle, he stalked closer and closer, his weapons becoming a blur of light. Initially, Obi-Wan took a slow step backward, but he overcame his fear and allowed the Force to guide him.[[Revenge of the Sith Read-Along Storybook and CD|''Revenge of the Sith'' Read-Along Storybook and CD]] Waiting for the right moment, he thrust his lightsaber between Grievous's flashing blades and met the cyborg's assault with determination. Though the Jedi deflected the blow, he knew he would not be able to keep up that pace for long and switched tactics. Kenobi leaped, flipping over Grievous as the cyborg's other two lightsabers stabbed at the spot where he had been standing. The Jedi landed behind him. Grievous spun to face the opposite direction and attacked again. Taking advantage of the general's brief moment of surprise, Kenobi slipped past his defense, repeatedly blocking and ducking Grievous's violent strikes. Kenobi limited Grievous to moving along the catwalk, neutralizing Grievous's usual, more wide-ranging fighting style. After so many encounters, Kenobi was accustomed to Grievous's movements and tricks and maintained the fight close to the cyborg, drawing on his experience from their prior duels. However, Kenobi kept his composure and carefully targeted Grievous's vulnerable wrists''[[Star Wars Use the Force!]]'' and, before long, sliced off a clawed mechanical hand, clattering down onto the deck, along with the lightsaber of none other than Shaak Ti, one of his primary four through the duel it had once held.{{Topps|set=2020 Topps Star Wars Holocron Series|subset=Lightsabers of the Jedi|cardname=Shaak Ti}} Grievous backed away, staring in surprise at his smoking stump. Furious and losing his focus, Grievous launched a wild attack, advancing with his spinning weapon at his opponent, but Obi-Wan continually deflected it. In a matter of seconds, the laughter died in his artificial throat{{EncyclopediaCite|Obi-Wan Kenobi}} as yet another hand severed and fell to the deck, releasing the lightsaber it had formerly wielded. Almost immediately, he lost both of his weapons and hands. With that, the fight became more even. The situation for the cyborg began to fall apart. [[File:Obi-WanclasheswithGrievous.png|thumb|right|264px|During their duel, despite having four lightsabers, Grievous quickly loses two hands to Kenobi's blade.]] Grievous was driven back further and further by Obi-Wan, who maintained the lead as the surrounding droids watched as their leader lost ground. But before the droids could assist Grievous in fighting back, there was a stalemate for a time, and just on cue, the 212 Battalion ambushed the Separatists, filling the air with a hail of blaster bolts. Swarms of LAAT/I gunships floated down into the [[sinkhole]], and clone troopers rappelled down from the gantries overhead. Fighting broke out all over Pau City between droid and clone forces, who were furthered backed by the local [[Utapaun Security Forces|Utapaun resistance]]. The Separatist droid forces were thrown into such disarray by the 212's unexpected and furious onslaught that they barely had time to organize an effective defense of their positions in Pau City. While the troopers engaged the battle droids, Obi-Wan was disappointed if he had any hope for Grievous to surrender; instead, despite the chaos around him, the general continued the duel, gloating that, army or not, Kenobi was doomed. Undaunted, before his opponent could adapt, Kenobi blasted the general with a tremendous Force push, propelling him up forcefully in the air to crash into a hanging cargo module from the ceiling. The impact knocked the lightsabers out of his hands, while Grievous slipped past the floor's edge and tumbled to the lowest level. Stunned and completely disarmed, the cyborg landed hard but survived, crouched like a [[spider]]. Defeated and realizing that the odds were turning against him, Grievous saw an opportunity to adopt his usual tactic of fleeing a battle that had turned against him and was certain that the chaos of battle would make it easier for him to flee. He went directly for his waiting wheel bike, scuttling away on six legs as Obi-Wan hurried down to the site where Grievous had fallen, arriving just in time to see his opponent shot away at the controls of his wheel bike. While he failed to crush Obi-Wan, who had barely made the leap to the lower level, he unleashed havoc on any clone troopers in his path. Kenobi was well aware that Grievous thought he could flee while his droids stalled him, but he chased after the fleeing cyborg relentlessly throughout the hanger. Pushing one trooper aside with his bike's legs, then grabbing two more clones and throwing them into a sinkhole as he sped past, and landing on the outer hull of the Core Ship that served as the Separatist base, the general's bike handled the shift in terrain in stride. Soon after, the Varactyl-mounted Kenobi trailed closely behind Grievous on the skin of the core ship, struggling without the [[magnet]]ic adhesion Grievous's wheel bike possessed. Kenobi even lost his lightsaber in the chaos. Commander Cody interrupted the Jedi Council's meeting in the [[Temple's war room|war room]] of the Jedi Temple on Coruscant and informed them that General Kenobi had tracked down and engaged Grievous and that the battle had begun on Utapau. Mace Windu then had Anakin Skywalker deliver the information to the Chancellor, as his reaction might give them a hint about his plans. Ki-Adi Mundi, Yoda, and Windu considered a potential possible plan of action to remove the Chancellor if, with the destruction of Grievous, he refused to relinquish his emergency powers; Mundi advised that to ensure a secure transition of power, the Jedi Order would need to seize control of the Senate in the meantime. Meanwhile, [[Tech]], a [[Clone commando|Clone Commando]] and member of [[Clone Force 99]], better known as "the Bad Batch," informed Depa Billaba that, according to Clone Intelligence, Obi-Wan Kenobi had located and confronted General Grievous on Utapau. [[Clone Corporal]] [[Echo]] added that if Obi-Wan succeeded in killing or capturing Grievous, the Separatist leadership would collapse, and the droid army would soon follow. Although Billaba found the theory compelling, she pointed out that they had no control over events unfolding on Utapau. Remaining behind, she allowed her Padawan, Caleb Dume, to accompany the '[[Genetically defective clone|defective]]' clone commandos [[Battle of Kaller|into battle]]. ====Death==== {{Listen|filename=GrievousDeath.flac|title=The Death of General Grievous|description=Listen to Grievous's death cry}} [[File:KenobipursuesGrievousonUtapau.png|thumb|left|255px|While Grievous attempted to flee on a wheel bike, Kenobi mounted a Varactyl to pursue the cyborg in a dangerous chase amid Pau City's windmills and chasms.]] Pursued by Kenobi on a varactyl named [[Boga]], Grievous attempted to flee to ''Soulless One'' on its small landing platform a distance from the main Separatist base. Surrounded by blaster fire and explosions, Grievous rushed as if the road was clear, avoiding collisions or crushing anyone in his path. Obi-Wan reaches for his lightsaber to fight off a shot but discovers it missing and realizes that it must have fallen. While the prospect of fighting the cyborg without his lightsaber was certainly unsettling, Kenobi knew that defeating him may signal the end of the Clone Wars and did not stop to retrieve it so as to risk missing his opportunity to capture him. Through increasingly packed tunnels, however, Grievous was forced to slow down to avoid a swarm of droids, whereas Kenobi's mount, able to achieve feats the general's wheel bike could not, moved to the tunnel's ceiling to avoid traffic congestion. Kenobi thus gained ground on Grievous in the chase for the landing platform, accelerating once more and catching up to the general. Obi-Wan had just caught up with the general when the Separatist leader, able to control his bike and battle, grabbed an electrostaff from its mount and began attacking Kenobi, attempting to shove him back. Obi-Wan managed to seize it, throwing Grievous off balance, while delivering a few jabs of his own. However, he grabbed the weapon and pulled both it and Kenobi over to him. Boga dropped back, remaining in pursuit, as the Jedi and the Separatist fought on the bike. The two opponents fought for the upper hand as the wheel bike careened through narrow canyons and over sharp turns. With the staff being wrestled for, Grievous drew his custom [[blaster pistol]], the [[Grievance Striker|Grievance striker]]. Obi-Wan dodged, but Grievous lost control of the bike during the struggle, flipping the two combatants off before the bike flew off into one of Utapau's many sinkhole abysses and exploded upon impact with the ground far below. Having arrived at the landing platform, both opponents recovered quickly, with Grievous raising the blaster as Obi-Wan snatched the electrostaff. Kenobi once again disarmed Grievous and knocked away his blaster out of his hand, while landing a few blows on the general himself, bending, but not breaking, the cyborg's metal. Grievous was knocked to the ground, and Obi-Wan plunged the shaft into his abdomen, but the cyborg kicked Kenobi clear, sending him and the staff flying with such speed that the Jedi could not stop it. With no weapons, the two engaged in a hand-to-hand combat that Grievous was coldly confident of winning. Grievous approached Kenobi, swung his arm, missed, but quickly backhanded him across the platform, bouncing off the ''Soulless One'', putting Obi-Wan at a physical disadvantage. Grievous's superior, formidable physical strength appeared to give him the advantage in beating down Kenobi. Grievous continued his assault, lifting up the Jedi and striking again, barely missing Obi-Wan's head with a terrifyingly powerful punch that heavily dented the starfighter. However, Kenobi dodged his actions and noticed that one of Grievous's plates was loose and took advantage of that, just before he appeared to be losing the fight, and moved in and grabbed the open, loose corner plates and pulled with all his strength, managing to rip open Grievous's chest plates to see his gut-sack. The plate came loose, and alarmed, the cyborg closed around Obi-Wan and hurled him away to the platform. Wounded but far from defeated, Grievous moved on Obi-Wan, chuckling, and attempted to crush him with his mechanical feet, whereas Kenobi attempted to knock down Grievous with a Force-enhanced kick to the leg. However, Kenobi's kick only succeeded in hurting himself. [[File:GrievousFlameOut-ROTS.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Grievous was killed with his own blaster turned against him by Kenobi repeatedly firing into his exposed gut-sack, finally destroying the cyborg once and all.]] Grievous laughed even louder, hurling Kenobi directly off the landing platform, and proceeded to gloat, but just in time, the half-stunned Jedi manipulated his position via the Force and caught hold of the edge. Grievous stalked to where Kenobi was still dangling, barely holding on and fighting to push himself back up to safety, with his legs hanging in the emptiness, above the city's seemingly-bottomless well. Confident that his greatest adversary would perish, Grievous charged Kenobi with an electrostaff to finish him off, only for Kenobi to summon to himself Grievous's own blaster—abandoned a few meters from him and forgotten by its owner,—with the Force. In defense of his own life, Kenobi took a careful aim and shot Grievous five times in his exposed gut-sack through the gaps in his chest armor, igniting the fluid that was keeping his organs alive. Grievous's remaining biological components ignited, spectacularly incinerating the famed cyborg from the inside. Screaming in pain, Grievous let out a sound halfway between a choke and a metal rustle before a succession of explosions and flames tore apart his body, as the living matter exploded, blasting out his eye sockets. With that, Grievous was dead. His few remaining organic remains proved to be his downfall, devoured by the fierce flames that finally consumed him. He collapsed as his blackened metal body crashed onto the hangar floor with a resounding clang, leaving behind nothing more than an empty shell, no longer animated by life,{{Topps|set=2021 Topps Star Wars Chrome Legacy|subset=Wielders of Lightsabers|cardname=General Grievous}} hatred, or the desire to destroy. Grievous's bloodthirsty rampage came to an end, as the cyborg paid the price for his arrogance in believing he could dominate the Jedi. After so many attempts over the previous years, the menace of the cyborg commander had finally come to an end at the hands of Kenobi,{{HelmetCollectionCite|35|Helmets}} in a fitting, if tragic, manner for a miserable creature whose obsessive pursuit of physical strength and combat skill had rendered him completely unrecognizable to anyone who had ever seen his natural face. Indeed, all that remained of Grievous was the lifeless shell that was his cyborg remains; the so-called improvements he had sacrificed so much of himself to have were left abandoned by Kenobi, who walked to the empty shell and threw down the blaster in disgust, as he considered blasters very uncivilized implements. Kenobi spared his rival one more look and breathed a sigh of relief before returning to the battle atop his awaiting varactyl. [[File:Dead_General.png|thumb|left|250px|After many years of carnage, the threat of Grievous had ended, the Confederacy had lost its importance, and the Clone Wars were over.]] Grievous had been the primary issue for Obi-Wan, and having been dealt with, Kenobi was left simply to alert the Council and the Chancellor, and then finally find out the Chancellor's true objectives. The news that Grievous was dead made it seem like victory was inevitable for the Republic forces, who, supported by the loyal Pau'an militias, were gaining momentum.{{HelmetCollectionCite|25|Highlights of the Saga}} (Spanish version) Still, Kenobi did not have time to elaborate and instead encouraged the clones to launch an offensive against the now-leaderless droids. With Grievous killed by Obi-Wan Kenobi, the beleaguered droids were further stunned, but continued to fight the clones, who were commanded to take control of the planet.{{BustCollectionCite|17|Star Wars Universe}} Without a clear front to fight on and disarray in the line of command, the droids were reduced to small pockets of resistance that were quickly overwhelmed. The battle was moving in their favor, and, with Grievous dead, the war that had claimed countless lives seemed to be coming to a conclusion; the end of the war appeared to be in sight, but the Jedi did not suspect that it would also be the beginning of the end. The Battle of Utapau was one of the last battles of the Clone Wars and was in its last stages. Across the battlefields, Jedi Generals felt victory. Meanwhile on Mustafar, the Separatist Council cowered, not realizing they had one more fatal part to play in the Sith plan. After Palpatine revealed his true identity as Darth Sidious to Anakin, the Jedi Council received word of Grievous's death. Even as Kenobi ended Grievou's reign of terror on Utapau, Anakin approached Mace Windu with the disturbing news that the Chancellor was the Sith Lord they had been searching for. As news of Grievous's demise spread, Mace Windu selected three of the Order's finest warriors{{HelmetCollectionCite|15|Highlights of the Saga}}—[[Agen Kolar]], Kit Fisto, and [[Saesee Tiin]]—and accompanied them to the Chancellor's private office to confront him and place him under arrest. Palpatine acknowledged that the Clone Wars had ended with Grievous's destruction, but he was surprised that the Jedi had [[Duel in Palpatine's office|arrived]] sooner than expected, forcing him to appear as though he might peacefully surrender and relinquish the Senate's emergency powers. Grievous's defeat resulted in the collapse of any functional command structure for the Separatist military, and the battle's outcome spread throughout the galaxy, thereby ending the war even while numerous other fronts were still active. ===Legacy=== ====A future with no Jedi==== {{Quote|But then came the slaughter of our forces on Hypori and the deaths of more Jedi… At the hands of the brutal warlord known as General Grievous.|Obi-Wan Kenobi writes about Grievous after the destruction of the Order|}} Unfortunately for Grievous, his wish to see a galaxy devoid of the Jedi Order was all but fulfilled, but only after his death; a short time after Grievous's demise, Sidious, using his alter ego of Chancellor Palpatine, ordered the clone troopers across the galaxy to [[Great Jedi Purge|execute]] [[Order 66]], turning the soldiers against their own generals. Escaping from his clone troopers, Kenobi survived and cautiously returned to the site of his final battle with Grievous. There, beside the smoking remains of his former foe, Grievous's personal starfighter, the ''Soulless One'', awaited him. Obi-Wan fled Utapau aboard the ''Soulless One'', running past the remains of his cyborg rival one final time without even sparing Grievous a passing glance. Heading for space as quickly as possible, he relied on the element of surprise to slip past his old flagship. Even if the Trade Federation cruisers in orbit spotted him, they would likely assume he was a Separatist fleeing the battle. Using the starfighter's powerful communications equipment, Kenobi broadcast a distress call and managed to contact Senator [[Bail Prestor Organa|Bail Organa]] of [[Alderaan]]. The Jedi Master later met with Bail Organa and Yoda aboard the [[CR-series|Alderaanian diplomatic cruiser]]{{SWE|technology|alderaancruiser|Alderaan cruiser}} ''[[Tantive III]]'', where Grievous's starfighter remained docked in the hangar. At that point, the ''Soulless One'' was briefly in Bail Organa's possession.{{InsiderCite|231|Win, Lose, or Draw}} As planned, the clones turned on their Jedi Generals, seemingly reading the war to end in total victory for the Separatists. Gunray succeeded Grievous as Confederate Head of State and commander of the droid army, believing that, with both Separatist leaders dead, the war was in his favor and more power would be his.{{ShipsandVehiclesCite|33|Starships and Vehicles}} [[File:Dark_Scheme_SWDLegacies.png|thumb|right|250px|With his real identity a secret, Darth Vader was rumored to be a counterpart to Grievous.]] In truth, however, Sidious no longer had any use for the Confederacy and dispatched his new apprentice Darth Vader, the very pupil he had told Grievous of, [[Mission to Mustafar|to wipe out]] the Separatist Council; Vader was none other than Anakin Skywalker, whom Sidious had managed to turn to the [[dark side of the Force]]. After once all of the council members had been disposed of, all remaining droid units of the Separatist Droid Army were ordered to shut down. With the Jedi all but destroyed, Sidious was able to step up and claim credit for defeating the Separatist. Placing the galaxy under Sith control for the first time in one thousand years, Sidious [[Proclamation of the New Order|transformed]] the Republic into the First Galactic Empire. After his [[duel on Mustafar|deadly duel]] with his former friend and mentor, Obi-Wan Kenobi, on Mustafar, Vader survived, defeated, disfigured, severely burned, and horribly scarred.''[[Star Wars: Book of Lists]]'' He underwent extensive reconstructive surgery performed by various droids, including FX-6, the same droid that had worked on Grievous's armor. He was then encased in [[Darth Vader's armor|black armor]] equipped with various mechanical limbs and [[life support]] systems. [[File:Tony-foti-starwars-forcecollector-fullwrap-art.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Karr Nuq Sin, a Force-sensitive travels the galaxy in search of knowledge about the Force.]] During the later New Republic Era, self-described Jedi history buff [[Karr Nuq Sin]] learned about Grievous's demise on Utapau in the [[Unidentified school (Merokia)|school]] he attended on the desert planet [[Merokia]], remembering the general's death as the effective end to the war.
