Both were displayed in his [[Batuuan]] store, [[Dok-Ondar's Den of Antiquities]], in [[Black Spire Outpost]] on the planet [[Batuu]]. Half [[Standard century|century]] after the Kaleesh warlord gained galactic infamy for his role leading the Separatist droid army, Grievous was referenced in several works also stemming from Batuu, including a toy of the cyborg general that was sold at [[Black Spire Outpost]].[[Galaxy's Edge 2|''Galaxy's Edge'' 2]] The B1-series battle droid and [[author]] [[R0-GR]] included mentions of Grievous in his ''[[Droidography]]'', describing IG-100 Magnaguards' capacity as bodyguards for the Separatist general. Grievous was also mentioned alongside Darth Vader as a cyborg who blurred distinctions between organics and true droids; R0-GR noted that thanks to them, being a droid was finally back in style. The work was published sometime after the Battle of [[Oetchi system|Oetchi]].''[[Star Wars: Droidography]]'' After the [[Battle of Crait]]''[[Star Wars: The Galactic Explorer's Guide]]'' in 34 ABY, Grievous's old enemy Hondo Ohnaka featured Coruscant in his book ''[[Galactic Explorer's Guide]]'' and, due to his role in the Battle of Coruscant, included Grievous in the "Rogue's Gallery" section for the planet. [[Resistance]] [[historian]] [[Beaumont Kin]] referenced Grievous' pre-arranged kidnapping of Darth Sidious whilst under his Senator Palaptine persona during the Battle of Coruscant in the academic work [[The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]], published sometime after the [[Battle of Exegol]].''[[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]'' ==Personality and traits== ===Physical appearance=== {{Quote|Although an accident left him almost fully cybernetic, he still bore the trademark snakelike yellow eyes with slit pupils, flat nose, and elongated ears of his species.|Excerpt from an artist's journal|}} [[File:Aggressive_Tactics_CWCS.png|thumb|right|250px|Grievous was a brilliant and unforgiving strategist who led the army of the Separatist Alliance against the Republic in the Clone Wars.]] A Kaleesh warlord who stood at 2.16 [[meter]]s (7 [[Foot|feet]], 1 inch) in height, Grievous, born as Qymaen jai Sheelal, possessed red colored skin and slit-pupilled golden eyes, as well as an elongated facial structure with slitted nostrils alongside a series of four spiky growths which protruded from his chin. Often donned with a Kaleesh mask sculpted from the skull of a Mumuu, a hostile predator native to his homeworld of Kalee, Grievous wore the mask throughout the duration of his people's war with the Huk. With a desire to become the leader of the largest and greatest military force within the entire galaxy, as well as possess the capability to combat Jedi, whom he had perceived as nearly invincible as a result of their powerful connection to the Force, the Kaleesh also aspired to become a great warrior and gained the reputation of an infamous warlord who developed vast numbers of enemies. When transformed into a reconstructed cybernetic warrior following his decision to embark on such a path and a gruesome shuttle crash, Grievous's brain was altered by Separatist engineers without conscience by the Kaleesh, which resulted in an increase in intelligence, agility and strength, as well as a deep and violent disposition for the Jedi following the false revelation by Count Dooku that the Jedi were responsible for his condition. Portions of Grievous's organic form that survived included his his beady eyes and his cold heart. Although cybernetic implants had been added to enhance, sharpen, and protect his vision from the vacuum of space, his eyes remained his own, with sufficient skull left behind them to anchor the organic muscles and tendons required for them to function as before. With his cybernetic transformation, Grievous exuded a malicious countenance{{InsiderCite|231|Launchpad}} and towered over most species, further enhancing his intimidating presence. His body was composed of metal plates resembling armor, welded together with little to no space for flesh. Grievous appeared as a hunched mechanical skeleton, complete with a skull-like head. He received claw-like feet, a set of arms, which were capable of separating themselves into an additional set, and a skull-like mask, specifically sculpted for his new body, from which his eyes peered, horrifically alive beneath his inert steel mask, malevolently staring down opponents. Furthermore, located behind a set of duranium teeth crafted to mimic those of the karabbac beast from his homeworld, Grievous's hoarse voice was emitted from an ultrasonic vocabulator. Grievous's magnetized talons were made of durasteel. ===General of the Confederacy=== {{Quote|Listen to me, Jedi. I do not care about your politics. I do not care about your Republic. I only live to see you die!|General Grievous's message to the Jedi Order|}} Alongside a hatred for political matters, Grievous had developed an understanding that his involvement in the Clone Wars was an opportunity to eliminate the Jedi Order and command the Separatist Droid Army, as opposed to serving Dooku's political ambitions. Grievous believed that the Jedi had simply chosen the incorrect side in their beliefs. However, as a result of his preeminent desire to eradicate the Jedi, one Confederacy member, General Kleeve, considered Grievous's personal goals as a distraction that influenced his military decisions. Grievous often reacted angrily to criticism and also lacked a terrific sense of humor. Grievous viewed leadership as a serious responsibility that leaves little room for personal enjoyment. He was quite proud of his position within the Separatist organizations and told others to refer to him as "general". He was also referred to as "My [[lord]]" by members of the Confederacy military, such as Asajj Ventress and TV-94. [[File:ChokedCloneTrooper-BFR.png|thumb|left|250px|Grievous was a ruthless adversary who killed the strong and the helpless alike.]] Grievous was known for his cruelty and ruthlessness and was seen as the Separatists' best general. Given his reputation, Grievous was feared throughout the galaxy as a strategic genius and for his hunting prowess.{{SW|url=news/sdcc-2019-marvels-the-rise-of-kylo-ren-revealed-and-more-highlights-from-the-lucasfilm-publishing-panel|text=SDCC 2019: Marvel's ''The Rise of Kylo Ren'' Revealed and More Highlights from the Lucasfilm Publishing Panel}} Following Dooku, Grievous was viewed by the Republic as the second-greatest threat in the war. The Republic described Grievous as a mechanical monstrosity, a portrayal that played on deep-seated anxieties about droids. No one terrorized Republic soldiers more than Grievous, the fearsome combatant of the Clone Wars, both a strategic mastermind and a nightmare on the battlefield. Grievous was a symbol of terror across the galaxy, whether sending his armies against entire worlds or facing opponents in close-quarters, lethal combat. According to legend, even the Jedi shivered at his name and feared facing him in battle, since no one could match his sheer relentlessness and determination. Although individual members of the Order reacted to him differently, some regarded him with caution or hatred, whereas others, such as Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi, displayed considerable confidence when confronting him. Iskat Akaris, meanwhile, was unusually fascinated by the prospect of fighting him. The brutal strategy he learned as a warlord required the Jedi to command clone troopers, which are made through technological advances. Many of the Jedi Council recognized the dangers to the Order, but they were pressured by the next incursion or the next loss of a world to the cyborg Separatist Leader. Another detail outlined in the legend of the Battle of Alamass was that Separatist leaders believed Grievous could be relied upon to complete critical missions, for his record was nearly unblemished, and he was highly regarded for his tactical insight, which had provided the Separatists with numerous victories. While Dooku dealt with matters of state, including military operations for the Confederacy of Independent Systems, Grievous oversaw the logistics and tactics of its vast droid armies, which were managed by Dooku's operatives, and handled the war's day-to-day operations. The general commanded a large number of capable admirals and generals recruited from across the Galaxy. Grievous, Trench, and their fellow commanders were placed in charge of broader campaign objectives, whereas Asajj Ventress employed stealth, bribery, robbery, and targeted killing to achieve her more specific goals. Grievous's campaigns against the Galactic Republic threatened the very existence of the Jedi Order. He could exert better control over his forces thanks to the droid commanders, who eliminated unauthorized thoughts and suggestions from underlings through their own strategic judgment. Only a few brilliant sentients, such as Trench, managed to retain command of offensive operations. In contrast, local forces, which were frequently organic, were primarily responsible for defensive actions, allowing them to protect and strengthen their homeworlds and hyperspace passages while leaving Grievous free to concentrate on assaults against the Republic. The Kaleesh cyborg became notorious for hunting Jedi, often using calculated boarding operations against Republic capital ships. One such attack targeted the ''Steadfast'', Jedi General Eeth Koth's flagship, where Grievous led an assault force that included BX commando droids and IG-100 MagnaGuards, intending to overwhelm the Jedi and his clones. After Koth was captured and used to mock the Jedi Council, Grievous became such a threat that the Council dispatched three of its best Jedi to release Koth and try to apprehend Grievous with the help of clones. ===Cyborg tyrant=== {{Quote|Those of you who can still stand— Return to your master…''and tell him to send more men!''|Grievous, upon slaughtering several Mandalorian warriors|}} [[File:GrievousRevealsHimselfMygeeto-Kanan10.png|thumb|right|250px|A cyborg warrior who did not need the Force to confront Jedi, Grievous struck fear in the hearts of those who supported the Republic.]] Cold, calculating, vain,{{Databank|general-grievous-speeder|General Grievous' Speeder}} deceitful, and unconcerned with the rules of combat outlined by the Galactic Accord of Systems, Grievous' cruelty was not limited to the field of battle: civilians and other non-combatants suffered at his hands. Well aware of the Jedi's soft spot for innocents and personally unconcerned about civilian casualties, Grievous devastated the populations of entire worlds and created a tactic out of exploiting the compassion of his foes, targeting civilians so as to force his opponents into changing priorities. Whereas his enemies would need to shift to the protection of innocents in his crosshairs, his troops were free to focus on victory at any cost. Beyond exploiting the Jedi compassion for civilians, he also noticed and exploited their compassion for the clone troopers under their command. Grievous had sown death and misty throughout thousands of star systems that had been defenseless against his ruthless tactics. The arrest for Grievous had swiftly became a top priority for the Jedi High Council. Every time his capture appeared certain, he had avoided the Republic forces at the last minute, leaving his army to be decimated. Grievous enjoyed a good conquest and could often be found laughing throughout combat, finding joy in conflict, his victories, and even murder. When Grievous became a cyborg general at the head of the Separatists' droid army, his ability to teach and lead his troops with exceptional skill from his days as a Kaleesh warrior remained. Dooku considered Grievous a successful leader due to the cyborg's ability to see the big picture; the general carried out high-handed tactics such as employing listening sites to ambush Republic fleets and attempting to invade Kamino to stop clone production.{{InsiderCite|188|The Grievous Growl}} Nonetheless, Grievous was never thrilled to receive orders and truly despised being paired with other commanders, believing it to be an insult on his ability as a leader and warrior. Though Grievous felt that he would emerge victorious, he was also arrogant enough to dismiss his subordinates' recommendations for caution. Maul considered Grievous as a monster with limited scope, whereas he viewed Dooku as having a broader perspective. Grievous was more frequently viewed as commander of a capital-class vessel, despite having his own starfighter. He frequently commanded naval engagements from his flagship dreadnought, the ''Invisible Hand'', demonstrating that becoming a cyborg had not weakened his tactical skills. Also holding command over a huge droid army, the largest ever created in fact, Grievous utilized his agile fleets and thousands of droid armies to strike planets like Falleen and Dorin, disrupting the Republic. Unable to predict where the droid general would strike next, the Republic became distracted, leaving previously conquered worlds open to reclaimed Separatist control. Grievous committed several blunders, although many of his setbacks proved temporary. Grievous did suffer defeats, most notably the loss of the Malevolence and his failed attacks on Kamino and Bothawui, though these were tempered by earlier victories on Falleen and Ruusan's moon. His mistakes frustrated Count Dooku, who eventually abandoned him on Vassek 3, deepening Grievous's hatred of Dooku. Despite these failures, Grievous also achieved important victories, including the successful second attack on Kamino, a bombing mission on Coruscant, and assaults against the Nightsisters of Dathomir and Hondo Ohnaka's pirate force. Playing an active role in the war, Grievous was often leading troops from the front in a horrifying display of lightsaber prowess and mechanical body strength, utilizing his enhanced physical capabilities to attack opposing forces and crushing everyone who came in reach, including Jedi. Overall, his combat, experience, and brutality especially shone in hand-to-hand combat. While he did compare his fair share of naval engagements to great effect, he in fact preferred the front lines, where he was surrounded by IG-100 MagnaGuards and challenged Jedi Generals in hopes of adding their lightsabers to his collection, although he would attempt to flee if the odds began to stack against him. Whether Jedi or not, Grievous was determined to achieve his goals and claim rewards. Grievous sometimes enlisted [[Commerce Guild]] forces for combat on rocky worlds or in urban areas, while [[OG-9 homing spider droid|OC-9 homing spider droids]] served as heavy armor and siege weaponry, with modified [[Spelunker probe droid]]s providing reconnaissance and sabotage. However, his skills are more than just physical. Behind Grievous's mask lurked one of the most astute military strategists of his time, one who doesn't hesitate to back down when the odds were against him. Grievous frequently avoided capture by the Republic and preferred brief skirmishes and repeated retreats, slipping away to fight another day, continually aggravating Republic commanders pursuing his capture or death. While Grievous was a more skilled warrior and tactician than any [[Republic officer|command officer]] in the Republic, the CIS's limited and unreliable resources have convinced him of the importance of having a quick and dependable departure option on even the safest of deployments. Grievous viewed retreat not as a defeat, but as a means of denying the Republic its final victory.{{ForceCollection|General Grievous [Elusive Commander]|star=5}} Grievous's military legend as a clever wrath who plunged into and out of engagements stealthily and quickly was a powerful weapon in the arsenal of the Separatists, and his own starfighter served as a continuation of that standing. While the general gained a reputation among the Republic and the Jedi for retreating when the odds were against him, his superiors admired his prudence, viewing his withdrawals as evidence of shrewd tactical judgment rather than cowardice.{{BuildFalconCite|40|Starship Fact File}} [[File:BattleOfDathomir-Sisters.png|thumb|left|300px|General Grievous was a ruthless warrior who waged and led campaigns of destruction and devastation.]] Not only a callously brilliant strategist, but his own fighting prowess made him a formidable foe in his own right. Grievous was a fearsome foe with a formidable duranium droid body guided by the twisted mind of a physically damaged warrior. The general demonstrated during the Clone Wars that one need not be strong in the Force to threaten even the greatest Jedi in combat. Grievous had shown himself to be more than a match for the Jedi opponents, demonstrating his strength even in situations where the Jedi did not act carelessly. Grievous believed that his mechanical limbs made him stronger than all of his enemies. He also thought that he was a better warrior than all the Jedi and wanted to prove himself in battle. Grievous employed ruthless tactics to secure numerous victories and instill fear in his opponents. His combat abilities only add to his reputation. On the battlefield, Grievous could be heard nursing a brutal hacking cough.{{Topps|set= 2018 Topps Star Wars: The Clone Wars 10th Anniversary|cardname=General Grievous}} Even with that drawback, he proved to be the most fearsome of opponents, with his whole, fast-moving physique best described as a living weapon.{{Topps|set=2018 Topps Star Wars Masterwork|cardname=General Grievous}} One of Grievous's weaknesses was that he didn't fully realize how much better his enhanced cyborg abilities were compared to the slower, less capable droids he commanded. He had little understanding of the Force and dismissed the Force as mere "tricks" or "magic", though he believed that the improvements made to his body gave him a greater power than that of the Jedi he hunted. He replaced this gap of knowledge with an appetite for destruction, especially of the power he did not truly comprehend. However, transforming his body into a fighting machine left Grievous's organic anatomy weak inside his armor. Grievous believed the Jedi weapon was a powerful symbol of faith and hope for its owners, serving as more than just a weapon in battle. Grievous's hatred for the Jedi was well known throughout the galaxy and directly stated by him on many occasions. A feared Jedi hunter, he was well known for his brutality and ruthlessness. While a formidable warrior, Grievous was known for fleeing from danger when confronted with an adversary he couldn't defeat. Grievous was quick to turn tail and run from a fight when the tide was turned against him, frequently scuttling away to safety using all four limbs. This tactic worked, until his final encounter with his nemesis, Kenobi, with whom Grievous shared a fierce rivalry. Kenobi could recognize the cyborg's mechanical cough from anywhere. Though Mace Windu and the rest of the Council branded Grievous a coward, that could not distract from his standing as a relentless and expert opponent who had defeated numerous Jedi in battle. Grievous had a brooding and sarcastic personality,{{EncyclopediaCite|Protocol and Service Droids}} showed sadism, and was known for being just as callous as the droids he commanded, whom he believed to be wrong. Grievous had a vengeful thirst for slaughtering Jedi and treasured their lightsabers as trophies. He also enjoyed in utilizing victims' lightsabers in battle. Grievous savored every kill he made, even children. He took macabre delight in beating Jedi on the battlefield and greatly enjoyed chasing down nimble Jedi. After capturing him, Grievous utilized Jedi Master Eeth Koth to make the Jedi suffer emotionally by feeling his pain and eventual death via their connection to the Force. When Kenobi and Skywalker were brought into his custody on the ''Invisible Hand'', the satisfied Grievous would have smiled if it was possible for him. Whether it's his pride in overseeing the galaxy's biggest droid army or his desire to murder Jedi, his goals appear to be entirely self-serving. The general was very confident in his own abilities, both personally and with the large forces he commanded, and became arrogant, believing that he was untouchable. However, this overconfidence repeatedly proved vulnerable. Grievous also insisted on fighting Jedi personally whenever possible, even when injured, which betrayed a sense of recklessness and restlessness in the cyborg general. Such was shown by his refusal to heed EV-A4D's advice to recuperate after his first bout with Kit Fisto and his former apprentice Nahdar Vebb. He acted recklessly again when he fought Obi-Wan on Utapau, which proved to be his undoing. ===Vicious streak and beyond the Jedi=== {{Quote|Whenever Grievous or Ventress cut down a Jedi, they brought me these little souvenirs of the battle. They make for quite the handsome display, don't you think?|Dooku, to Quinlan Vos|}} [[File:GrievousSaberCollection-ROTS.png|thumb|right|250px|Grievous had a horrific habit of killing Jedi and keeping their lightsabers as trophies.]] Grievous maintained a gloomy trophy room within his hidden lair and carried many stolen lightsabers in the lining of his cape or at his waist to terrify all challengers. Grievous had been collecting weapons as trophies for a long time, dating back to his days as a warlord on Kalee. By the end of the Clone Wars, he was rumored to have captured or killed about a dozen Jedi, including Jedi Master Neebo and the newly knighted Nahdar Vebb, and had amassed nearly a hundred lightsabers in his macabre collection. Both Anakin Skywalker and Obi-Wan Kenobi managed to avoid being added to Grievous's list of victims. In particular, he took great pleasure in hunting Jedi and claiming their lightsabers as trophies. The Jedi regarded such deceptive tactics as dishonorable, but Grievous held no such notions of dignity or honor. Instead, he took pride in his ever-expanding collection of war trophies: the lightsabers of his defeated enemies, along with other grisly souvenirs, such as a gruesome display of severed [[Padawan braid]]s taken from those struck down before their [[Knighting Ceremony|knighting]]. Although Grievous killed many Jedi during the Clone Wars, his greatest prizes were the lightsabers of Pablo-Jill, Eeth Koth, Roron Corobb, and Shaak Ti. Nahdar Vebb's lightsaber was briefly a part of his collection but was lost when Kit Fisto reclaimed it. At one point, Grievous gained the lightsaber of Jedi Master Jmmaar.[[Star Wars: Complete Vehicles (2018)|''Star Wars: Complete Vehicles'' (2018)]] His ruthless streak wasn't limited to the Jedi. He personally killed Gungan General Roos Tarpals on Naboo and massacred the Nightsisters of Dathomir. There, he showed no mercy, wiping out an [[Dathomiri clan|entire clan of witches]] and leaving only a handful of survivors. Grievous specifically sought out Old Daka, the oldest and wisest of the Nightsisters,{{SWE|characters|olddaka|Old Daka}} and killed her. He also killed Nightsister Selena in front of her daughter, Morgan Elsbeth. Although Mother Talzin escaped Grievous during his first assault on Dathomir, he was ultimately given the honor of delivering the final blow to the defeated Talzin during their second encounter. ===Relationships=== {{Quote|Chancellor Palpatine managed to escape your grip, general. Without Count Dooku, I have doubts about your ability to keep us safe.''"
"''Be thankful, Viceroy, you have not found yourself in my grip.|Nute Gunray, and Grievous' retort|}} [[File:Grievous_SOM.png|thumb|left|250px|Grievous conferring with Dooku.]] Grievous was loyal to both of his masters, Count Dooku and Darth Sidious, While Grievous had clashes with Dooku, he displayed a great respect towards the Confederacy's leader, whose orders the general would carry out without hesitation. Indeed, Grievous once made it clear to [[Nix Card]] that Dooku was the only person he was willing to take orders from, although he was also more than willing to obey the whims of the shadowy Sidious. Dooku himself, however, regarded the cyborg as nothing more than a useful tool.{{Databank|url=count-dooku-biography-gallery|text=Count Dooku Biography Gallery}} {{C|Image caption 11}} He shared his master's confidence and philosophy, such as when Dooku talked about his past and when Dooku informed him of Savage Opress's growing power, to which Grievous simply laughed at the notion that Opress could pose a threat to them. Grievous believes that Dooku was once Jedi Master Yoda's student. After Maul and Mother Talzin successfully captured Dooku, Grievous was trusted enough to join Sidious in rescuing him from a Nightbrother village on Dathomir. For all the respect he showed Dooku, such as directly calling the count his master, Grievous also had a hate for Dooku, which deepened when Dooku leaked the location of his lair to the Jedi, something that Grievous was unwilling to forgive. Grievous criticized Dooku for not killing Maul when he had the chance and believed Maul was too dangerous and insisted that letting him live was a mistake. Grievous wondered why Talzin would put herself in danger just for Maul. While fleeing the Battle of Coruscant, Grievous decided that, with any luck, he would be able to blame the disaster on Dooku. Furthermore, Grievous expressed no remorse for the count's death at the hands of Jedi Knight Anakin Skywalker, even if Dooku had helped him in lightsaber combat; rather, he viewed having full control over the Separatist forces as immensely helpful. Grievous knew that Darth Sidious was Count Dooku's master, but he had no idea that he was actually Sheev Palpatine himself. In a meeting with Sidious and other Separatists, Grievous learned of a new and even more powerful "apprentice" but never learned of their identity.[[Star Wars Jedi Master Magazine 3|''Star Wars Jedi Master'' Magazine 3]] While Sidious had no need for the cyborg by that time and abandoned his pawn, Grievous sought to show himself worthy of Sidious. [[File:VentressFlirty-ARCTroopers.png|thumb|right|278x278px|Ventress teases Grievous on Kamino.]] Despite being on the same side,{{EncyclopediaCite|Boba Fett and Other Characters of the Underworld}} General Grievous and Asajj Ventress shared a rivalry, and this suited Count Dooku perfectly and was very much the Sith way. There was an implication of perpetual conflict between them demonstrated by how both worked separately, rather than together. Grievous and Ventress were constantly tested and challenged by Dooku, in the same way Dooku's master repeatedly tested and challenged him. Grievous seemed to hold a little respect for her, as he praised her on her style and noted that they could be equals, but Ventress dismissed the idea. Unaware that it was Dooku who had turned on Ventress, Grievous regarded her as a traitor after her departure from the CIS. The general openly declared that he had always been superior to her during the Battle of Dathomir. Grievous and Ventress shared some traits; neither had a deep affection for the Jedi Order and both disliked battle droids. As for Grievous, the Republic and the Jedi intervened in a conflict between his people and the Huk, siding with their enemy and leaving his people to starve to death; as for Ventress, the Jedi had abandoned''[[Dooku: Jedi Lost]]'' her master, [[Ky Narec]], who had discovered her on the planet [[Rattatak]]{{TCW|Nightsisters (episode)}} and taught her in the use of the Force. Grievous valued loyalty and bravery in others, such as Captain Rackham Sear. Additionally, he viewed intricacy as a strength rather than a weakness and admired a formidable opponent. Grievous had always disliked Nute Gunray, the Neimoidian Viceroy who led the Separatist Council, Gunray, in turn, despised Grievous for Count Dooku preferential treatment of the cyborg. He threatened to kill Gunray, when the Neimoidian was brave enough to publicly criticize the cyborg. Gor was one of the few creatures that Grievous cared for, displaying a certain affection for his cyborg pet and being dismayed upon learning of the creature's death, which became another reason for his hatred of the Jedi. He also developed a kind of bond with his medical droid EV-A4-D, though he yelled at him from time to time and humiliated him, he let him criticize him without tearing him apart. Grievous shared his secrets with his medical droid, one of the few entitles in the galaxy who knew Grievous's secrets.{{BuildR2Cite|20|Droid Directory}} [[File:ScuttlingtoSafety-GeneralGrievous-SWU.jpg|thumb|left|270px|Grievous had a low opinion of his B1 battle droids.]] Despite taking pride in leading the most powerful droid army, Grievous also had a disdain for the battle droids, especially B1 models, considering them all but useless and terrible troops entrusted with a glorious mission above their ability. Grievous was frequently dissatisfied with the droid army's failure to live up to his high expectations and became upset by the droids' limitations,{{SW|url=battle-droid-history-gallery|text=Battle Droid History Gallery}} {{C|Image caption 14}} and he expressed his contempt through cruel physical abuse and wouldn't hesitate to destroy or abandon them in an instant. This habit often caused Dooku to remind Grievous that the droids were expensive. He had little patience for hesitation and reacted harshly whenever a droid appeared to question his decisions. When Grievous was in a bad mood after he had suffered a humiliating defeat, distracting him with a lightsaber never worked out well for the battle droid at hand. Legend claimed he was so willing to harm them because, in some ways, the droids reminded him of his own flaws. Furthermore, Grievous could not see the similarities between himself and the droids he harassed, believing that his organic heart made him stronger and better than the droids he tried to think he was nothing like. Given Grievous detested battle droids, his IG-100 MagnaGuards had to be impressively tough to withstand their master's demands. In remembrance of his first devoted Izvoshra bodyguards, Grievous ordered the MagnaGuards to wear cloaks and hoods that resembled the attire worn by the companions. Aside from training them in combat, he also taught his MagnaGuards various lessons in organic psychology. Grievous acknowledged the supremacy of clone warriors over his droids. He also had respect for the Mandalorians. With his four arms, smooth skull-like metal mask, and clawed feet, Grievous looked like something from a [[Dream|nightmare]] caused by the [[spice]], instead of looking like a real individual. He was more machine than living creature, but the amber slitted eyes that peered through his mask, staring down at opponents, revealed a dreadful malice: underneath the armor was the heart of an warlord,''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: Head-to-Head]]'' who was regarded as an evil individual by his foes. Though hugely powerful and may have appeared like a mechanical creation on the outside, Grievous despised droids and felt humiliated and responded with wrath whenever anyone dared to mistake him for one at first glance. Nonetheless, Grievous acknowledged that his new form made him frightening. He referred to his artificial skills as "improvements" and was concerned about his enhancements, insisting to his medical droid EV-A4-D that his drastic metamorphosis was his own decision. Legend specified in order to enjoy the benefits of both organic and inorganic lifeforms, he believed he could be as strong and versatile as a droid, with all the cunning, passion, and capacity for emotion of an organic being. On Utapau, it was not the first time he gloated over how his metal mask revealed no emotion, which was useful for Grievous when dealing with the Separatist Council; Grievous regarded them as ignorant beings who could not realize the extent of his disdain for them. [[File:GrievousBeforeCyborg-AORGrievous1.png|thumb|right|268x268px|Grievous feigned boastful satisfaction with his cybernetic form but was secretly angry.]] The legend of the Battle of Alamass made further claims about Grievous's mental state. Despite his military prowess, the general was still unhappy, for though he changed his body, he was not satisfied with his fate in life. In truth, he would never find peace or completion through the continued modification of his form, for deep down, he sought escape. No matter how much he might change what he was, he could never change who he was. Being a creature ruled by his heart, however, the general could never see this in himself. As a result, the general who would become a cyborg was a troubled soul, and he expressed his troubles through the only means he knew: violence. Grievous became increasingly angry and vengeful, lashing out at anyone he perceived as weak. Grievous's deep hatred of the Jedi, whom he blamed for crimes against him and his people, drove him to seek revenge by targeting individual Jedi. Grievous felt it was his duty to rid the galaxy of the "filth" of Jedi. By the time of the Clone Wars, Grievous cared not for the Republic or any political motivation to fight and instead focused his energy on destroying the Jedi Order. Grievous believed he was motivated purely by duty, but deep down, he still longed for the power, fear, and independence he once had, leaving him unsure of his true self. Grievous accepted that others might be right in calling him a "beast," but added that he was not an ordinary beast, but a force to be reckoned with. He had deliberately transformed himself into something unique and horrifying, warning others that they would soon understand the danger someone like him represented. Grievous’s opposition to the Jedi helped him recognize that his identity and purpose came from within himself rather than from an outside faith. Grievous had fully accepted his identity and confidence as a monster whose mission was entirely dedicated to destroying hope and those who upheld it. During the strategic purpose of the mission targeting the Jedi Temple on Coruscant, Grievous believed that the destruction of the tower would demonstrate to both the Galactic Republic and the Separatists that neither the Jedi Order nor the Republic was invincible, potentially altering the course of the entire war. ==Skills and abilities== ===Lightsaber abilities=== {{Quote|You fool! I've been trained in your Jedi arts by Count Dooku!|Grievous to Obi-Wan Kenobi|}} [[File:AoR-GeneralGrievous-Larraz-textless.png|thumb|left|200x320px|Grievous was very skilled with lightsabers, which allowed him to defeat and kill several great Jedi duelists.]] Although he lacked a powerful connection to the Force, Grievous was a highly skilled warrior who was capable of proficiently wielding lightsabers in combat against his enemies. His skill was a result of training received from Count Dooku, a Sith Lord once a Jedi Master. As the Separatist cyborg did not use the Force, Grievous' stolen lightsabers lacked the dark-side-induced corruption necessary for his [[bleeding|kyber to bleed]] and glowed the same color as those of the former masters he had slain. A master of several forms of lightsaber combat, Grievous was capable of quickly adapting to the fighting styles implemented by his opponents. Furthermore, due to the enhancements provided to him by his cybernetics, the Kaleesh often utilized superior strength and agility during his encounters with Jedi. A skilled lightsaber combatant who specialized in the form known as [[Jar'Kai]], which contributed to his personalized style of combat, Grievous utilized the advantage of his additional limbs during battle with others, which thereby allowed him to wield four lightsabers as a result and employ a personalized variation to overwhelm opponents. Grievous relied on the three crucial elements—fear, surprise, and intimidation—and if any of them were absent, it was preferable to retreat, reorganize, and attempt to reintroduce them before moving forward. Throughout the Clone Wars, Grievous often crossed blades with numerous Jedi Generals of the Republic. Even members of the Jedi Council struggled to challenge him. Many Jedi who encountered Grievous on the battlefield were slain by his blade, while few survived their encounters with him.{{HelmetCollectionCite|19|Databank A-Z}} According to the Kaleesh general's own account, he once faced an entire Jedi strike team. Grievous encountered Jedi Master Ki-Adi Mundi, leaving him with scars across his face. He also repeatedly clashed with Jedi General Obi-Wan Kenobi on multiple occasions. Their confrontations frequently ended without a clear victor, including their duels on Caliban, aboard the ''Malevolence'', aboard the ''[[Surrogator]]'' above Saleucami, and on Kamino. Although Grievous came close to defeating Kenobi several times, he ultimately defeated him aboard the ''Negotiator'' near Florrum and later aboard the Separatist supply ship above Utapau. In the end, however, Kenobi slew Grievous on Utapau. Grievous could destroy numerous enemies, including clone troopers, hordes of Telemak's droids, militiagung, the undead, Nightsisters, and Mandalorian warriors. Grievous fought and kept up with the dual-wielding Jedi Master Kit Fisto, despite losing one hand; dueled Eeth Koth after the Zabrak was shot in the arm, forcing him back and defeating him with the assistance of his bodyguards; and fought Adi Gallia in the midst of a firefight, driving her back and sending her flying with a kick before eventually defeating and capturing her. Grievous quickly overpowered Ahsoka Tano, the Padawan of Anakin Skywalker, in their first encounter during their time aboard Skytop Station, knocking her unconscious in the process, where he utilized intimidation tactics, such as roaring, to discourage his opponent. However, while Tano had improved by the time of their second encounter on Florrum, as she utilized the Force to gain an advantage, Grievous was once again able to overpower the Padawan through the implementation of his additional limbs and clawed feet. On Raxus, Grievous turned the fight around after Quinlan Vos initially gained the upper hand, disarming Grievous of his lightsabers and severing one of his hands. Grievous then overpowered Vos in midair and slammed him against a wall before subsequently being trapped in a security room. Despite the Grand Jedi Master's Force abilities, Grievous fought Yoda and survived long enough for his reinforcements to arrive. Grievous fought Depa Billaba on two occasions. He dueled Billaba on Haruun Kal and nearly killed her, and on Mygeeto, despite having two of his hands cut off, he struck her with a glancing blow to the back. During his mission to capture the Chancellor, Grievous dueled Shaak Ti. Although Ti managed to continue fighting, Grievous eventually gained the upper hand. He ensnared her with electrified cables, knocking her unconscious. [[File:2ndBattleDathomir-SoD-4.png|thumb|right|280px|Grievous could fight not only the Jedi Order members he despised, but also other combatants.]] Although Grievous was best known for battling the Jedi he despised, he also faced formidable opponents outside the Jedi Order. Grievous fought the former Sith assassin Asajj Ventress on two occasions. He dueled her on Dathomir and landed a kick on her, but she sliced off one of his arms, forcing him to call in backup. On Raxus, he pinned Ventress down with his foot against her throat, then used all four arms to seize her and throw her to a lower level. Ventress survived and escaped. Grievous also dueled the former Sith Lord Maul on two separate occasions, both resulting in stalemates.''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know, Updated and Expanded]]'' According to the legend, Grievous was able to fight fiercely and without hesitation because his body was designed to avoid pain, repair damage easily, and improve his strength, making him a very tough opponent. Grievous was also very skilled at deflecting blaster bolts with his lightsabers. He deflected several shots of clone troopers with a single blade and deflected several shots in close range while running toward them, deflected one shot while dangling from a rope, deflected shots of two clone troopers while spinning his lightsabers, despite being in a disadvantageous position, and deflected several [[booma]]s hurled by Gungans. He even demonstrated some skill in throwing his lightsaber, having launched it at Kit Fisto and the legs of two clone troopers. ===Other abilities=== {{Quote|I met a Kaleesh on my travels who bragged of a revered warrior. He supposedly had cybernetic implants for enhanced combat!|An artist, in his journal|}} Grievous chose an unorthodox fighting style while contending with the Jedi, using his four arms to his advantage. While possessing no Force abilities, Grievous compensated for his lack of supernatural powers with extensive cybernetic enhancements. His heightened senses, the precise articulation of his artificial limbs, and his advanced cybernetic systems provided him with reflexes and agility comparable to those of a Jedi Knight, making him a dangerous opponent for any Jedi he encountered. His entire body was designed as a weapon, allowing him to deliver precise blows at speeds far beyond what his natural body could achieve. Electro-motors could instantly transform his two arms into four, allowing him to wield multiple weapons simultaneously and greatly increasing his strength and efficiency on the battlefield. Grievous could even wield a blaster at close range while engaging in a lightsaber duel, presenting a lethal double threat to even the most skilled Force-sensitive opponent. [[File:EscapePlan-SWVPotDS.png|thumb|left|270px|Grievous could move very quickly when using all his limbs for locomotion.]] With arms that can split into four, Grievous could wield up to four lightsabers at once. He could also use his mechanical arms to spin his lightsabers, both with and without separating them, so quickly that they became pinwheels of destruction, creating a deadly shield. One of his favorite strategies was to spin his lightsabers at near-impossible speeds to deliver a deadly blow. Most Jedi he encountered reacted quickly enough to counter this tactic. He could also rotate his torso; when the clones piled on top of him during the Battle of Saleucami, he used this ability to throw the troopers off. His magnetic, claw-like limbs allowed him to cling to the outside panels of starships like a spider or quickly scale vertical metal surfaces, allowing him to reach areas that would otherwise be difficult to access. Each arm could also function as a leg, allowing him to use his extra limbs to scurry forward like a giant insect with remarkable agility. When Grievous had the opportunity, he rarely fought fairly. During his duel with Nahdar Vebb, after locking blades with him, Grievous used his free hands to draw a blaster and fire several shots into Vebb's torso. Later, he employed a similar tactic against Obi-Wan Kenobi, using one of his free hands to seize Kenobi and hurl him to the ground after engaging him in combat. He also made use of his IG-100 MagnaGuards. During his fight with Eeth Koth, Grievous was aided by his MagnaGuards in capturing the Jedi Master. Later, after Anakin and Obi-Wan escaped from their bonds, Grievous had his MagnaGuards engage the Jedi. Grievous was very fast as he was able to use his cybernetics to crawl on the ground and make a quick escape if he needed to. Grievous was able to quickly catch up to a large creature that was too fast for someone to pursue on foot, and he even outran a Padawan who had a head start. Not only was he fast, but he also had enhanced strength. He could knock a B1 battle droid's head off with a backhand, lift and stop a rolling droideka before smashing it into the floor, and leap high enough to grab a large creature by the neck and slam it into the ground despite having virtually no leverage. He could also kick a large blast door across a room and shake a tunnel with a stomp. In addition, he kicked Kenobi onto a gunship hard enough to shake it, lifted a varactyl off himself with one arm, pushed through several Mandalorian warriors while crushing [[Mandalorian armor|their armors]], and accidentally dented his starfighter with a punch, despite its hull being reinforced with tremendously resilient impervium. His hand-to-hand combat abilities far exceeded those of an ordinary soldier, as he utilized his two or four arms in a unique fighting style, lifting, throwing, choking, and crushing his opponents with his bare hands or his powerful durasteel feet. His feet were magnetized and sharp enough to function effectively as talons, allowing him to grip and manipulate objects and even transfer weapons into his hands. [[File:Grievous_Charred.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Equipped with strong armor, Grievous could stand up to explosions and other attacks.]] With a metal body stronger than any droid's shell, Grievous was very durable and could even resist explosions from fuel barrels. His biological remains were very much not fireproof, but they remained safe behind his armor. Thanks to his cyborg form, Grievous was able to survive in space and grip effectively onto a ship's hull. When Kenobi kicked at him during the Battle of Utapau, Grievous hardly felt it, but it very much hurt Kenobi. Grievous was Force pushed by Eeth Koth with enough force to crack a ship's window, yet quickly recovered. After being Force pushed into a wall by Yoda, he quickly stood back up. Even after Kenobi Force-pushed him against a wall and ceiling, Grievous was able to flee. Grievous managed to escape after Kenobi Force pushed him into heavy machinery on the ceiling and sent him tumbling down, although he lost his grip on his remaining lightsabers. Grievous crashed his speeder into a herd of varactyls and emerged unscathed from underneath one of them. Grievous was seemingly unaffected when Maul tackled him into a window. When Grievous passed through Talzin's Force barrier, which was capable of absorbing blaster fire, while Sidious and Dooku struck it with Force lightning, he remained unharmed. Although losing limbs was survivable for him due of his cyborg form, damage to one of his limbs would required repair by his medical droid, EV-A4-D. ===Military skills=== {{Quote|The general's description of your tactics have been one hundred percent accurate today. Very impressive, even by ''my'' standards.|TV-94, to Anakin Skywalker|}} [[File:GoH-Grievous.png|thumb|left|250px|Grievous was a force to be reckoned with in both strategy and combat.]] On his homeworld, Grievous had already demonstrated himself to be a brilliant military leader and proven his abilities as a warlord. Grievous was also a competent strategist as he used his massive army to overwhelm his opponents. He was able to predict outcomes based on past experiences and could read micro-expressions and use them to uncover information. According to legend, Grievous devised a tactically sound-sounding strategy to attack an enemy force from a risky route, but it would cost him a large portion of his droid army. Grievous was able to distract Kenobi and Skywalker with a droid attack, allowing a combat-capable mouse droid to slip onto their ship and reprogram it to fly into a star. Grievous led a devastating campaign in the Outer Rim, crushing multiple legions and fleets along the way. During the Battle of Bothawui, the Kaleesh warlord maneuvered his fleet through Bothawui's planetary ring, using it as cover from Republic attacks. He managed to damage a Republic cruiser before Skywalker realized what he was attempting to do. He was able to correctly anticipate the Republic's movements and accurately foresee Anakin's tactics during the Battle of Saleucami. Grievous was also able to fool the Republic forces during the Battle of Kamino with his ships taking heavy casualties, completely fooling even Anakin, but Obi-Wan Kenobi, his rival, was the only person who eventually identified his plan. Later, he led his fleets to victory against Kenobi, the Republic's wise and tactical Jedi General, and captured his flagship without losing a single capital ship. Grievous was able to sneak aboard enemy ships with his MagnaGuards and attack them from within. He was also able to recognize that Maul had yet to deploy warships during the Battle on Ord Mantell. Tey-Zuka calculated that the enemy ships had been destroyed on the initial bombardment, but soon their [[Grievous's Providence-class Dreadnought (Campaign against the Shadow Collective)|dreadnought]] was hit, and Grievous recognized that they had been lured into a trap. Grievous lured Depa Billaba into a trap, cutting off her escape routes and surrounding her with battle droids on Mygeeto. Grievous could control his battle droid forces remotely via radio commands transmitted through his antennas. Grievous could also command the ''Invisible Hand''{{'s}} defense via his built-in cybernetic comlinks, while the dorsal sensor and communications masts coordinate surrounding droid fighters. [[File:ImperviumPlating-SWZ.png|thumb|right|300px|Grievous pilots the ''Soulless One''.]] The general gained a reputation as a talented flier and piloted a customized [[Belbullab-22 heavy starfighter|Belbullab-22 starfighter]] known as the ''Soulless One''. He was skilled enough to avoid and escape Anakin Skywalker's starfighter. Not only did Grievous successfully avoid each laser fire, but he also managed to achieve hyperspace without a single shot, demonstrating his superior cyborg-enhanced piloting skills. Although it should be noted that Skywalker almost shot him down, but his starfighter lost a piece of shrapnel embedded in the fighter that caused it to careen off course. While chasing him and Kenobi on Utapau, he managed to keep up with Skywalker, who was considered the best pilot in the Republic, scoring enough hits on the Jedi's [[Unidentified freighter (Utapau)|freighter]] to damage it and even keeping up with them when the pair escape on a ''Sheathipede''-class transport shuttle. Grievous was an incredibly talented fighter on the ground, but he recognized that his skills as a fighter pilot, while not insignificant, were not on par with those of a Jedi, and thus he utilized his ship more frequently to escape or for personal purposes. ==Equipment== {{Quote|So uncivilized…|Obi-Wan Kenobi disposing of Grievous's blaster|}} [[File:Annihilator_blaster_sw_thi_blaster.png|thumb|left|250px|Grievous wielded a custom DT-57 "Annihilator."]] Despite lacking Force sensitivity and Jedi training, Grievous used a variety of lightsabers in combat. In addition to his ever-growing collection of stolen lightsabers used in close-quarters combat, Grievous also used a blaster weapon for ranged engagement. As opposed to his Jedi adversaries, he also owned a custom [[DT-57 "Annihilator" blaster|DT-57 "Annihilator"]] blaster pistol called the "Grievance Striker",{{Destiny|set=Convergence|cardname=Grievance Striker|link=https://swdestinydb.com/card/09169}} utilizing everything of the technology at his disposal. Furthermore, such as an electrostaff or other models of blasters, such as the [[DC-17]] pistol or E-5 rifle. Grievous's cybernetic body protected his remaining organs within a pressurized synthskin gut-sack, allowing him to operate in space without the need for a spacesuit. His form was completed with two [[LX-44 robotic leg]]s, powerfully magnetized feet ending in four talon-like toes, and [[Electrodriver|electro-driven]] mechanical arms that could split at the shoulders and become four, transforming him into a four-armed cyborg monstrosity. Each hand possessed its own opposable thumb and articulated fingers, with integrated [[sensor]]s that allowed him to feel and touch the world around him.[[Age of Republic - General Grievous 1|''Age of Republic - General Grievous'' 1]] More machine than flesh, all that remained of Grievous was metal, mechanical [[actuator]]s, [[armorplast]], and hatred. Grievous was equipped with grapple lines built into his wrists, which he could launch at a long distance to attach himself to objects. The general also piloted a customized Belbullab-22 starfighter known as the ''Soulless One''. Not only did he use his own starfighter, but the brutal cyborg used other vehicles, including a combat speeder and a modified wheel bike. ==Behind the scenes== ===Overview=== {{Quote|With General Grievous, I wanted somebody who was reminiscent of what Anakin is going to become, which is a half man, half robot. In this case, Grievous is sort of 20% alien and 80% robot.|[[George Lucas]] on the creation of Grievous|{{Film|III}} DVD commentary}} [[File:AoR-GeneralGrievous-Concept-textless.png|thumb|right|250px|Later-stage concept art of the droid general.]] General Grievous was developed for [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] as a powerful new villain on the side of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Confederacy]].''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'', Disc 7, Star Wars Archives: Episode III General Grievous Marquette video commentary{{DB|character|generalgrievous|Grievous, General}} The character made his first appearance in the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' piece "[[Republic HoloNet News Core Edition 15:3:02]]" from [[Star Wars Insider 75|issue 75]]{{InsiderCite|75|Republic HoloNet News Core Edition 15:3:02}}—which was released on [[April 6]] of [[2004]] but was shipped to subscribers starting [[March 19]]{{SWArchive|url=community/fanclub/mag/news20040315.html|text=The New Face of Evil}}—after an indirect mention in [[Star Wars Insider 73|''Star Wars Insider'' 73's]] "[[CIS Shadowfeed Dispatch 15:01:15 Edition]]"{{InsiderCite|73|CIS Shadowfeed Dispatch 15:01:15 Edition}} on [[January 13]] of that year.{{SWArchive|url=community/news/2003/12/news20031219.html|text=Mark Hamill On Stage In ''Insider'' #73}} Although he went so far as to grace the cover of ''Star Wars Insider'' 75 and had been introduced to the ''[[Star Wars]]'' fanbase by [[StarWars.com]] on [[March 15]] as the "New Face of Evil," [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]]'s introduction is considered to have come''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]'' on [[April 8]], 2004,{{SWArchive|url=hyperspace/about/news/news20040323.html|text=''Clone Wars'' Season 2 on Hyperspace}} within "[[Chapter 20 (Star Wars: Clone Wars)|Chapter 20]]" of the [[2003]] animated series ''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]''.{{CW|20}} As of [[2014]], many of these stories are now considered to be part of the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity.{{SW|url=news/the-legendary-star-wars-expanded-universe-turns-a-new-page|text=The Legendary Star Wars Expanded Universe Turns a New Page}} [[Canon]]ically speaking, Grievous made his first appearance in ''Revenge of the Sith''. While Grievous would only have around six minutes of screen time in the final film, with Darth Sidious actually being the film's primary antagonist, StarWars.com had teased Grievous's coming role in ''Revenge of the Sith'' on [[May 26]], 2004, claiming that Grievous would be "the Villain of Episode III."{{SWArchive|url=kids/explore/episode-iii/news20040526.html|text=The Villain of Episode III}} In ''Revenge of the Sith'', the character was portrayed by [[Matthew Wood]], the film's supervising sound editor. In his first appearance in Chapter 20, Grievous had been voiced by [[John DiMaggio]] before [[Richard McGonagle]] took on the role for the rest of the original ''Clone Wars'' series.{{CW|21}} However, StarWars.com had confirmed before release of ''Revenge of the Sith'' that Grievous "[wouldn't] necessarily" sound in the film like he did in that animated series. Since ''Revenge of the Sith'', Wood has retained the role of Grievous, portraying the droid general in the [[2008]] animated series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' and numerous other post-''Revenge of the Sith'' appearances. ===Development=== ====Creation==== {{Quote|It's rare to have a new main character that has to be designed from scratch.|Warren Fu|{{InsiderCite|213|Warren Fu: Envisaging Grievous}}}} [[File:Head_of_the_Confederacy.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Early concept art of Grievous.]] During the development of ''Revenge of the Sith'', Grievous was created when it was clear that, with Dooku dying early in the film, the movie would need a new villain.{{SW|url=news/10-things-we-learned-from-the-star-wars-archives-1999-2005|text=10 Things We Learned from ''The Star Wars Archives 1999-2005''}} The initial instructions that Director George Lucas gave the Art Department were very open-ended: "a droid general," specifying that the character needed to be reminiscent of the [[Original trilogy]]'s Darth Vader without being a copy of the famous Sith Lord.{{SW|url=news/10-things-we-learned-from-the-star-wars-archives-1999-2005|text=10 Things We Learned from ''The Star Wars Archives 1999-2005''}} From that vague direction, the artists developed a lot of explorations, some purely mechanical, some not, for the look of General Grievous. Lucas later noted to the crew that Grievous needed to clearly and visually be a cyborg, denying early designs that depicted his mask with robotic [[photoreceptor]]s. An early concept design featured Grievous as "a disembodied alien head, trailing a number of prehensile tentacles".{{SWArchive|url=episode-iii/bts/artofrev/2005/02/artofrev20050207.html|series=Art of Revenge|text=Head of the Separatists}} Legend has it that Nilo Rodis-Jamero got the idea for Boba Fett's ship from the San Rafael streetlamps. In that spirit, concept artist [[Warren Fu]] drew on unexpected ideas from everyday objects. A spray bottle inspired his first passes at interesting heads. Those designs weren't picked, but George gravitated towards another one of Wu's designs, which ended up being the MagnaGuards.{{InsiderCite|213|Warren Fu: Envisaging Grievous}} Amongst the artists of the Episode III art department who made designs for Grievous were [[Derek Thompson]], [[Erik Tiemens]], [[Alex Jaeger]], and [[Warren Fu]]. Ultimately, it was a sketch by the latter that most defined what Grievous would look like, even though it was only a quick sketch that he was not very impressed by. Lucas, meanwhile, was instantly impressed by the drawing. [[File:RockDrillStatue.png|thumb|right|300px|Jacob Epstein's statue ''Rock Drill'' (reconstruction pictured) has been connected to Grievous's design by commentators.]] According to StarWars.com, artists [[Robert E. Barnes|Robert Barnes]], [[Iain McCaig]], and [[Ryan Church]] were also involved in creating Grievous. When interviewed ''[[The Star Wars Archives: Episodes I–III, 1999–2005]]'', Wu stated Grievous's white coloration was created to be the opposite of Darth Vader's black suit, further noting that, within Chinese culture, the color of white represents death. According to [[Rob Coleman]], [[Wikipedia:Ray Harryhausen|Ray Harryhausen]]’s [[Wikipedia:Kali|Kali]] from the [[Wikipedia:The Golden Voyage of Sinbad|''The Golden Voyage of Sinbad'']] was an inspiration for the four-armed general.{{Twitter|ArfKeldo|status/1065365045045952512|[[Rob Coleman]]|quote=Yes, Ray Harryhausen’s Kali from the Golden Voyage of Sinbad (1973) was definitely an inspiration for the four armed General Grievous}} From Warren Fu's initial sketch came further refinements, and the finalized character would emerge from discussions between Barnes, McCaig, Church, and Wu, followed by sketches. Finally a foot-tall maquette sculpted by Robert Barnes showed what the general would look like in three dimensions. This sculpture was further modified to become a realistic computer-generated model for use by [[Industrial Light & Magic]]. According to [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''The Clone Wars'']] and [[Star Wars Rebels|''Rebels'']] co-producer and writer, [[Henry Gilroy]], Lucas briefly considered having [[Maul]] be Grievous, in that his upper half would be inside the armor.{{WebCite|url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1179944/star-wars-creator-george-lucas-briefly-considered-making-general-grievous-darth-maul-in-disguise-exclusive|text=Star Wars Creator George Lucas Briefly Considered Making General Grievous Darth Maul In Disguise [Exclusive]|author=Busch, Jenna|date=2023-01-26|work=[[Wikipedia:/Film|Slashfilm]]|archivedate=20260203164747}} Grievous's design was finalized around the end of [[2002]], only six months before shooting for the movie began.''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'', Disc 7, Star Wars Archives: Episode III General Grievous Marquette description Commentators have drawn a connection between Grievous's design and ''[[Wikipedia:Rock Drill (Jacob Epstein)|Rock Drill]]'',{{BookCite|author=Brandon, Laura|title=Art and War|publisher=Bloomsbury Publishing|date=2012-11-25|isbn=9780857732811}} a 1913-1915{{WebCite|url=https://thenewartgallerywalsall.org.uk/exhibition/robotic-futures-epsteins-rock-drill-1913-15|text=Robotic Futures Epstein’s Rock Drill 1913-15|archivedate=20250419013530}} statue by British artist [[Wikipedia:Jacob Epstein|Jacob Epstein]]. The statue's design has also been compared to the B1 battle droid.{{BookCite|author=Mullins, Charlotte|title=A Little History of Art|publisher=Yale University Press|date=2022-04-26|pages=234|isbn=9780300265538}} After Lucas approved the maquette design, Industrial Light & Magic began its work on creating the character's CGI model. The model of Grievous was one of the most complicated ILM had ever constructed, having so many parts of differing physical qualities. ====Continued production and filming==== On set, no one person played Grievous, though off-screen dialogue reader [[Duncan Young]] read his lines. For combat sequences, stunt performer [[Kyle Rowling]] wore a greenscreen or bluescreen suit to play Grievous in his battles with Obi-Wan Kenobi. During production, the crew found it hard to film the duel between Kenobi and Grievous when the cyborg warlord uses all four of his hands. After considering having one actor sit atop another or having one suspended from the ceiling to achieve the tall general's multiple armed attack run, it was decided to use two stunt performers, with one standing in front of the other, to achieve the scene, but it was decided this strategy did not work out. Their next idea was to have one performer learn both Grievous's above and below attacks, allowing the complete attack run to be assembled out of both passes in post-production. In the end, it was decided that Grievous should lose several of his hands quickly to make filming easier on the crew, explaining why Grievous only briefly uses all four of his limbs to duel in ''Revenge of the Sith''.''[[The Star Wars Archives: Episodes I–III, 1999–2005]]'' Lucas originally wanted a powerful erect posture for the 'droid, but decided during production to have him rendered hunched and sickly.{{BookCite|title=[[Wikipedia:Entertainment Weekly|''Entertainment Weekly'']]|number=#820}} To that end, during the production of ''Revenge of the Sith'', George Lucas came into work one day with a cough and decided that it would be amusing to record it and use it on the new Episode III villain. According to animation director [[Rob Coleman]], the idea of this sicky element was to foreshadow ''Star Wars''{{'}} more famous half-man/half-machine, Vader, whom Grievous was "like the alpha version of." Grievous's vampiric movements were inspired by the German horror classic [[Wikipedia:Nosferatu|''Nosferatu'']], one of many monster-movie references in ''Sith''. Coleman further stated in the ''Revenge of the Sith'' DVD commentary that Grievous's cybernetics were seen as a step in the development of the Vader armor by Lucas and company, with Vader's cybernetics finally perfecting what had been the prototype with Grievous. This explains why Grievous suffers from a cough but Vader does not. [[File:ROTS-GeneralGrievousheadshot.png|thumb|left|300px|General Grievous's computer generated design was approved in March 2004 but would not be completed for some time (Grievous's finalized model in ''Revenge of the Sith'', pictured).]] At least as argued by some fan and commentators,{{WebCite|url=https://www.inverse.com/entertainment/general-grievous-clone-wars-20-year-anniversary|text=20 Years Ago, Star Wars Introduced its Most Hardcore Villain — Then Ruined Him|author=Ryan Britt|date=2024-04-09|work=Inverse|archivedate=20250124112115}} there is a difference between the more "relentless" Grievous seen in pre-''Revenge of the Sith'' material and the quick-to-retreat, "mustache-twirling" villain depicted in the film, an apparent contradiction even acknowledged by [[Star Wars Insider|''Star Wars'' Insider]]. It was George Lucas who wanted to make Grievous more of a "Dracula Droid" and made the call after watching a rough cut of ''Revenge of the Sith''.{{InsiderCite|149|General Grievous: Beneath the Armor}} Grievous's computer generated design was approved in March of 2004. According to StarWars.com, as of May 26 of that year, Grievous's model had yet to "painted," nor had his body language and animation been refined or developed. As such, Grievous's model had not yet been added to the cut of the film as it existed at that time. No voice actor had been found at that time as well, with producer [[Rick McCallum]] hypothesizing that voice-work for Grievous and the rest of the cast would begin sometime between August and November of that year. ====Finding a voice==== It would be many months before a voice actor was hired to perform Grievous's dialogue. In the end, Supervising Sound Editor Matthew Wood had submitted the winning audition. According to Wood himself, he was a sound editor for Lucas's projects when Lucas started recording many different actors for the voice of Grievous. They had planned to process Grievous's voice to make it sound like it was coming out of his "little cyborg face."{{YouTube|video=D9sSSJ-h4hQ|text=Matthew Wood interview Voice of general grievous|channel=@Ecwa2k|name=ECWA}} Lucasfilm recorded [[Ben Burtt]]'s voice for General Grievous while [[Rick McCallum]] put out a huge casting call. [[Chris Scarabosio]], the dialogue editor, and Wood devised how Grievous was supposed to sound, and George approved it.{{Blogspot|subdomain=starwarsinterviews1|url=2010/04/matt-wood-interview-general-grievous.html|name=Star Wars Interviews|text=Matt Wood interview General Grievous Star Wars|date=2005-09}} After getting auditions from various actors, Lucas never gravitated towards one he liked. Wood had the luxury of hearing everyone's auditions, so his friend encouraged him to put one. Chris said Matthew should try to get the part, but he thought it was "too weird and I couldn't do it." In his own words, Wood had an advantage in knowing what George wanted as he heard him talk to the actors about Grievous. Finally, Wood decided to give it a try. Chris recorded him and put the tape under an anonymous name with the rest. Matthew didn't think about it after that until one day Rick McCallum came up to him and asked if Matthew had the agent's name of the person whose voice was on a certain tape since he had all the documentation. Wood thought it was a prank, "that he knew it was me and I had screwed up," but Rick couldn't have known. Thinking he had crossed the line, Wood confessed it was him. McCallum apparently said afterward, "Are you s**tting me?" before asking Wood what to do, to which he suggested telling George. McCallum then called George and said it was Matthew Wood's voice. George then called Wood and asked him to come over and record it. Wood would later state that Lucas was "really cool about it," much to his own shock of receiving the role of a lead villain in a new Star Wars movie. He would later say of the experience in an interview, "It was fun, because I don't have any shyness around George." By Wood's own admission, that chance changed his life and opened the doors for many other voice-acting roles. When auditioning, Matthew Wood used an Eastern European accent from recently spending time in Prague and a [[Wikipedia:Bela Lugosi|Bela Lugosi]] Dracula component that Lucas himself liked, mixed with "a little bit of a drill sergeant vibe." According to Mathew Wood, Grievous's original origin was that he was a Jedi who had been betrayed by Dooku and "had a bone to pick with the Jedi." Wood didn't tell anyone about his role until, finally, when the film was printed, he told "everybody." Before Matthew Wood was cast as Grievous, British actor [[Gary Oldman]] was offered Grievous's role. According to a report in the [[Wikipedia:Daily Star (United Kingdom)|Daily Star]], which quoted Oldman's official spokesman, "Gary was excited and looking forward to working on the film. The snag is that the movie is being made without members of the [[Wikipedia:Screen Actors Guild|Screen Actors Guild]]. It means Gary would have been working illegally overseas. Out of respect and solidarity with the other members, he could not and would not consider violating the rules of his union." Production had already been completed, and Oldman's work was limited to providing the voice of General Grievous - described at the time as an evil Jedi Knight killer - and was due to be completed during the post-production process taking place then at the LucasFilm HQ, [[Skywalker Ranch]].{{WebCite|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2004/sep/16/news.starwars|text=Oldman shelves Star Wars role in the name of thespian union|date=2004-09-16|work=The Guardian|archivedate=20140916201231}} Gary Oldman said he did a voice on the ''Happy Sad Confused'' podcast. However, due to something to do with union and non-union talent, he did not want to be at the center of any controversy surrounding breaking union rules. He could be deployed into battle in ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Defense]]''.''[[Star Wars: Galactic Defense]]'' He was playable as part of the player's team in ''[[Star Wars: Force Arena]]''''[[Star Wars: Force Arena]]'' and is playable in ''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]''.''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]'' On [[May 15]], [[2025]], Grievous was added as an outfit in ''[[Fortnite]]''{{'s}} thirty-fifth season of its six chapter, alongside cosmetics based on his Kaleesh cape and the TSMEU-6 personal wheel bike.{{FortniteWeb|url=news/strap-in-starfighter-star-wars-is-taking-over-in-fortnite-galactic-battle|text=Strap in Starfighter, Star Wars is Taking Over in Fortnite: GALACTIC BATTLE!}} On [[April 26]], [[2025]], Grievous was added as a playable character in ''[[Brawlhalla]]'' as part of a Star Wars crossover event to celebrate May the 4th and the 20th anniversary of Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith.{{Brawlhalla|url=news/brawlhalla-star-wars-may-the-4th-event-wave-ii-reveal-trailer|text=Brawlhalla STAR WARS May the 4th Event Wave II Reveal Trailer}} ===Contradictions=== [[File:Displate-Grievousstandsthere.png|thumb|left|300px|General Grievous as a cyborg warrior]] According to San Hill - Banking Clan Chairman - ''Base Series 1'', which was released as part of ''[[Star Wars: Card Trader]]'', Grievous proved to be a volatile ally towards San Hill, Poggle the Lesser, and Dooku in the time before his cyborg transformation. As such, the three began conspiring to destroy Grievous and rebuild him into a super-cyborg of servitude.{{SWCT|set=Base Series 1|cardname=San Hill - Banking Clan Chairman}} At the time, [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] member [[Pablo Hidalgo]] said this was an outdated Legends reference{{Twitter|pablohidalgo|status/672253588018618368|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=Tweet lost but did state that San Hill - Banking Clan Chairman - ''Base Series 1'' contains an outdated reference to Legends via San Hill, Poggle, and Dooku working together to destroy and rebuild Grievous.|nobackup=1}} based on the character's backstory from the comic "[[The Eyes of Revolution]]."{{StoryCite|story=The Eyes of Revolution|book=Star Wars: Visionaries}} However, as other modern sources have canonized "The Eyes of Revolution"-inspired details, the Story Group may have changed its mind. As established by the reference book ''[[Star Wars: On the Front Lines]]'' and supported by episodes of ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'',{{TCW|The Phantom Apprentice}}{{TCW|Shattered}} only a few days pass between the Battles of Coruscant and Utapau. "[[The Duel for Peace]]" states that Kenobi had not seen Grievous in a long time before the Battle of Utapau. However, they had last seen each other face-to-face in the Battle of Coruscant mere days prior. [[Star Wars Bust Collection 68|''Star Wars Bust Collection'' 68]] also claimed that Grievous hid on Utapau in "the closing weeks" of the war after the Battle of Coruscant.{{BustCollectionCite|68|Character}} However, as only a few days pass between the Battles of Coruscant and Utapau, that cannot be accurate. The [[2023]] reference magazine [[Star Wars Starships & Vehicles 55|''Star Wars Starships & Vehicles'' 55]] states that Grievous requested a more advanced battle droid after becoming Supreme Commander of the Separatists, which led to the development of the MagnaGuard. In specific, it claims he asked for more advanced droids than the [[Trade Federation]]'s simple combat droids, which he criticized for relying on commands from a central [[computer]] and being incapable of learning from their mistakes on their own. The majority of sources, however, state that Grievous requested such droids back when he was fighting for the InterGalactic Banking Clan, placing the creation of the MagnaGuards earlier in the ''Star Wars'' timeline. This article sides with the majority of sources and states that Grievous requested his advanced droid troops during his days as an IGBC enforcer. The presence of MagnaGuards in [[33 BBY]] via to their appearance in [[Darth Maul (2017) 3|''Darth Maul'' (2017) 3]][[Darth Maul (2017) 3|''Darth Maul'' (2017) 3]] helps to narrow down the timeline
