{{Top}} {{Youmay|the [[Jedi Master]] Cin Drallig, nicknamed "the Troll"|[[Troll (disambiguation)|other uses of the term]]}} {{Update|[[Star Wars: Force Collection]]}} {{Character |type=Jedi |image=[[File:Cin_Drallig_SWE.png]] |name=Cin Drallig |homeworld=[[Lavisar]]''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Character Encyclopedia - Join the Battle!]]'' |birth= |death=[[19 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' [[Coruscant]]{{SWE|characters|cin-drallig|Cin Drallig}} |species=[[Human]] |gender=[[Gender|Male]] |pronouns=He/him |height=1.74 [[meter]]s {{C|5 [[Foot|ft]], 9 in}} |mass= |hair=[[Color|Dark blond]] |feathers= |eyes=Blue |skin=Light |cyber= |families=new |parents=new |partners=new |siblings=new |children=new |affiliation=[[Jedi Order]] |masters=[[Yoda]]''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]'' |apprentices= }} {{Quote|Safety is a flexible concept.|Cin Drallig, to [[Sammo Quid]]|[[Kanan 8|''Kanan'' 8]]}} '''Cin Drallig''' was a [[Force-sensitive]] [[human]] [[Gender|male]] [[Jedi Master]] who served the [[Jedi Order]] as [[Battlemaster]] and [[Chief of Security]] of the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] during the [[Clone Wars]]. He was the head of the [[Jedi Temple Guard]] and a [[lightsaber]] instructor who was disrespectfully nicknamed "'''the Troll'''" by members of the [[Jedi]]. Drallig was killed by [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] during his [[Operation: Knightfall|attack]] on the Jedi Temple. ==Biography== ===Early life and Jedi career=== [[Homeworld|Hailing]] from [[Lavisar]], Cin Drallig, a gifted [[Force-sensitive]] [[human]] [[Gender|male]], was [[Padawan|apprenticed]] to the [[Jedi High Council]]'s [[Grand Master]] [[Yoda]]. Faithfully honing his skills and attunement to the Force, Drallig garnered many years of knowledge and experience, and eventually became the [[Jedi Order]]'s [[Battlemaster]].{{ForceCollection|Cin Drallig|star=4}} Drallig also achieved the rank of [[Jedi Master]], and led the [[Jedi Temple Guard]] during the [[Clone Wars]] as the temple [[Chief of Security]]. As a Master, he was a teacher of [[lightsaber]] combat who passed his skills on to new generations of [[Jedi]],{{Databank|cin-drallig|Cin Drallig}} such as [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Anakin Skywalker]]. Although he was regarded as perhaps the finest duelist in the Order, he earned the unflattering nickname "the [[Troll]]" from other members of the Jedi Order. ===The Clone Wars=== ====Guarding the Temple==== {{Quote|Stay with them. Keep an eye out for those mini-drone explosives.''"
"''Yes, Master Drallig.|Cin Drallig orders Jedi Temple Guards to stay with a group of younglings|}} [[File:Jedi_guards_at_rally.png|thumb|left|250px|Drallig guards the Jedi Temple during a rally.]] In [[21 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' places "[[Liberty on Ryloth]]" and "[[Children of the Force]]" in [[21 BBY]]. As this episode takes place between these two episodes according to {{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-clone-wars-chronological-episodeorder|text=''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Chronological Episode Order}}, "[[Holocron Heist]]" must also take place in 21 BBY. [[Cad Bane]] slipped past Drallig and the Temple's security forces using specialized technology and his intelligence and managed to slip into the [[Holocron Vault]]. A Jedi [[holocron]] was stolen. During the [[Cloning|Clone]] Wars, the [[Bombing of the Jedi Temple hangar|Jedi Temple was bombed]] by [[Padawan]] [[Barriss Offee]]. Before the perpetrator had been caught, the Jedi led an investigation to determine who was behind the attack.{{TCW|Sabotage (episode)}} As the bombing caused great alarm, Drallig being the head of Temple security, was most concerned at how vulnerable the Jedi Order had become.{{SW|url=explore/the-clone-wars/ep517|text="Sabotage" - ''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide|nolive=1}} Skywalker approached Drallig, who was standing guard with the Temple Guard at the gates of the Jedi Temple, where protesters were demonstrating against the war and the Jedi Order's involvement in it. Skywalker showed Drallig a [[Hologram|holographic]] image of their then-suspect, [[Jackar Bowmani]], and asked the Jedi Master to be on alert for him. This led to the suspect's wife, [[Letta Turmond]], being taken into custody after spotting the holographic image, and the Jedi ultimately learned that Turmond was part of the plot to attack the Jedi Temple.{{TCW|The Jedi Who Knew Too Much}} [[File:CinDrallig-Kanan8.png|thumb|right|250px|Drallig defends younglings from Separatist explosives, aided by two Temple Guards.]] The Temple was later [[Bombing at the Jedi Temple|attacked]] by [[Captain]] [[Rackham Sear]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. During the attack, Drallig led two Temple Guards in securing the quarters of the Jedi [[youngling]]s. He arrived just in time to cut a small explosive drone in half before it detonated in a room with several younglings. He ordered the guards to stay with the younglings and destroy any more explosives that entered the area. Drallig then joined Masters [[Mace Windu]] and Kenobi, reporting to them that the younglings were safe, but that there were explosions throughout the Temple and that the source was unknown. Master [[Depa Billaba]] and [[Jedi Initiate|Initiate]] [[Kanan Jarrus|Caleb Dume]] ended the attack by confronting Sear on the roof of the Temple, where he committed suicide by leaping off the building. ====Fall of the Jedi Temple==== [[File:CinDrallig.png|thumb|264x264px|left|Drallig dueled Darth Vader alongside Padawans Whie and Bene.]] At the end of the war, Skywalker turned to the [[dark side of the Force]] and became Darth Vader, apprentice to [[Darth Sidious]], the [[Dark Lord of the Sith]]. Vader [[Operation: Knightfall|attacked the Jedi Temple]] with the [[501st Legion]] of [[clone trooper]]s, while Sidious issued [[Order 66]] to force the clones to turn against the Jedi Order. Drallig fought to defend the Jedi Temple{{Film|III}} alongside Padawans [[Whie Malreaux]] and [[Bene]], both of whom perished in [[Lightsaber duel|lightsaber combat]] with an enraged Darth Vader. Drallig confronted Vader himself, but proved unable to put an end to the Sith Lord's rampage. ===Legacy=== Shortly after Drallig's death, Masters Yoda and Kenobi returned to the Temple, where they witnessed a security hologram recording depicting Drallig's final moments dueling Darth Vader alongside Padawans Bene and Whie. Sometime after his death, the [[holocron of Cin Drallig]] was sold in an auction on [[Denon]] to the [[noble]] [[Rin Praji]], who kept the holocron safe at [[Rin Praji's estate|his estate]] on [[Kaikielius]].''[[Knights of Fate]]'' ==Personality and traits== [[File:VaderDrallig-TheSecretsOfCloneTroopers.png|thumb|right|275px|Cin Drallig takes a stand against Darth Vader, his former comrade Anakin Skywalker.]] Cin Drallig was a stoic and resolved Jedi Master, a noted leader who presided over the Temple Guard at the Jedi Temple on Coruscant. He stood at 1.74 [[meter]]s tall, or 5 [[Foot|feet]] 9 inches. He had [[Color|dark blond]] hair, blue eyes, and light skin. ==Equipment== Drallig wore classic Jedi robes and boots and kept his hair long. From time to time he had protective gauntlets on his arms and hands. Drallig wielded a single green lightsaber. ==Behind the scenes== For his brief appearance in the [[2005]] film [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], Cin Drallig was portrayed by [[prequel trilogy]] stunt coordinator [[Nick Gillard]], whose name was the [[Tuckerization|basis for the character's name]] (Cin is Nick backwards without the K, and Drallig is Gillard backwards). Drallig later reapeared in [[2013]] in "[[Sabotage (episode)|Sabotage]]," the seventeenth episode of the [[The Clone Wars: Season Five|fifth season]] of the animated television series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'', where he was voiced by [[Robin Atkin Downes]]. For the episode a clay marquette of the character' head was modeled by [[Darren Marshall]]{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/sabotage-episode-guide|text="Sabotage" Episode Guide | The Clone Wars}} and Marshall also created his final model for the episode, which was finished on [[August 2]], [[2011]]. Drallig's model used the previous model of [[Jedi Knight]] [[Ky Narec]].{{WebCite|url=https://dmarshallart.com/portfolio/the-clone-wars-season-5|text=The Clone Wars – Season 5|work=[[Darren Marshall]]'s website|archivedate=20260123054301}} ==Appearances== {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of Cin Drallig}} *{{TCW|Sabotage (episode)}} *[[Kanan 8|''Kanan'' 8]] *{{Film|III}} {{1st}} {{Hologram}} *''[[The Odyssey of Star Wars: An Epic Poem]]'' {{Mo}} ==Sources== *{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/sabotage-episode-guide|text="Sabotage" Episode Guide | The Clone Wars}} *{{SWE|characters|cin-drallig|Cin Drallig}} *{{SWE|groups|jedi-temple-guard|Jedi Temple Guard}} *''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'' *''[[Star Wars Super Graphic: A Visual Guide to a Galaxy Far, Far Away]]'' *''[[Star Wars: Force Collection]]'' *''[[Knights of Fate]]'' *''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]'' *{{InsiderCite|187|Nick Gillard: From Circus to Sith|reprint=1}} *''[[Star Wars: The Lightsaber Collection]]'' *''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Character Encyclopedia - Join the Battle!]]'' *[[Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga – The Official Collector's Edition|''Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga'' – The Official Collector's Edition]] {{Imo}} *''[[Star Wars: The Mini Book of Lightsabers]]'' *''[[Star Wars: The Secrets of the Clone Troopers]]'' *''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' *{{Databank|cin-drallig|Cin Drallig}} *{{Databank|jedi-temple-guard|Jedi Temple Guard}} ==Notes and references== {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |el=Σιν Ντράλιγκ |es=Cin Drallig |fr=Cin Drallig |ka=სინ დრალიგი |ko=신 드랄리그 |pl=Cin Drallig |uk=Цин Дралліґ }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Drallig, Cin}} [[Category:Humans]] [[Category:Individuals with he/him pronouns]] [[Category:Jedi Battlemasters]] [[Category:Jedi Masters of the Jedi Order]] [[Category:Jedi Purge victims]] [[Category:Males]]

''[[Tantive IV]]'', [[Exegol]]''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: Expanded Edition]]'' |species=[[Sullustan]] |gender=[[Gender|Male]]{{Databank|nien-nunb|Nien Nunb}} |pronouns=He/him |height=1.6 [[meter]]s |mass= |hair= |feathers= |eyes=[[Color|Black]]{{Film|VI}} |skin=Tan |cyber= |families=new |parents=new |partners=new |siblings=new |children=new |affiliation=*[[SoroSuub Corporation]]''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded]]'' *[[House of Organa]][[Princess Leia 4|''Princess Leia'' 4]] *[[Sullustan resistance]]''[[Battlefront: Twilight Company]]'' *[[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] **[[Fourth Division]]''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' **[[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gold Squadron]] *[[New Republic]] **[[New Republic Defense Fleet]]{{BuildXWingCite|17|Starfighter Aces}} *[[Coalstreak Squadron]] *[[Resistance]]{{Film|VII}} **[[Red Squadron (Resistance)|Red Squadron]]''[[Poe Dameron: Flight Log]]'' **[["Reb" Squadron]]''[[Star Wars: The Last Jedi: Expanded Edition]]'' **[[Exegol air team]]{{Film|IX}} |masters= |apprentices= }} {{Quote|Only ''you'' could have smuggled an entire ''rescue craft'' under the Empire's noses.|Princess Leia Organa, to Nien Nunb|[[Princess Leia 5|''Princess Leia'' 5]]}} '''Nien Nunb''' {{Pronounced|nēin nənbə|file=NienNunbPronounciation1.flac}} or {{Pronounced|nīn nəm|file=NienNunbPronounciation2.flac}} was a [[Sullustan]] [[Gender|male]] [[arms dealer]] and [[smuggler]] who joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]]. Shortly after the [[Battle of Yavin]], Nunb answered the call from his friend, [[Rebel pilot]] [[Evaan Verlaine]], to help smuggle a group of [[Alderaanian]]s off [[Sullust]] while avoiding detection from the [[Galactic Empire]]; the Empire was searching for surviving Alderaanians after the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|First Death Star]] blew up its first planet, [[Alderaan]]. He went on to further assist Verlaine and [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] in their [[Mission to rescue the survivors of Alderaan|mission]] to unite the surviving Alderaanians, during which time he helped Organa escape from potential Imperial captivity. Only a few [[Standard year|years]] later, Nunb became part of the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance Fleet]] and flew as the co-[[pilot]] for [[General]] [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]] aboard the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'' during the [[Battle of Endor]]. Together, they fought against Imperial forces while attempting to destroy the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station]] in [[orbit]] of the [[Tree|forest]] [[moon]] of [[Endor]]. Their battle was a success, and the ''Millennium Falcon'' fired the shot that destroyed the second Death Star and delivered a devastating blow to the Galactic Empire. Three [[Standard decade|decades]] later, Nunb was a [[starfighter]] pilot with the [[military rank]] of [[Lieutenant Commander]] in the [[Resistance]] and fought in the [[Cold War]], including the [[Battle of Starkiller Base]]. After the [[Battle of Crait]] Nunb was left as one of the few surviving Resistance members and successfully escaped with the remainder of the Resistance. One year later, in [[35 ABY]] Nunb fought in the [[Battle of Exegol|decisive battle]] against the [[Sith Eternal]] piloting the ''[[Tantive IV]]'' alongside [[Urcos Furdam]]. However, during the battle, the ''Tantive IV'' was disabled by [[Darth Sidious]]' massive burst of [[Force lightning]] and Nunb perished. ==Biography== ===Early life=== Nien Nunb [[Homeworld|hailed]] from the [[planet]] [[Sullust]]. He would learn his early [[pilot]]ing skills flying a [[freighter]] for the local [[Sullustan]] [[SoroSuub Corporation]], however, once the company became friendly with the [[Galactic Empire|Empire]], he displayed his opposition by stealing from it on the behalf of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebellion]]. He soon thereafter became an independent ace pilot and an able [[arms dealer]] and [[smuggler]] who owned and operated the [[starship]] ''[[Mellcrawler]]''. He became friends with fellow smuggler [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]], as well as [[Rebel pilot]] [[Evaan Verlaine]]. ===Galactic Civil War=== ====Organa's mission==== {{Quote|Nien Nunb, with stealth and courage you led the Alderaanian survivors off Sullust at great risk of Imperial interception. Thanks to you, we are now in command of a small fleet. Were these not lean days for the throne, a precious medal would have been struck in your honor. As it stands, I am pleased to award you the chalcedony waves from my late mother.|Princess Leia Organa|}} [[File:NunbChalcedonyWaves-PrincessLeia4.png|thumb|left|200px|Organa presents Nunb with the chalcedony waves that once belonged to her mother as a token of gratitude for his assistance.]] Shortly after the [[Destruction of Alderaan|destruction]] of [[Alderaan]] and the [[Battle of Yavin]], [[Alderaanian]] [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] set out with Verlaine on a [[Mission to rescue the survivors of Alderaan|mission]] to unite the few Alderaanians who remained alive in [[the galaxy]]. Their mission brought them to Sullust, where a group of Alderaanians lived in an [[Alderaan Enclave|enclave]] beneath the world's [[Volcano|volcanic]] surface. The Galactic Empire, which used its [[Imperial Military|military might]] to hunt the surviving Alderaanians across the [[galaxy]], discovered Organa and her united forces on Sullust. Nunb answered Verlaine's call for help and smuggled the Alderaanians off of Sullust and into [[Realspace|space]], without detection from Imperial forces. He also provided the arms in his ship to Organa and her people, so they could be used against the Empire. Organa was grateful for Nunb's assistance and presented him with the [[chalcedony waves]] [[necklace]] that once belonged to her adoptive mother, [[Alderaanian monarchy|Queen]] [[Breha Organa]] of Alderaan, as a token of her gratitude. Later in the mission, Organa turned herself over to Imperial [[Commander]] [[Dreed]] on the [[desert]] world of [[Skaradosh]] in exchange for the release of [[Tula]], an [[Imperial officer]] from Alderaan; Tula's sister, [[Tace]], was part of Organa's group of [[refugee]]s and Tula secretly manipulated her sister for information about Organa's whereabouts. Before Organa could be taken captive, the ''Mellcrawler'' arrived to rescue her, with Nunb having slipped the ship onto the planet without the [[orbit]]ing Imperial forces noticing. Verlaine fired on Dreed and his Imperial [[stormtrooper]]s, [[Death|killing]] the commander while Organa and Tula were able to make their way on board. Though Organa thanked him for his efforts, Nunb said that the real test would be making it past the Imperial forces alive. The [[Star Destroyer]] in orbit detected the ''Mellcrawler'' once they received word that Dreed had been killed. Nunb launched a decoy to fool the Imperial vessels, leaving them to follow the [[sensor]] decoy as the ''Mellcrawler'' avoided their detection. The trick was successful and the [[Dreed's Star Destroyer|Star Destroyer]] crew believed the ''Mellcrawler'' had been destroyed, and Organa with it. It was at that moment that a [[Alderaan Flotilla|fleet]] of Alderaanians from [[Espirion]] arrived to assist Organa and her people. The arrival of the [[fleet]] allowed the Alderaanians to destroy the Star Destroyer, and the Alderaanian fleet escaped the wrath of the Empire. Nunb later attended a celebration in which Organa, Verlaine, and their people celebrated the success of the mission to unite them. ====Sullustan resistance==== {{Quote|Memorize the names on display. Nien Nunb, Sian Tevv, Corjentain Malaqua…these are rebels with known ties to Sullust. They are potential infiltrators. They may be smuggling in arms and equipment for a full-on revolution.|An Imperial lieutenant|}} [[File:Sullust_hovering_TIEs.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Nien Nunb's homeworld Sullust was under Imperial occupation]] About three [[Standard year|years]] later, Nunb returned to Sullust on a mission for the Rebel Alliance, in which he led the [[Sullustan resistance]] as they supplied items to members of the [[Cobalt Laborers' Reformation Front]] at [[Pinyumb]]. Shortly after, a [[Siege of Inyusu Tor|battle]] broke out between Imperial and [[Alliance Military|Alliance's]] [[61st Mobile Infantry]] as they took the factory of [[Inyusu Tor]]. As the Sixty-First attempted to leave for the next target in their [[Operation Ringbreaker|operation]], their [[CR90 corvette]] the ''[[Thunderstrike]]'' was shot down and its escort, the [[Braha'tok-class gunship]] ''[[Apailana's Promise]]'', was forced to flee. The Sixty-First was stranded and faced an inevitable attack so its [[Captain]], [[Hazram Namir]], went to Pinyumb to find Nunb and the Sullustan resistance. Namir and his soldiers were attacked and Namir was apprehended by stormtroopers, but Nunb came to the rescue and took Namir to the [[Sullustan resistance safe house]] to meet the others. He asked Nunb for support but Nunb and the others could not help them. The [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Herald]]'' soon arrived to finish the Sixty-First and the ''Apailana's Promise'' came back too to fight it off. The battle went on in the sky and on the ground but the ''Herald'' was forced to retreat due to internal sabotage turning the tide of the battle. Nunb rallied the Sullustan resistance Cobalt Laborers to take Pinyumb as the ground forces began to dwindle at Inyusu Tor. The joint effort caused a planet-wide uprising on Sullust, taking it for the alliance. ====Operation Yellow Moon==== {{Quote|It's good to be wanted.|Nien Nunb on his bounty from the Empire|''[[Moving Target: A Princess Leia Adventure]]''}} [[File:Yellow_Moon_crew.jpg|thumb|left|240px|Nien Nunb participated in Operation Yellow Moon]] Shortly after the [[Battle of Hoth]], Nunb was tasked with [[transport]]ing Organa to a meeting on [[Zastiga]]. On Zastiga, Nunb met with [[Wedge Antilles]] and [[Luke Skywalker]] to discuss reconnaissance tactics. Once [[Operation Yellow Moon]] was approved, Nunb transported the team to the [[Corva sector]]. Upon reaching [[Basteel]], Nunb flew his ship to [[Eladro City]]. His casual piloting through the turbulent atmosphere unnerved [[Kidi Aleri]] but he was able to safely land his ship. Once on the ground, Nunb was given some [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]] by Organa and he headed to a [[Cantina|bar]] to get a drink and some local intel. On the way to the bar, Nunb, Aleri, and [[Antrot]] stopped at a [[Eladro City bazaar|bazaar]]. While the rest of the team climbed out of the [[mountain]] in the tunnels above the [[city]], Nunb returned to his ship so he could pick them up once they were clear. He was detained when the Empire arrived on Basteel and checked out the credentials for all the ships that were present. Once he was cleared, he flew to the top of the mountain and picked up the team. When they were all on-board and safely away from Basteel, Nunb got them hot beverages and [[blanket]]s to help them warm up from the exposure to Basteel's harsh environment. Nunb then flew the team to [[Sesid]]. Once they landed at [[Thrinaka]], he suggested that they purchase tourist [[Clothing|clothes]] to better blend in. After they completed their mission to place a beacon, he warned them not to return to Thrinaka, as stormtroopers were present in the city. He rendezvoused with the team above the planet and flew them to their next destination. After they arrived at [[Jaresh]], Nunb went to see if he could swing a deal with any local [[merchant]]s for a load of the planet's main export, [[fertilizer]]. As they were leaving the planet, Nunb was ambushed by the ''[[Shieldmaiden]]'', which snuck up on his ship from the dark side of the planet. He was able to avoid being snared by a [[tractor beam]] by skimming under a massive commercial freighter that happened to be passing through the [[Star system|system]]. Once clear of the tractor beams, he made the jump to [[hyperspace]]. When they were safe in hyperspace, Organa had a meeting with the team and left them to decide if they wanted to continue with the operation. Nunb found it humorous that if he quit, they wouldn't have a ship to finish the mission, but agreed to stay to the end. Nunb flew the team to the rendezvous at [[Galaan]] and when other starships arrived, he made sure his ship was in position to transmit the tightbeam encryption code directly to them so Organa could contact them. During Organa's speech to the assembled ships, Nunb detected the ''Shieldmaiden'' incoming. He attempted to flee, but was unable to avoid the Star Destroyer's tractor beams and was forced to shut down his [[engine]]s to prevent damage to the ''Mellcrawler''. As the yacht was drawn into the belly of the Star Destroyer, Organa prepared to destroy the ''Mellcrawler'' using the volatile fertilizer Nunb had picked up on Jaresh, which he was hoping to sell elsewhere at a profit. However, when [[Lokmarcha]] stopped her, Nunb instead purged the logs of his ship to prevent any data from falling into Imperial hands. Nunb was captured and [[Prison|imprisoned]] onboard the ''Shieldmaiden''. He was able to free himself when Lokmarcha set off an [[electromagnetic pulse]] that disabled part of the Star Destroyer. He gave directions to Organa so she could lead the surviving members of the team from the detention center to the [[Hangar|docking bay]]. Once in the bay, they were discovered by a squad of stormtroopers and Nunb quickly entered the ''[[Tydirium]]'', an [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle|Imperial shuttle]]. He powered it up and was able to safely escape the ''Shieldmaiden'' with the surviving members of the team. ====Look before you leap==== {{Quote|Those two TIE fighters definitely landed here, right? We tracked them.''"
"''We did, Nien Nunb. To this exact spot. Which is why I told you it's dangerous for us to land here.|Nien Nunb and Shriv Suurgav before discovering the TIEs were destroyed|{{IDWAdventuresCite-2017|issue=7|story=Tales from Wild Space: Look Before You Leap}}}} [[File:Nien_and_Shriv.jpg|thumb|245px|Nien and Shriv during escape of the blue worm species.]] Nunb and the [[Duros]] [[Shriv Suurgav]] tracked two [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE fighters]] to a [[Unidentified planet (Live islands)|dangerous planet]], but they lost sight of the TIEs while entering the [[atmosphere]]. After landing Suurgav insisted that they should first have done a full scan for dangerous life forms. Shortly after, the ground moved and sucked them and the ''[[Mellcrawler II]]'' and droped them into a [[cave]] covered in [[Color|green]] gunk which clogged the starship. They discovered one of the TIE fighters; which was being eaten by [[Unidentified worm species|blue worm creatures]]. Suurgav managed to unclog the starship and later escaped. ====Battle of Endor==== {{Quote|Don't worry. My friend's down there. He'll have that shield down on time. Or this'll be the shortest offensive of all time.|Lando Calrissian, assuaging Nunb's concerns about the Battle of Endor|}} [[File:LandoCalrissiansDeathStarAssault-RotJ40-Prouse.png|thumb|left|220px|Nunb and Calrissian in the cockpit of the ''Millennium Falcon'', just before the Battle of Endor.]] Shortly thereafter, Nunb was a member of the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance Fleet]] and was selected to fly as co-pilot to [[General]] Lando Calrissian aboard the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'' during the [[Battle of Endor]], where he piloted the ''Falcon'' and led the fighter assault to destroy the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|second Death Star]]. Before the battle, when the Alliance Fleet was gathered near Sullust, Nunb expressed concern about the plan of attack and whether General [[Han Solo]], Organa, and their [[Endor strike team|team]] would be able to successfully destroy the Death Star's [[Deflector shield generator|shield generator]] on the [[moon]] of [[Endor]] before the fleet arrived. Owing to Lando's understanding of the [[Sullustese|Sullustan]] [[language]], he personally picked Nunb for the mission, impressed by his exploits aboard the ''Mellcrawler''. Worried about the mission, Calrissian assured Nunb that Solo would have the [[Death Star's shield generator|shield]] down on schedule. The Alliance Fleet arrived over Endor to find that the shield generator was still active, and they realized that the battle was a trap set by [[Darth Sidious]] to destroy the Rebel Alliance once and for all. The fleet remained over Endor and engaged Imperial forces in the hopes that Solo and his team would be able to destroy the generator. The fleet kept to fighting TIE/ln space superiority starfighters and Star Destroyers, particularly once they learned that the Death Star was operational, after previously believing that it did not yet have the use of its primary, planet-destroying [[superlaser]]. Once Solo's team destroyed the shield generator, the ''Millennium Falcon'' entered the Death Star's superstructure and fired the shot that began a chain reaction that led to the [[battle station]]'s destruction. Calrissian and Nunb were in a race against [[time]] as they outran the fireball that their attack created, and they escaped the Death Star just before it was consumed in a massive explosion. The Alliance was victorious, the [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] was dead, and the Empire was shattered. On the surface of Endor, the Rebels held a celebration along with the native [[Ewok]]s, who helped Solo's team destroy the shield. Following the battle, Nunb was awarded a [[medal]] by the Alliance known as the [[Kalidor Crescent]] for his bravery. ===New Republic=== Twenty [[Standard day|days]] after the Battle of Endor, Imperial Captain [[Lerr Duvat]] began [[Operation: Cinder]], a [[contingency]] plan issued posthumously by the late Emperor. Operation: Cinder called for the scouring of Sidious' homeworld, [[Naboo]], with the use of a [[climate disruption array]]. The Rebel Alliance, currently transitioning into the [[New Republic]], quickly deployed a portion of its fleet to defend the planet. Nunb accompanied the fleet aboard his new yacht, the ''Mellcrawler II''. The fleet soon [[Battle of Theed|destroyed]] the Imperial forces, succeeding in the planet's defense.[[Shattered Empire 3|''Shattered Empire'' 3]] Following the revelations of [[Senator]] Organa's [[parent]]age as the biological daughter of [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] in the New Republic's [[New Republic Senate|Galactic Senate]], Nunb sent a message expressing support for his former rebel colleague. Later, he along with several former rebel veterans and New Republic personnel were present at a meeting in the [[New Republic senatorial complex]]'s hangar bay where Leia established the [[Resistance]], a paramilitary organization to protect the Republic.[[Bloodline (novel)|''Bloodline'']] Nunb was among the earliest Rebel Alliance veterans who joined the Resistance, having been stirred by Organa's words.''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]'' ===Service under the Resistance=== [[File:Nien_Nunb_X-wing.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Nunb piloting his X-wing during the Battle of Starkiller Base.]] After joining the Resistance, Nunb offered his support and provided his skills by piloting a [[T-70 X-wing starfighter]] in the [[Resistance Starfighter Corps]]''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: The Visual Dictionary]]'' having the [[Navy|naval]] [[Military rank|rank]] of [[Lieutenant Commander]].''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: New Adventures]]'' He wore flight gauntlets, a pressurized interstellar orange g-suit, and a gear harness, along with a specialized [[flight helmet]] to fit his unique head. His helmet also featured older [[Coalstreak Squadron]] stripes on the upper right-hand side of his helmet, appearing as two, parallel black lines. Nunb was the pilot on a mission led by [[Vice Admiral]] [[Amilyn Holdo]] to steal the head of [[Admiral]] [[Mathieson]]'s [[Mathieson's protocol droid|protocol droid]], which held recordings of every conversation the New Republic Admiral had for the last five years, from the [[space station]] [[Brooksdion Station|Brooksdion]] as proof of [[New Republic High Command]]'s inaction against the [[Cold War|growing threat]] of the [[First Order]]. After the theft, Nunb evaded the [[New Republic Defense Force]]'s [[Rapier Squadron]], led by Commander [[Poe Dameron]].[[Age of Resistance - Poe Dameron 1|''Age of Resistance - Poe Dameron'' 1]] Nunb attended the [[Funeral of L'ulo L'ampar|funeral]] of fellow [[Resistance pilot]] [[L'ulo L'ampar]] at the [[Resistance base]] on [[D'Qar]] after the Duros was killed during a [[Battle in the Fjor system|battle]] with the First Order over a [[Unidentified desert planet|desert planet]].[[Poe Dameron 14|''Poe Dameron'' 14]] ====Battle of Starkiller Base==== When the First Order [[Hosnian Cataclysm|destroyed]] the [[Hosnian system]] with the use of a [[superweapon]], the Resistance base became the next target. Quickly establishing a plan to eliminate [[Starkiller Base]], Nunb, along with eleven others from the [[Starfighter Corps]], left for the planet. Wearing his modified helmet, Nunb flew as ''[[Red Three]]'' on [[Red Squadron (Resistance)|Red Squadron]] with [[RP-G0]],''[[Poe Dameron: Flight Log]]'' an [[R-series]] [[astromech droid]].''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'' During the [[Battle of Starkiller Base|assault]], five Resistance ships were lost before Dameron triggered a chain reaction that caused the weapon to implode. Nunb was one of seven surviving [[X-wing starfighter|X-wing]] pilots who returned, and he celebrated with the rest of the Resistance. ====A brief breathe==== Following the victory at Starkiller Base, Nunb joined other crew and survivors in celebration. With the map to Luke Skywalker, [[Rey Skywalker|Rey]], [[Chewbacca]], and [[R2-D2]] in the ''Millenium Falcon'' left for the planet [[Ahch-To]] while Nunb and a crowd of Resistance personnel waved good luck. With the rush of celebration over, he attended the [[funeral of Han Solo]], who died at Starkiller at the hands of his and Organa's son [[Ben Solo|Kylo Ren]]. ====Evacuation of D'Qar==== [[File:ResistanceBriefing-SWBC62.png|thumb|left|250px|Nien Nunb on the ''Raddus'', listening to Admiral Holdo.]] With the Resistance base's location revealed to the First Order, the Resistance [[Battle of D'Qar|evacuated]] their base and during the ensuing battle above D'Qar, Nunb was stationed aboard the [[flagship]] [[Raddus (MC85 Star Cruiser)|''Raddus'']]. After General Organa was injured, he was present for a briefing in which Commander [[Larma D'Acy]] presented Admiral [[Amilyn Holdo]] as the new fleet commander.{{Film|VIII}} ====Crait==== At the [[Battle of Crait]], Nunb was one of the members of [["Reb" Squadron]], the group of pilots that flew [[V-4X-D ski speeder]]s along the [[salt]] plains of [[Crait]]. He, Rose Tico, Finn, [[C'ai Threnalli]], and squadron leader Poe Dameron were the only members of Reb squadron to survive the assault on the First Order's [[superlaser siege cannon]]. When their lines were broken, an evacuation of the whole of the Resistance took place. After taking heavy losses, Nunb was one of the few remaining Resistance members to escape onboard the ''Millennium Falcon''. ====Aboard the ''Falcon''==== {{Quote|Oh. Hello, Nien.''"
"''Eetuu achaa doo ahmtee vee an…?''"
"''No, no. Be my guest. I have other work to do. And from what I recall, you have as much right to the co-pilot's seat on the ''Falcon'' as anyone.|Leia Organa and Nien Nunb|[[Poe Dameron 27|''Poe Dameron'' 27]]}} Having escaped from the First Order, Nunb met Organa and Chewbacca in the ship's cockpit while the ''Falcon'' traveled into hyperspace. Organa invited Nunb to sit in the co-pilots seat and left the cockpit to him and Chewie, assuring him that he had as much right to sit in the co-pilot's seat as anyone. Chewie and Nunb shared a mutual look of approval with each other before bumping fists. ====Batuu==== [[File:BekAndNunb.jpg|thumb|right|270px|Nunb piloted a Resistance transport with his longtime friend Bek while stationed on Batuu.]] Sometime later Nunb was positioned at the Resistance base on [[Batuu]]. In his time on Batuu, he was tasked with flying the [[Intersystem Transport Ship]] that flew Lieutenant [[Bek]] and his recruits to General Organa's secret location. However, the ship did not make it as they were intercepted by the First Order. Nunb and the rest of the Resistance crew were captured and taken on board the ''[[Finalizer]]'' to be interrogated. However, Poe Dameron arrived with reinforcements, and a [[Battle of Batuu|space battle]] between Resistance starfighters and First Order TIE fighters ensued. The battle helped give Nunb and his crew mates enough time to reach the escape pods of the Star Destroyer and launch safely back to the Resistance base on Batuu.{{GEAttr|Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance|Rise of the Resistance}} ====Ajan Kloss==== {{Quote|There aren't enough of us!|Nien Nunb|}} [[35 ABY|A year later]],''Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary'' dates the events of [[Star Wars: Episode IX The Rise of Skywalker|''Star Wars'': Episode IX ''The Rise of Skywalker'']] to one [[Standard year|year]] after the events of [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']]. As ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates the events of ''The Force Awakens'' to [[34 ABY]], the events of ''The Rise of Skywalker'' must occur in [[35 ABY]]. Nien Nunb continued his allegiance with the Resistance and joined them in their relocation to [[Ajan Kloss]]. Nunb was appointed as the pilot of General Organa's command ship, the recovered blockade runner, ''[[Tantive IV]]'', her former consular vessel, an accolade which he was honored to be the recipient of. Upon receiving the news from a [[Armitage Hux|spy]] within the First Order that Darth Sidious had indeed returned, the Resistance sought to plan their [[Battle of Exegol|decisive offensive]] against the [[Sith Eternal]]. Following the passing of Organa, Nunb attended and spoke at a briefing held beneath ''Tantive IV''. Nunb, alongside his co-pilot, [[Urcos Furdam]], departed from Ajan Kloss in the ''Tantive IV'' with an assortment of fighters to [[Exegol]]. As the legions of [[Xyston-class Star Destroyer|''Xyston''-class Star Destroyers]] immediately engaged the comparatively minute collection of Resistance craft, Nunb and Furdam successfully maneuvered their vessel and were able to slug it out against adversaries multiple times their size while many of their comrades fell to concentrated fire from enemy ships. Shortly following the arrival of [[Citizens' Fleet|reinforcements]] led by Nunb's old friend and former co-pilot, Calrissian, as well as Solo's partner Chewbacca on the ''Falcon'', the mass of [[Force lightning]] hurled into the sky by Sidious disabled the bulk of the Resistance forces, the ''Tantive IV'' included.{{Film|IX}} The lightning kicked off explosions in the vessel, leading to the loss of the ship and Nunb himself, but his sacrifice wasn't in vain as it led to the final defeat of the Emperor and the [[Sith]] and prevented the First Order from combining forces with the Sith Eternal's fleet, the [[Final Order]], so they could establish a new [[Sith Empire]] as well as a massive [[Uprising against the First Order|uprising]] across the galaxy. ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|Nien Nunb is the bravest Sullustan I know.|Daz|{{IDWAdventuresCite-2017|issue=27|story=Ghosts of Kashyyyk, Part 1}}}} [[File:NienNunbT70-SWZ.png|thumb|left|250px|Nunb's T-70 X-wing fighter]] Nien Nunb was a Sullustan male. He had large black [[eye]]s, as well as large [[ear]]s and jowl, and had light skin. He spoke in the liquid-like [[tongue]] of the Sullustan language but was able to speak [[Galactic Basic Standard]] with difficulty. He was considered upbeat and optimistic, and frequently cracked sarcastic, if not anti-climactic jokes. Known for celebrating little victories, his comrades were always upbeat with Nunb's laugh and jokes. Despite his outward appearance of wisecracking jollity, he was extremely dedicated to whatever mission or cause he served, and displayed a loyalty and courage heralded by many of his closest friends. Caring deeply about others, he would go out of his way to provide for those less fortunate than him, and would help his people during the Imperial occupation of his planet as a resistance fighter. ==Skills and abilities== [[File:NienNunb-BaseSeries5.png|thumb|right|200px|Nien Nunb in his pilot gear for the Resistance.]] {{Quote|Nunb can fly anything, in any conditions.|[[Gial Ackbar]]|}} Nunb was an able pilot and smuggler, one who had the skills necessary to often avoid Imperial detection. His piloting abilities led to Calrissian personally selecting him to co-pilot the ''Millennium Falcon'' during the Battle of Endor. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|Nien Nunb is a Muppet, a guy under the deck does his thing. He's got some dialogue to do. He's got this funny, twitchy face. He's a terrific character in my mind.|[[Richard Marquand]], director of ''Return of the Jedi''|''[[The Making of Star Wars: Return of the Jedi]]''}} Nien Nunb made his first appearance in the [[1983]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']]. He was brought to life as both a puppet and as a costumed-actor during the film. For scenes in the ''Millennium Falcon'', Nunb was puppeteered by [[Mike Quinn]]. Nien Nunb's mask wasn't going to be articulated until Quinn suggested that Nunb would be used as a puppet. In the shots with Nunb in the ''Millennium Falcon'', Quinn was wedged underneath the puppet. He layed flat on his back with only a small TV monitor to see what the camera was shooting.{{SW|url=news/much-to-learn-you-still-have-7-things-you-might-not-know-about-sullustans|text=Much to Learn You Still Have: 7 Things You Might Not Know About Sullustans}} He was portrayed by [[Richard Bonehill]] in wide shots. Nunb's name originated from the fact that he was referred to as "Number Nine" on creature packaging.{{Blogspot|subdomain=starwarsinterviews1|url=2010/01/mike-quinn-interview.html|name=Star Wars Interviews|text=Mike Quinn Interview}} The character was voiced by [[Kipsang Rotich]], a [[Wikipedia:Kenya|Kenyan]] student who spoke the [[Wikipedia:Gikuyu language|Kikuyu]] language dialect of Kenya's majority tribe.{{WebCite|url=https://www.csmonitor.com/1983/0728/072823.html|text=In Kenya, audiences roar at language in 'Jedi' film|date=1983-07-28|work=Christian Science Monitor (Compiled From Wire Service Dispatches With Analysis From Monitor Correspondents Around The World)|archivedate=20190811180657}} According to [[Ben Burtt]] however, Rotich spoke in his native language called "Hyah" and some of Nunb's phrases are exact translations of what he was saying, in that language.[[Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide (real-life book)|''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide'']]; note that since there is no language called "Hyah", Burtt perhaps referred to the [[Wikipedia:Haya language|Haya language]], which however is spoken in Tanzania. Rotich was uncredited in ''Return of the Jedi''. Quinn and Rotich returned to the role for the [[2015]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']].{{Facebook|noprofile=1|url=photo.php?fbid=1020510661313136|name=[[Mike Quinn]]|date=October 20, 2015|quote=Well I'm small and blurry and only in a brief moment, but I made the trailer, lol! I'm just to the left of Finn's cheek. You can just make out my large head and black vest ;) Dang I love those new X-Wings!}}{{SW|url=news/the-road-to-rotich-finding-nien-nunb-part-1|text=The Road to Rotich: Finding Nien Nunb, Part 1|nolive=1}} The character later appeared as an animatronic on the [[Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge|''Star Wars'': Galaxy's Edge]] ride [[Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance|''Rise of the Resistance'']].{{WebCite|url=https://techcrunch.com/2019/02/27/how-disney-built-star-wars-in-real-life|text=How Disney Built Star Wars, in real life|author=Panzarino, The silence…solitude… Ah, this is ''beautiful''. I'm in a world all my own. I do not feel alone. ''It's easy to see; I fit perfectly; in this wonderful, beautiful, simp…'' Oh, oh, no, no, no, no, no! I was so happy.|AP-5 reflecting on the peace of space and beginning to sing, before being picked up again|{{Rebels|Double Agent Droid}}}} '''AP-5''', nicknamed '''AP''', was a [[Gender|masculine]] [[RA-7 protocol droid]] who served as an [[Analysis droid|analyst droid]] on a [[Galactic Republic]] [[Venator-class Star Destroyer|attack cruiser]] during the [[Clone Wars]]. At the end of the conflict, the Republic was replaced by the [[Galactic Empire]], and AP-5 was relegated to [[Inventory droid|inventory duty]] aboard the [[Imperial Cargo Transport 241|cargo transport 241]], an [[Class four container transport|Imperial cargo ship]]. In the third [[Standard year|year]] before the [[Battle of Yavin]], AP-5 encountered the [[astromech droid]] [[C1-10P|Chopper]] when the latter hid in the cargo ship while evading several pursuing [[stormtrooper]]s. Tired of being mistreated, the inventory droid befriended Chopper, helping him steal the cargo ship and providing his rebel allies with a suitable [[Atollon|location]] for a secret base. After joining the rebellion, AP-5 continued working as an inventory droid for the [[Phoenix Cell]] at [[Chopper Base]] on the planet [[Atollon]]. Despite his grumpy and sarcastic personality, AP-5 remained loyal to his new rebel masters. During a [[Mission to loot an Imperial cargo ship|mission]] on [[Wynkahthu]], AP-5 played an indispensable role in helping the [[Spectres]] to recover cargo from a derelict Imperial cargo ship. Later, AP-5 along with the [[Lasat]] warrior [[Garazeb Orrelios]] and Chopper helped to stop the [[E-XD-series infiltrator droid]] [[EXD-9]] from reporting their base's location to the Empire. ==Biography== ===Early existence=== {{Quote|I also served in the Clone Wars, as a military analyst on a Republic warship....I was also part of the Ryloth campaign.|AP-5 on his background|}} An [[RA-7 protocol droid]] with [[Gender|masculine programming]], AP-5 was activated some point before the fall of the [[Galactic Republic]]. During the pan-[[The galaxy|galactic]] [[Clone Wars]] that pitted the Republic against the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]], AP-5 served as a navigator{{Databank|ap-5|AP-5}} and a military [[Analysis droid|analyst]] aboard a [[Venator-class Star Destroyer|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]].{{RebelsRecon|Pdz8MeDzolI|#2.18: Inside "The Forgotten Droid" | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/rebels-recon-inside-the-forgotten-droid}} He notably participated in the [[Battle of Ryloth|Ryloth campaign]], in which he estimated the Republic's tactical strategies were only 70% effective. Although the Republic ended up winning the campaign,{{TCW|Liberty on Ryloth}} AP-5's [[commander]] did not survive. ===Age of the Empire=== ====Fall of the Republic==== {{Quote|I was the best Republic navigator in my class, but when the Empire took control, I was downgraded to inventory duty here.|AP-5|}} At the end of the Clone Wars, the leader of the Republic, [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]], unilaterally abolished the regime, [[Proclamation of the New Order|transforming]] it into an authoritarian [[Galactic Empire]]. Although AP-5 had been, according to himself, the best Republic navigator in his class, he was downgraded and reassigned to [[Inventory droid|inventory]] duty aboard [[Imperial Cargo Transport 241|cargo transport 241]], an Imperial [[class four container transport]], serving as a [[quartermaster]]. ===The Rebellion=== ====Joining Phoenix Squadron==== {{Quote|Chopper helped me, and I have chosen to help Chopper.|AP-5 to Hera Syndulla|}} [[File:AP-5.jpg|thumb|left|200px|AP-5 during the Age of the Empire]] [[3 BBY|Three]] [[Standard year|years]] before the [[Battle of Yavin]],''[[Dawn of Rebellion]]'' dates the [[Attack on Phoenix Squadron (3 BBY)|attack on Phoenix Squadron]] to three [[Standard year|years]] before the [[Battle of Yavin]], or [[3 BBY]] according to ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''{{'}} [[Galactic standard calendar|dating system]]. As the heist at [[Horizon Base]] take place immediately before the attack on [[Phoenix Squadron]], it can be determined that it also takes place in 3 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]]. AP-5 encountered [[C1-10P|Chopper]], a feisty [[astromech droid]] who belonged to a group of rebels called the [[Spectres]]. The astromech had been [[Heist at Horizon Base|separated]] from his rebel cell and stranded on [[Horizon Base]], where the cargo transport 241 was docked at the time. Looking for a safe haven from the Imperial [[stormtrooper]]s, Chopper had boarded the cargo ship. During a ship-wide search for the stowaway, AP-5 did not report Chopper's presence to his Imperial superiors, gaining the latter's trust and developing a friendship by telling war stories. When the ship's abusive [[Unidentified Imperial cargo ship captain|Imperial captain]] belittled AP-5, Chopper sprung to his defense and managed to knock out the [[captain]]. The two droids then joined forces to seize control of the ship. After the captain regained consciousness, AP-5 initially managed to bluff him stating that Chopper had taken him as a hostage. Later on, AP-5 aided the rebellion by warning the rebels that the [[Yost system]], their original jump destination, was not safe because an Imperial fleet had already been dispatched there. He instead provided the coordinates of an alternative world called [[Atollon]] which lacked any Imperial presence, making it a more suitable location to plant a rebel base. The captain then realized that AP-5 had betrayed him and shot AP-5 as he was transmitting the coordinates. Despite taking a critical injury, AP-5 managed to send the new coordinates through to the Rebels, but not before being shot a second time. This enraged Chopper, who proceeded to knock the captain out with a flurry of attacks. Before he shut down, AP-5 told Chopper that he would not forget their friendship. Fortunately, after the two droids rendezvoused with the rest of the [[Phoenix Cell]] rejoined the crew of the ''Ghost'', [[Sabine Wren]] managed to repair AP-5, using some parts disassembled from Chopper's stolen ambulatory strut. Immediately upon being restored to working order, AP-5 chided Chopper for not thinking logically, prompting Chopper to reply with a string of expletives. AP-5 retaliated by saying that the words were so foul that the droid would be disintegrated in six systems. [[File:ChopperAP5ChopperBase-MoCB.png|thumb|right|250px|Chopper and AP-5 at Chopper Base]] Using AP-5's information, the Phoenix Cell was able to establish a new base on Atollon called [[Chopper Base]]. AP-5 was placed in charge of checking the cargo that arrived from the base. Used to working with the Empire, AP-5 was unhappy with the frequent delays in rebel shipments arriving at Chopper Base. When the crew of the ''Ghost'' arrived with a shipment of power generators, AP-5 complained that the shipment was already several hours overdue. AP-5 then asked his friend Chopper whether it was routine for rebel shipments to be late; to which the droid answered in the affirmative.{{Rebels|The Mystery of Chopper Base}} ====Homecoming party==== AP-5 was later part of a homecoming party that greeted Kanan, Ezra, and Chopper after they returned from their [[Mission to Malachor|perilous mission]] to [[Malachor]]. He and the Spectres, and Captain [[Rex]] witnessed a blinded Kanan hugging Hera while Ezra exited the starship ''[[Phantom]]'' without former [[Jedi]] [[Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano]], who Ezra and Kanan believed had perished on Malachor.{{Rebels|Twilight of the Apprentice}} ====Rescuing defectors==== {{Quote|We've arranged to insert you into a squad of new cadets headed for Skystrike. AP-5 will prepare fake credentials.|Hera Syndulla to Sabine Wren|{{Rebels|The Antilles Extraction}}}} After the Phoenix Squadron received word that a group of [[Imperial cadet]]s from the elite [[Skystrike Academy]] were planning to defect to the rebellion, AP-5 was tasked with preparing fake credentials for Sabine's [[Escape from Skystrike Academy|infiltration mission]]. ====Mission to Wynkahthu==== {{Quote|"Estimating chance of mission success at 38.5%."
"38.5%? This was your plan!"
"I have factored that in. Without me, your chances are almost zero."|AP-5 and [[Kanan Jarrus]]|{{Rebels|The Wynkahthu Job}}}} [[File:AP5Wynkahthu-TWJ.png|thumb|left|250px|AP-5 and Kanan above Wynkahthu]] Later, AP-5 lent his expertise to a mission undertaken by the crew of the ''Ghost'', the pirate [[Hondo Ohnaka]], and the [[crime lord]] [[Azmorigan]] to steal cargo from an Imperial cargo ship that had become trapped in the atmospheric storms in [[Wynkahthu]]'s upper atmosphere. Due to his experience working aboard a class four container vessel, AP-5 was able to advise the [[Lasat]] warrior [[Garazeb Orrelios]] when planning the mission. AP-5 and Zeb's planned involved jumping onto the hull of the ship, restarting its power plant, and then opening the cargo ramp doors to evacuate the cargo with grappling guns. AP-5 calculated that the mission had a 38.5% chance of success. When Kanan protested, AP-5 responded that they would have a zero percent chance without him. AP-5 stayed with Hera and Kanan aboard the ''Ghost'' while the other rebels, Hondo, and Azmorigan boarded the ship. Despite his careful planning, AP-5 overlooked the fact that restarting the power generator reactivated one of the [[DT-series sentry droid]]s. The sentry droid attacked Azmorigan and Zeb and locked them in the brig. When Zeb contacted the ''Ghost'', AP-5 apologized for his mistake and warned the rebels not to engage the droids. Despite his warning, Azmorigan destroyed one of the droids. This triggered the other sentry droids which attacked the rebels and their confederates. However, they managed to escape the cargo ship before it collided with the vortex and exploded. AP-5 stayed aboard while the rebels celebrated their cache of [[proton bomb]]s and Hondo and Azmorigan left with their [[Ugnaught]] crew member [[Melch]] with their "treasure." ====Strike on Lothal==== After Hera briefed Phoenix Squadron on a planned strike against the [[Imperial Armory Complex]] on the planet [[Lothal]], AP-5 began loading explosives aboard the rebel freighter ''[[Ghost]]''. While he was chatting with his friend Chopper, Sabine arrived with the second load of explosives. Despite AP-5's protestations that they had enough, Sabine insisted on loading more and stressed that she was the weapons expert. AP-5 grumbled about the changes to the supply schedule but compiled with Sabine's orders. When Sabine remarked that AP-5 and Chopper came from the same supply line, Chopper remarked that she needed an attitude adjustment.{{Rebels|Visions and Voices}} ====Defending Chopper Base==== [[File:Zeb_and_company_versus_EXD-9.jpg|thumb|right|250px|AP-5 helping Zeb and Chopper to subdue EXD-9]] Later, AP-5 along with Chopper, the Lasat warrior Captain Garazeb Orrelios, and communications officer stayed behind to guard Chopper Base while the other Spectres and Phoenix rebels departed for a training exercise. AP-5 took advantage of the training exercise to commence a thorough inventory of the base's munitions depot. AP-5 tried to solicit Zeb and Chopper's help but the two were not interested in such mundane work. When Zeb remarked that he did not regard counting crates as fun, AP-5 quipped about teaching the Lasat how to count. Zeb and Chopper then headed to the command center. Later, AP-5 caught them leaving and tried to solicit their help unsuccessfully.{{Rebels|Warhead (episode)}} That evening, AP-5 was lamenting the disorganized state of the depot when Zeb and Chopper arrived with a [[protocol droid]] they had found on the outskirts of Chopper Base. Zeb had taken pity on the "stray" droid and got AP-5 to charge up the droid. Due to the emergency protocol, the protocol droid began to revive quickly and started scanning its surroundings including the depot, Zeb, and Chopper. Impressed, AP-5 decided to take on the stray droid as his inventory assistant. Unknown to the rebels, the protocol droid was actually an [[E-XD-series infiltrator droid]] designated [[EXD-9]]; which had been dispatched by [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn]] to probe the [[Outer Rim Territories]] for rebel bases. Later, AP-5 and Chopper took the protocol droid on a tour of the depot. At that point, Zeb arrived to warn AP-5 and Chopper that the protocol droid was actually an Imperial Infiltrator Droid. Upon hearing the word "rebels," EXD-9 assumed his "attack mode" and attacked the rebels. EXD-9 fought with Zeb, who managed to severe the droid's left hand following a fierce struggle. When AP-5 suggested contacting Hera, Zeb refused because they did not have enough time and vowed not to fail the rebel leader. After finding a wrecked astromech droid that had been drained of its power and stripped of its spare parts, AP-5 cautioned that Chopper was unable to track down the Infiltrator Droid because it was low on power. The three rebels then discussed their plan to capture and disable the Imperial droid. During the discussion, AP-5 advised Zeb against using his [[bo-rifle]] since they were in a munitions storehouse. In the end, Zeb agreed to disable the droid and AP-5 volunteered to help him do so. After Chopper lured EXD-9 out of hiding, Zeb attacked the Infiltrator Droid. Following a fierce struggle, Zeb managed to pin down EXD-9 and AP-5 managed to deactivate him with considerable difficulty. After subduing the intruder, Zeb asked AP-5 about the good news. AP-5 reported that he could not detect any long-range transmissions which meant that EXD-9 had not been able to contact the Empire. When Zeb asked about the bad news, AP-5 informed the Lasat that EXD-9 had activated his self-destruct mechanism. Chopper managed to freeze the droid's timer before it could detonate its proton warhead. Following a discussion with Zeb and Chopper, the rebels decided to send the Infiltrator Droid back to the Empire but with its proton warhead rigged to explode. As part of the plan, AP-5 reprogrammed EXD-9 to its protocol mode and timed the detonator to explode when it connected with the Imperial network. AP-5 then followed Zeb and Chopper as they tracked EXD-9 back to his pod. After Zeb shot EXD-9's long-range [[transmitter]], the trio watched as EXD-9's pod departed into space. AP-5 then began expressing doubts that he had reprogrammed the droid correctly. However, Zeb reassured AP-5 that he done his great job. Despite not being on good terms, AP-5 commended Zeb for his admirable work. In the end, AP-5's plan worked and the rigged EXD-9 destroyed an Imperial Star Destroyer and several other Infiltrator Droids. However, Thrawn was still able to narrow down the search to 94 systems. The following day, AP-5 accompanied Zeb and Chopper as they met up with the other Spectres. When Hera asked what happened, AP-5 claimed he had nothing to do with it; prompting a question from [[Kanan Jarrus]]. At the command center, the rebels were contacted by the rebel source [[Fulcrum]], who commended them for reprogramming the Infiltrator Droid and setting it off to self-destruct. This rebel source was the disillusioned [[Imperial Security Bureau]] [[Agent]] [[Alexsandr Kallus|Kallus]], who had earlier befriended Zeb. When AP-5 began to recount the story, Zeb playfully muffled him while the other Spectres watched in bemusement. ====Rescuing Kallus==== After the rebels discovered that the Empire was monitoring Agent Kallus' Fulcrum transmissions, AP-5 accompanied his friend Chopper and Ezra Bridger on a [[Rescue of Alexsandr Kallus|mission]] to rescue Kallus, who was stationed aboard [[Lieutenant]] [[Yogar Lyste]]'s [[Arquitens-class command cruiser|''Arquitens''-class command cruiser]]. The rebels' plan involved the droids and Ezra stealing a [[Star Commuter 2000]] shuttle from the planet Lothal's [[Capital City spaceport]]. The rebels would then purposely allow their ship to be captured by Lyste and Kallus' light cruiser. The plan worked and Ezra was captured. AP-5 and a disguised Chopper managed to avoid capture by claiming they were unwilling passengers aboard the stolen shuttle.{{Rebels|Through Imperial Eyes}} The rebels' rescue mission was complicated when Grand Admiral Thrawn requested an audience with Kallus and Lyste aboard his [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|Imperial Star Destroyer]] ''[[Chimaera]]''. Lyste insisted on taking Ezra to showcase his success to the Grand Admiral. AP-5 and Chopper managed to convince Lyste to bring them aboard by claiming that Chopper had film footage to use as testimony against Ezra, who claimed to be a [[bounty hunter]]. Once aboard the ''Chimaera'', Chopper alerted the retrieval team members to the change in plans. Kanan instructed Chopper and AP-5 to obtain a new set of clearance codes that would allow them to land on the ''Chimaera''. AP-5 then told the astromech droid that they could only obtain clearance codes from an officer's port. The two droids then argued about whether to rescue Ezra first or to steal the clearance codes. Agent Kallus resolved that argument by freeing Ezra from his cell. After Kallus informed Ezra and the droids that Thrawn was close to locating Chopper Base, AP-5 convinced Ezra and the others to infiltrate Thrawn's office in order to steal the clearance codes. While AP-5 served as a look-out, the other rebels and Kallus infiltrated [[Thrawn's Office]] and completed their objectives. AP-5 witnessed Thrawn and another stormtrooper sentry returning to his office but failed to stop them from reaching the door. Kallus managed to distract Thrawn by reprogramming his Imperial sentry droids into assassins, giving the rebels enough time to escape to the hangar. Following a brief scuffle between Kanan, Rex, Lieutenant Lyste, and [[Governor]] [[Arihnda Pryce]], AP-5 and his rebel comrades managed to escape aboard Kanan and Rex's [[Sentinel-class landing craft|''Sentinel''-class landing craft]]. Kallus opted to stay behind in order to continue feeding information to the rebels and framed Lyste as Fulcrum. However, Thrawn quickly discovered his deception but allowed Kallus to remain undetected in order to find the rebel base. ====Mon Mothma's speech==== AP-5 along with Commander Jun Sato and Captain Rex were present at the Chopper Base command room when the former Imperial [[Senator]] [[Mon Mothma]] gave a live [[HoloNet]] broadcast urging the galaxy to rise up in rebellion against the Empire. ===Alliance to Restore the Republic=== ====Saving Chopper from himself==== [[File:Double_Agent_Droid_thumb.png|thumb|left|250px|AP-5 tries to talk to Wedge in the refresher]] After the formation of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]], AP-5 was given a [[Mission to recover Imperial codes|mission]] by Phoenix Leader Hera Syndulla to steal clearance codes from the [[Killun Station|Imperial Security Bureau station]] on [[Killun 71]]. These clearance codes were needed by the Phoenix Squadron as part of their upcoming raid on Lothal. For that mission, AP-5 was accompanied by his friend Chopper and the rebel pilot [[Wedge Antilles]], who had recently defected from the Empire to the rebellion. During the mission, AP-5 argued with Chopper, who was jealous that the former inventory droid had been allocated the mission. AP-5 was unapologetic and insisted that he would make a better spy due to his programming. This bickering annoyed Wedge, who quickly realized why the other Spectres had not volunteered for the mission. After landing at Killun Station, AP-5 and Chopper disembarked from their stolen ''Sentinel''-class landing craft. The two droids proceeded without incident through an Imperial sensor but Chopper's presence was detected by the crew of an Imperial [[IGV-55 surveillance vessel]]. After some haggling with Chopper, AP-5 proceeded to the base's central computer core alone. There, he was confronted by a female RA-7 protocol droid called [[PZ-7]], who inquired about his presence. AP-5 tartly told her that she had been reassigned to inventory duty and that he was her replacement. AP-5 then easily acquired the clearance codes and found Chopper motionless at a [[network terminal]]. AP-5 thought Chopper was sulking and returned to the ''Sentinel'' shuttle first. In fact, Chopper had been remotely reprogrammed by the Imperial intelligence officers aboard the surveillance vessel. These Imperials wanted to use Chopper to steal the coordinates of Chopper Base. When Chopper rejoined them, AP-5 realized that his friend was acting suspiciously when he cited [[Imperial Code 16]] as an excuse for his inactivity. However, Wedge did not share AP-5's concerns and welcomed Chopper's more pliable nature. AP-5 tried to warn Antilles while the latter was using the [[refresher]] but Wedge thought that the protocol droid was being childish and dabbling in conspiracy theories. Unknown to AP-5, the Imperial surveillance crew were watching his interaction through Chopper's visual processor. Their controller [[Boon|LT-319]] dismissed AP-5 as a threat on the grounds that the protocol droid had undermined his own credibility. Back aboard the ''Ghost'', AP-5's warnings were initially greeted by deaf ears. However, Hera validated AP-5's warnings after she stopped Chopper from downloading the ''Ghost''{{'s}} hyperspace logs. Before they could check Chopper, the reprogrammed astromech droid brought the ''Ghost'' out of hyperspace. When the rebels headed to the engine room to confront Chopper, AP-5 questioned the wisdom of everyone going to the same place. However, Ezra accused him of cowardice and AP-5 was compelled to follow the group. Chopper then trapped the rebels in the ship's cargo bay and attempted to expose them to [[Realspace|zero gravity space]]. After Hera had secured the cargo hold, she dispatched a reluctant AP-5 outside of the ship in order to open the entrance to the hold from outside. AP-5 used his metallic body to navigate through the ''Ghost''{{'s}} hull and reach the maintenance hatch outside. Despite being spotted and attacked by Chopper with [[blaster]]s, AP-5 managed to open the entrance to the cargo hold. Chopper returned for a second loop and pushed him into space. While AP-5 was left floating in space, the other Spectres managed to reprogram Chopper and neutralize the Imperial threat by reversing the data feed back to their ship, destroying the surveillance vessel from afar. [[File:AP5Neebray-DoubleAgentDroid.png|thumb|AP-5 floating through space surrounded by a group of baby neebray]] While floating in space, AP-5 reflected that he should be frightened but that he was strangely calm. As the protocol droid embraced the solitude of silence, he was surrounded by a herd of glowing baby [[neebray]] and he befriended them and began to break into a song. However, his moment was quickly interrupted by the return of the ''Ghost''. Despite his rescue, AP-5 was upset that his solitude had been disturbed and protested that he wanted to stay, but he was nonetheless abruptly scooped up through the freighter's open cargo door. Unaware of the earlier events, AP-5 thought that Chopper was still compromised. This prompted the exasperated astromech droid to slap him and Wedge in the legs. ====Ezra's errant mission==== {{Quote|Ah, AP-5. Yeah, that calculator's working overdrive these days.|A rebel trooper to Ezra Bridger on AP-5|{{Rebels|Twin Suns (episode)}}}} After hearing from [[Kanan Jarrus' holocron]] and the [[Sith holocron (Malachor)|Sith holocron]] that the former [[Sith apprentice]] [[Maul]] was planning to kill [[Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], Ezra produced a faux manifest purportedly from AP-5 delivering munitions to Phoenix Squadron's [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor|A-wing fighters]]. The rebel trooper guarding the airfield was distracted long enough for Ezra to borrow an [[RZ-1T trainer]] and travel to [[Tatooine]] to [[Mission to Tatooine (Imperial Era)|find]] Kenobi. ====Mission to Konkiv==== Wren, Orrelios, Chopper, and AP-5 [[Mission to Konkiv|traveled]] to an [[Imperial listening post (Konkiv)|Imperial listening post]] on [[Konkiv]], based on intelligence that AP-5 provided that stated the base was abandoned. However, upon arrival, they were pursued by a [[Unidentified DT-series sentry droid|DT-series sentry droid]], forcing the rebels to travel further into the base. The four discovered the base was not abandoned at all, being met by an [[Unidentified Imperial admiral (Konkiv)|admiral]] and a squad of stormtroopers. AP-5 masqueraded as an Imperial spy that lured the rebels to their capture, but in reality was aiming to get Chopper connected to the base's database. The sentry droid continued its pursuit, forcing the admiral to take the rebels and AP-5 to the command center. There, the droid caught up to the group and the admiral revealed that the base was largely forgotten by the Empire, so the personnel began a new life for themselves away from the Empire's bureaucracies. Their DT-series [[sentry droid]] lost control of its programming, acting violent and erratic towards its masters, so they had to keep it away from the base. They could not destroy the sentry droid, or else the Empire would be alerted. The admiral ordered his stormtroopers to contain the droid, who along with Orrelios, fought the droid. Wren and AP-5 convinced the admiral to deactivate the droid, so AP-5 could reprogram it before the signal interrupts. Wren promised to keep their secret, in return for Imperial intelligence.{{RebelsMagCite|32|To Thy Metal Heart Be True}} ====Battle of Atollon==== During the [[Battle of Atollon]], AP-5 reported that scanners had picked up Imperial [[walker]]s approaching the western quadrant of Chopper Base. Shortly later, the remnants of Phoenix Squadron and [[General]] [[Jan Dodonna]]'s [[Massassi Group]] fought against Grand Admiral Thrawn's ground forces before retreating into space. AP-5 and the other rebels were surrounded by Thrawn's [[death trooper]]s before they could flee aboard the ''Ghost''. However, an enigmatic being known as [[Bendu]] summoned a storm which gave the rebels a window to escape. After the rebel forces had reached space, AP-5 recommended doing a double hyperspace jump in order to cover their tracks. Rex recommended a third and the rebels traveled to [[Yavin 4]].{{Rebels|Zero Hour}} ====Strike on Lothal==== During the [[Lothal campaign]], AP-5 was present at a briefing at the [[Great Temple|rebel base]] where Syndulla presented a captured [[TIE/D Defender Elite|TIE Defender Elite]] [[flight data recorder]] to the Rebel Alliance leadership including Mothma, General Dodonna, [[Erskin Semaj]] and [[Senator]] [[Bail Prestor Organa|Bail Organa]]. Syndulla also convinced the Alliance leadership to approve a [[Attack on Lothal|strike]] on [[Lothal]] to destroy the TIE Defender factories there.{{Rebels|Crawler Commandeers}} ==Characteristics== {{Quote|Sorry for my delayed response. I was just rather stunned by the fact that you had a good idea.|AP-5, to Garazeb Orrelios|}} [[File:Zeb_and_rebel_droids.jpg|thumb|right|250px|AP-5 and Chopper teaming up with their nominal "foe" Zeb to defeat an Imperial infiltrator droid]] AP-5 had a grumpy''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]'' and pessimistic personality due to his exploitative treatment at the hands of his Imperial superiors. AP-5 prided his service as an analyst droid during the Ryloth campaign and deeply resented being relegated to inventory work under the Galactic Empire. AP-5 had an antagonistic relationship with his Imperial captain, who believed that he was destined for the scrap heap. AP-5 found an unlikely friend in the form of Chopper, an astromech droid who was part of the rebellion. AP-5 gained Chopper's trust and friendship after he removed his [[restraining bolt]]; giving AP-5 the will to defy his master. Despite his friendship with Chopper, AP-5 could still be abrupt and condescending to his friend when he berated Chopper for committing the "illogical act" of sacrificing his stolen [[ambulatory strut]] to repair him. Despite only knowing the Rebels for a short time, AP-5 has already formed an attachment to them, as he seemed saddened to learn of Ahsoka Tano's apparent death. Using his knowledge of Class four container vessels, AP-5 helped the Lothal rebels plan their operation to steal cargo from an Imperial cargo ship. While he was a skilled planner, he was a calculating pessimist who believed that their mission had little chance of success. He also overlooked the presence of sentinel droids aboard the cargo ship and tried in vain to advice the recovery team not to provoke hostilities with the droids. AP-5 was a rigid stickler to the schedule and grumbled when Sabine once insisted on loading more explosives. Due to their similar personalities, Chopper and AP-5 got on well. This led Sabine to once remark that the two droids came from the same supply schedule. AP-5 initially did not get on well with the Lasat Garazeb Orrelios and regarded him as a heavy-lifting grunt. AP-5 could also be caustic towards Zeb and once joked about teaching him how to count. In return, Zeb found AP-5's attention to detail fastidious and long-winded. Later, AP-5 gained a better appraisal of Zeb after witnessing the Lasat's combat prowess against the E-XD infiltrator droid EXD-9. AP-5 displayed team spirit when he helped Ezra and Chopper during a mission to rescue Agent Kallus. AP-5 managed to fool several stormtroopers and Lieutenant Lyste into believing that he and Chopper were unwilling passengers aboard Ezra's stolen shuttle. The Imperials did not suspect AP-5's deception since he was still in the livery of an RA-7 protocol droid. AP-5 used his knowledge of Imperial starships and procedures to help the rebels obtain a new set of clearance codes that allowed Kanan and Rex's landing craft to land on Grand Admiral Thrawn's flagship ''Chimaera''. AP-5 at times could be arrogant and condescending even to his friend Chopper. He once took pride with the fact that he had been assigned by Hera to steal a set of clearance codes from the Empire and took offense that Chopper should be upset. AP-5 annoyed Wedge Antilles by his acidic nature and attention to detail. AP-5 used his guile to convince the inventory droid PZ-7 that he was her replacement and mocked her for believing his ruse. As a rebel agent, AP-5 was a perfectionist who was meticulous with his work. Due to his knowledge of Imperial protocol and his observation skills, AP-5 was one of the first to realize that Chopper had been compromised by the Empire. AP-5 found his moment of solitude with space and befriended a herd of baby neebray. He was upset that his moment of solitude was disturbed by his rescue at the hands of his fellow ''Ghost'' crew. AP-5 was also slow to forgive Chopper for the actions he had committed under his Imperial reprogramming and opined that he was still compromised. This prompted an angry outburst from the exasperated Chopper, who had been through a rough day. ==Equipment== As an RA-7 protocol droid, AP-5 had an insectoid head and a blue metallic body. He had a masculine programming and served as an analyst droid for the Republic and later as an inventory droid for the Empire. Due to his position, he was aware about Imperial fleet movements and star charts. AP-5 used this knowledge to help the rebellion to find a safe haven on Atollon. As an inventory droid, AP-5 was fastidious when it came to details. He also knew how to operate machinery, charge up, and reprogram other droids. AP-5 was also an ingenious tactician who conceived a plan to conceal Chopper Base from the Empire by sending a bomb-rigged EXD-9 to blow up a Star Destroyer. As a former Imperial droid, AP-5 was familiar with the layout of Imperial ships and knew how to obtain clearance codes. Due to his mechanical body, AP-5 was capable of surviving zero gravity space. His metallic body could also double as a magnet for climbing on ships in space. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|He either wants one of two things: stuff to organize, and to be left alone. So I imagine, if he's free floating in the cosmos, he could probably just catalogue all the stars around him and that's his happy place.|Pablo Hidalgo on AP-5|{{RebelsRecon|9LJGjPz2RFc|#3.19 | Inside "Double Agent Droid" | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/rebels-recon-inside-double-agent-droid}}}} AP-5 first appeared in the episode "[[The Forgotten Droid]]" of the [[Star Wars Rebels Season Two|second season]] of the animated series ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' in [[2016]]. He was voiced by [[Stephen Stanton]], who based his portrayal on the late British actor [[Wikipedia:Alan Rickman|Alan Rickman]].{{Twitter|starwars|status/710291710056632321|[[Star Wars]]|date=2016-03-17|quote=It was & @Stephen_Stanton (also the voice of Grand Moff Tarkin) nailed it!}} {{C|in response to: "The new droid character on #StarWarsRebels sounded like his voice was inspired by Alan Rickman"}} Stanton identified the voice acting process for the droid as different than for other characters as he would often only act alone opposite to the sound effects of Chopper. AP-5 is named after producer [[Athena Yvette Portillo]], and his name also references her height. His design was meant to be a little more unique and as such he was based upon the original concept art for the "[[Death Star]] Droid" created by [[Ralph McQuarrie]] for the [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|original ''Star Wars'' film]], that would later evolve into the RA-7 droids in the film, but with the proportions of the ''Rebels'' version being closer to the original sketch. {{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/the-forgotten-droid-trivia-gallery|text="The Forgotten Droid" Trivia Gallery}} AP-5's animation model was designed by [[JP Balmet]] and finished on [[March 11]], [[2015]].{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/the-forgotten-droid-concept-art-gallery|text="The Forgotten Droid" Concept Art Gallery}} The writer's consciously tried to make the relationship dynamic between Chopper and AP-5 distinct from the one between [[R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO]]. In the [[Rebels Recon]] episode for the [[Star Wars Rebels Season Three|third season]] episode "[[Double Agent Droid]]", series creator [[Dave Filoni]] explained that AP-5 left the Empire because they were going to turn him into scrap and that he tolerated the rebels, but suffered under their lack of organization an structure and in some ways, he would just like to float alone in space until his battery died. He also said that in his euphoric moment, he began to sing without even necessarily realizing it. Stephen Stanton similarly pointed out that AP-5 was annoyed because the rebels were ignoring him throughout the entire episode and that he as such would possibly prefer the solitude. Brand manager [[Pablo Hidalgo]] explained that AP-5 only ever wants to organize things and to be left alone, and that as such he would would likely be very happy floating in the cosmos and cataloguing all the stars around him. AP-5's singing moment in the episode had been part of the script and Stanton had asked Filoni if he was sure about it, with him replying "Why not?". Filoni later clarified that the encounter with the neebrays and song was intended to give a funny and bizarre light-hearted ending to a "filler episode."
