After taking R5 back to the fighter, Djarin took Grogu with him to Sundari's [[Civic Center]]. Together, they ventured past the center and into a well. As they searched for the mines, Djarin found a Mandalorian helmet. He was then captured by a [[Spider Tank]] piloted by a [[Cyborg mech]]. Djarin told Grogu to get back to the fighter and get help. Sometime later as the mech prepared to drain Djarin's blood, Grogu returned with Lady Kryze. Krzyed saved Djarin and freed him after she killed the mech. After he was given soup from Kryze, Djarin and Grogu were taken to the mines by Kryze. There, she showed them the mines and told them how her father and the Royal family attended her [[Mandalorian initiation ritual|initiation]] and watched her with pride as she took the creed. Djarin undo took the initiation and redeemed himself. Unfortunately, he walked too close to edge of the shallow water and fell into a trench. As Kryze saved Djarin, she saw a [[Mythosaur]]. Djarin, however, was saved but did not see it. He recovered and took a flask of the Living Waters with him as he, Grogu and Kryze left the mines. Djarin and Grogu were taken back to Kalevala by Kryze to their ship at her [[Kryze Fortress|Fortress]]. Unfortunately, they came under [[Bombing of Kryze Castle|attack]] by several [[TIE/IN interceptor|TIE Interceptors]]. Djarin, Grogu and R5 were able to return to their fighter. He was able to shoot down several of the interceptors and protect Kryze.However, they were unable to stop the [[TIE/sa tactical bomber|TIE bombers]] from destroying the Fortress.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 19: The Convert}} ====Return to the Covert==== After Kryze destroyed one of the bombers, Djarin convinced her to retreat with him when more TIEs arrived. Together, then went to the [[Armorer's planet|planet]] where Children of the Watch's [[Mandalorian secret covert|covert]] and the Tribe were. As they landed their ships, Djarin told Kryze to keep her helmet on her due to the Covert's adherence to the ancient Mandalorian way. They were approached by [[Paz Vizsla]], who was skeptical of their claim of reaching the Mines and bathing in the Living Waters. However, the Armorer believed their claims when Djarin showed her a flask that contained a sample of the living waters. Djarin was told that he and Kryze had been redeemed in the living waters. Djarin and the rest of the covert allowed to stay and live as her ancestors did. Djarin allowed Grogu to train with the other Foundlings. He watched as Grogu used [[Mandalorian training darts|training darts]] during a practice match with [[Ragnar Vizsla]]. After Grogu won the match, a [[Reptavian]] [[canyon raptor]] attacked. Djarin tried to shoot the raptor but Paz did not want to harm Ragnar. Djarin, Paz and several others attempted to go after the raptor but ran out of fuel. Djarin, along with Kryze, Paz, and the [[Shriek-hawk Training team]] went after the raptor on foot from [[Gauntlet (Bo-Katan Kryze)|Kryze's starfighter]] to [[Rescue of Ragnar Vizsla|rescue]] ragnar. Together, they scaled the cliffs to the raptor's nest. When they got to the nest, Djarin detected three raptor chicks. As Paz rescued Ragnar from the the raptor and it's chicks, Djarin fired his cables at the raptor. With help, Djarin, kryze and the team were able to force it down and it was eaten by the lake monster. Djarin and Paz attended to Ragnar. Djarin and the others returned to covert with the raptor chicks in tow. Djarin and the covert were then approached by Captain Teva, who learned of their location from R5. Djarin was shown a message from Magistrate Karga asking for help in reclaiming Nevarro from [[Gorian Shard]] and [[Gorian Shard's pirate crew|his crew]]. Djarin was able to convince Vizsla and the others to let him go due to him letting him go once before. Djarin believed Teva's warning about the [[Imperial holdouts|Imperial remnants]] growing, and that Karga needed their help. However, Kryze that she would need help in fighting Shard's pirates. Djarin spoke with the covert about helping Karga and Nevarro's citizen, despite their brief fight with Karga's hunters and Imperials. Despite their hesitation, Paz and the rest of the covert decided to support Djarin and Kryze in fighting Shard's pirates and relocating to Nevarro. ====Uniting the Mandalorians==== Afterward, seeking to united the Children of the Watch with [[Mandalorian resistance|Kryze's former unit]], Djarin and Grogu travelled with Bo-Katan to the planet [[Plazir-15]]. They travelled to its central city, contained within a dome, and met with its rulers [[Captain]] [[Bombardier (individual)|Bombardier]] and [[the Duchess]]. Kryze requested to see the Mandalorians, whom the royals had hired as mercenaries as an organized military was illegal on the planet according to the [[Charter of the New Republic]] due to Bombardier's Imperial past. The royals told them they would allow them to see the Mandalorians if they take care of the malfunctioning [[battle droid]]s on their planet, which, despite being reprogramed to serve, had attacked humans and vandalized the city. They explained that the Charter prevented them from using the mercenaries to deal with the problem, as standing armies were not permitted to enter the city. Their constables could not carry weapons. Kryze and Djarin, however, were allowed to enter as it was reasoned that they did not qualify as a militia and, as weapons were considered part of the Mandalorian religion, it would be discrimination to take them away. In addition, should they complete the task, Plazier-15 would recognize Mandalore as a sovreign system if Kryze retook it and petition the New Republic to adopt this stance. Kryze and Djarin agreed and went to visit [[Commissioner]] [[Helgait]], head of the planet's security.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 22: Guns for Hire}} There, Helgait explained that, though a failsafe switch was existed to shut off all droids, as Plazier-15 was the Galaxy's only direct democracy, the people voted against using it, as the droids took care of all work for them, meaning they'd have to end their permanent period of leisure. Kryze asked for a list of rogue droids and Helgait told them to speak to the Ugnaughts in the planet's lower levels. There, Kryze asked about the droid malfunction but alienated the Ugnaughts by accusing their droids of malfunctioning. Djarin, having experience with the culture of the Ugnaughts through Kuill, effectively communicated with them and got them to hand over the list. The Ugnaughts indicated that it was likely the next malfunction would occur at the loading docks. The Mandalorians travelled to the loading dock and Djarin discovered the malfunctioning droid by attacking them until one [[B2-series super battle droid|super battle droid]] retaliated and fled. After a long chase through a city street, Kryze shot the droid and discovered a [[spark pad]] for [[The Resistor]] bar, which the Mandalorians took as their next lead. They interrogated the barkeep and discovered that the malfunctioning droids all drunk from the same batch of [[Nepenthé]], a substance consumed by droids which reprogrammed them, usually delivering the latest update. They took the remains of the super battle droid to a [[Unidentified lab tech (Plazir-15)|lab technician]] who informed them of [[nano-droid]]s in the Nepenthé. Together, they discovered a chain code, pointing to Helgait as the one who introduced the droids. The Mandalorians confronted the security chief who revealed himself as a Seperatist, believing both the Republic and Empire to have been corrupt. Kryze stunned Helgait and brought him before the Duchess and Bombardier. Helgait was exiled and the Mandalolrians were given an audience with Kryze's old unit. [[File:EnterDjarin-CH22.png|thumb|right|250px|Kryze, Woves, and Djarin on [[Plazir-15]]]] There, Kryze discovered [[Axe Woves]] had taken over leadership. She challenged Woves to a formal duel and Kryze emerged victorious, though she did not kill him, remarking that enough Mandalorian blood had been spilled. Kryze attempted to take control of the unit but they were resistant, as the Darksaber remained in the hands of Djarin, who they viewed as a Zealot. Djarin told the Mandalorians that, while exploring the planet Mandalore, he had been captured by an alien who took the Darksaber from him. Kryze saved him and fought with the Darksaber meaning, by technicality, she was its rightful owner, saving them from having to duel to the death. Woves and the Mandalorians accepted Kryze as Mandalore's ruler. Djarin handed the Darksaber to Kryze, who ignited it. ===Retaking Mandalore=== ====Scouting and capture by Gideon==== {{Quote|I only know of this weapon what you taught me. To be honest, it means nothing to me or my people. Nor does station or bloodline. What means more to me is honour. And loyalty. And character. These are the reasons I serve you, Lady Kryze. Your song is not yet written. I will serve you until it is.|Din Djarin|{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 23: The Spies}}}} Djarin and Kryze, along with the members of Woves' party, flew back to Nevarro and introduced them to the Children of the Watch who, despite skepticism, treated them civilly. High Magistrate Karga approached Djarin and gifted Djarin a bottle of wine from [[Coruscant]]. They walked back to his office and Karga gifted him [[IG-12]], a droid built from the chassis of IG-11, lacking a memory circuit, to act as a mechanised walker suit for Grogu. Djarin believed Grogu was too young to operate it but the child used the voice function to repeated "no". While walking down a street of Nevarro, Grogu ate some food and crushed a melon from a market, as he did not understand the concept of currency. Later that night, the combined Mandalorian forces met for a feast and it was decided that a recon party would be sent to scout the surface of Mandalore and search for the [[Great Forge]]. Djarin and Grogu, Woves and Koska Reeves, Paz Vizsla, the Armorer and others volunteered to join the scouting team. The next day, the Mandalorian fleet travelled to Mandalore and the scouting party landed on the planet. After briefly scouting, they spotted a [[Langskib]] approaching them, which they soon discovered was manned by [[Mandalorian survivors]], still loyal to Kryze, who had continued living on the planet following the Purge. They joined the survivors in their ship and Kryze explained how she surrendered to the Imperials, as she was promised they would spare further Mandalorian killings, losing the Darksaber to Moff Gideon in the process of laying down her arms. Privately, Djarin admitted to Kryze that he initially believed she had forsaken the way and that she was selfish and uncaring but grew to value honour, loyalty and character above all else. He pledged to serve her until her "song is [...] written". On board the ship, a brawl broke out between Vizsla and Woves after the latter called the former a "primitive". Grogu stopped the fight in IG-11 and Kryze told Djarin he taught him well. A gigantic [[trinitaur]] smashed the langskib and the Mandalorians continue on through a cave. After discovering the Great Forge, the Mandalorians were ambushed by Imperial troopers, wearing jetpacks and Beskar armour. A gun battle ensued and Vizsla covered Woves, who escaped the cave in his jetpack to inform the fleet and bring reinforcements. The Mandalorians followed as the [[Imperial Armored Commando]]s retreated and they discovered an Imperial base. There, Djarin was trapped, separated from the other Mandalorians by a blast door. Djarin fought against troopers but, after being restrained by three [[fibercord whip]]s, he was brought down. Moff Gideon revealed himself, wearing next-generation [[Dark Trooper]] armour and a Mandalorian-style helmet. He explained his intention to create a perfect army, comprising the best aspects of the [[Clone trooper|Clones]], [[Jedi]] and Mandalorians, before sending off fighters to destroy the fleet, declaring that the Purge of Mandalore would soon be complete. He ordered for Djarin to be taken away. Kryze cut a hole in the door and escaped with the other Mandalorians, sans Paz Vizsla, who sacrificed himself to hold back the Imperials, dying by three [[Gideon's Praetorian Guard]]s. ====Mandalore reclaimed==== {{Quote|Mandalorians are weak once they lose their trinkets.''"
"''Mandalorians are stronger together.|Moff Gideon and Bo-Katan Kryze|{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 24: The Return}} }} As Djarin was escorted by troopers, he broke free and engaged in a fight with them. One of the troopers wrapped his wire around Djarin's neck but was stopped from killing him by Grogu. Djarin thanked the foundling and resolved he would have to defeat Gideon or else their battle would never end. Using his comlink, he spoke to Kryze and informed him of his plan to take on Gideon. Kryze told him the Mandalorians were under attack and she had to get them to safety. Djarin contacted his droid, R5-D4 and asked him to infiltrate the base and find the location of Moff Gideon's command centre. The droid was successful and beamed the plans of the base to him. He ordered Grogu to stay close and headed towards the command centre. [[File:DinDjarinvsPraetorianGuard-Displate.png|thumb|left|250px|Djarin fighting Praetorian Guards on Mandalore]] Djarin, weaponless, discovered the command centre was blocked by a series of shields. He asked R5 to deactivate them on his command. The Mandalorian fought his way through in a tough battle and discovered the Gideon's laboratory, full of clones of the Moff. Djarin used the controls to cause the tanks to explode and the water inside to escape, wrecking the incubation of the clones and rendering them useless. Djarin entered the command centre and tried to shoot Gideon, who was furious at the Mandalorian's tampering with the clones. The blasts bounced off Gideon's beskar armour and Djarin charged forward with a jetpack he procured from one of the troopers. Gideon hurled him aside and the two fought hand to hand. Gideon gained the advantage, as his Dark Trooper armour granted him superhuman strength. Gideon's [[Praetorian Guard]]s attacked the Mandalorian and, before they could kill him, Grogu walked in and said "no" with IG-12. The Praetorian Guards focused their attention on Grogu and walked toward him. Djarin tried to stop them but Gideon used his cord to topple him. The Moff pinned the Mandalorian and, as he was about to finish him off, Bo-Katan arrived and freed him, engaging in combat with Gideon using the Darksaber. She encouraged him to stop the Praetorians before they killed Grogu. [[File:GideonsLastStand-Displate.png|thumb|right|250px|Kryze, Grogu, Djarin, and Gideon, shortly before the latter's death]] As Kryze dueled Gideon, Djarin saved Grogu and he fought against the Praetorian Guards with the foundling. As Gideon gains the upper hand, crumpling the Darksaber, Djarin shot Gideon with his new blasters and Gideon stumbled back toward the edge. Grogu used the force to cast his [[electrostaff]] into the pit and, at this moment, the Mandalorian Capital Ship, which Woves had programmed to crash into the Imperial Base, collided with the walls, creating a gigantic explosion. Gideon was engulfed in flames but Grogu created a force barrier around himself, Kryze and Djarin, who survived. ===Adopting Grogu, taking on work for the New Republic and living on Nevarro=== {{Quote|Let it be written in Song that Din Djarin is accepting this foundling as his son. You are now Din Grogu, Mandalorian apprentice.|The Armourer|}} [[File:Ragnar_creed.png|thumb|left|250px|Djarin watching Ragnar swear the Creed once more, in the living waters of Mandalore]] Later, the Mandalorians officially retook Mandalore. Ragnar swore the creed in the true living waters of Mandalore and Djarin proposed to the Armourer that Grogu be promoted from foundling to apprentice. The Armorer repeated that this was impossible due to Grogu's inability to speak. He asked whether he this would be possible with parental permission and the Armorer confirmed this. Din Djarin adopted Grogu as his own and the Armorer dubbed him "Din Grogu", an apprentice. She encouraged him to continue questing offworld and grant his apprentice the experiences his own master granted him. [[File:Din_Djarin_Carson_Teva_Din_Grogu_MandoS3.png|thumb|right|250px|Djarin, Grogu, and Teva at Adelphi Base]] Djarin and Grogu flew to Adelphi Base and offered his services hunting Imperial warlords and other New Republic business on a case-by-case basis to Carson Teva in the base's bar. He wished to take on more savoury missions now that Din Grogu was his apprentice. Teva knew this would not be approved by the Republic but agreed to keep it secret. Djarin asked for an advance payment of the head of an IG droid above the bar and Teva agreed. [[File:Grogu-Mando-Home-CH24.png|thumb|left|250px|Grogu and Djarin at their cabin on Nevarro]] Djarin brought the assassin head to the Anzellans on Nevarro, who used its parts to repair IG-11. In the town square, Karga thanked Djarin for his help in repelling the pirates and gifted him the deed to a cabin outside the town. Djarin thanked him and told the High Magistrate he too had a gift. Djarin presented the restored IG-11 to Karga to act as Marshal of Nevarro, a role Djarin had previously rejected. Later, Djarin and Din Grogu relaxed in their new cabin. The Mandalorian watched as his apprentice used the force to levitate a frog. Following these events, the two would continue their adventures together.''[[The Mandalorian: The Adventures of Din Djarin]]'' ====Hunting Barro==== {{Quote|You know, it's better if you bring him in alive. You see, you catch the bad guy and they tells us where the other bad guys are.''"
"''Things went a little sideways.|Garazeb Orrelios and Din Djarin|''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu]]''}} [[File:MandoFlamethrowerSnowtroopers-TheMandalorianAndGrogu.png|thumb|right|250px|Djarin fighting Barro's troopers in the warlord's base of operations]] Years later, around [[14 ABY]],{{MandoDate|MandalorianAndGrogu}} Djarin was contracted to accompany [[Garazeb Orrelios]] on a [[Attack on Barro's Imperial remnant|mission]] take down the Imperial Warlord [[Barro]]. Djarin tracked a group of [[Cold weather assault trooper|snowtroopers]] to [[Phostera]], and undertook an attack on the [[Phostera Imperial base|base]]. Djarin fought his guards and Barro escaped before he could enter the Warlord's office. The landowners, who were pressured into paying tribute to Barro, pointed Djarin to the elevator shaft and the Mandalorian followed him down but was stopped by several snowtroopers. In response Djarin dropped a grav charge, killing them. Outside Grogu destroyed a [[polar mouse droid]], but hid when a Imperial Remnant AT-RT Driver arrived. As the trooper left his All Terrain Reconnaissance Transport, Djarin used the walker to kill the driver before telling Grogu to get on. Driving the smaller walker, Djarin sees that Barro escaped into an AT-AT. Djarin managed to destroy the two walkers behind it; using two grav charge to destroy one of Walker 3's legs, causing it to fall from a cliff and destroyed the second one, killing the crew before breaching the hatch. On the front walker, Djarin killed both the AT-At pilots, kicking them both off and using his flamethrower. But after getting in he sees Barro piloted an [[escape pod]] out of the walker. Djarin discovered he set the walker's [[autopilot]] and primed a set of [[Bomb|explosives]] to destroy the vehicle but Djarin aimed his rifle, trying to shoot down the [[INT-4 Interceptor]]. Grogu encouraged him to hurry by tapping his helmet but Djarin held the walker's target sight and used the [[Laser cannon]]s to shoot the pod which made it crash into a mountain and explode, killing the Imperial Warlord. The Mandalorian and his apprentice escaped the walker via jetpack just before the explosion reached them. They rendezvoused with Zeb in his [[UT-60D U-wing starfighter/support craft|U-wing]] and flew back to Adelphi Base. As they came back Zeb was disappointed he didn't get Barro alive so he can tell them where the other bad guys are, which Djarin explains there were complications. ===Conflict with the Twin Hutts=== ====Task from the twins==== [[File:Din_Djarin_and_Grogu_meeting_with_Ward.png|thumb|left|250px|Djarin and his apprentice meeting with Colonel Ward at Adelphi Base]] When they returned, Djarin met with [[Colonel]] [[Ward]] who, despite being appreciative of his work, called his extraction messy, as Barro was worth more alive than dead due to the information they could have gained. Djarin asked whether this meant his pay would be withheld and Ward responded "you're getting paid alright. Come with me." Ward gave the Mandalorian a new Razor Crest, which they procured from the collection of a captured Imperial Commandant, as both payment for his last mission an advance on his next mission. Ward informed him the mission entailed visiting [[the Twins|the Twin Hutts]] on [[Nal Hutta]], who, in exchange for the Mandalorian's rescue of [[Rotta|Rotta the Hutt]], their nephew, promised to give them them information on the whereabouts of [[Commander]] [[Janu Coin|Coin]], a mysterious Imperial remnant who the New Republic had next to no information on. Djarin was hesitant on working for the Hutt [[gangster]]s, who were crime lords, but Ward reassured him he was still working for the New Republic and, if he did not accept, she had nothing else for him. Zeb, Djarin and Grogu boarded the Razor Crest and they flew to Nal Hutta. They arrived and, escorted by two [[HH-87 Starhopper|HH-87 Starhoppers]] flown by two of the [[Droid Gotra]] [[sentry droid]]s hired by the Hutts, landed once he tells the droid pilots that he is requesting clearance from the Twins. With Grogu, Djarin entered the Twins' palace, passing by many droids and Hutts in many rooms. Djarin explains to Grogu that the Hutts have been head of criminal enterprises for thousand of years using violence and treachery to maintain control. He warns Grogu that while htye may be their guest they are not safe. Passing by two large droids at the throne room, the Twins greeted the Mandalorian, happy he is working for them, but Djarin tells them he is working for the New Republic and he is told he can lead him to the Imperial fugitive Commander Coin. The Hutts explained to him that Rotta was being held captive on the planet [[Shakari]] and showed him an image of Rotta as a child, as he had not been seen in a long time. Djarin departed and flew to the planet. Zeb explained to him that, as they were operating outside New Republic territory, back-up could not be called should things go awry. Djarin taught Grogu the right way to wear his armour. ====Search for Rotta the Hutt==== {{Quote|No-no-no. No-no-no-no-no-no-no. I don't want your credits. Cause I didn't give you any information.''"
"''His name is Rotta.''"
"''[Chuckles]''"
"''Something funny?''"
"''Yeah, yeah. Everybody, everybody, knows Rotta the Hutt. That guy's a monster.|Hugo Durant and Din Djarin|}} [[File:Hugos_frycooks.png|thumb|right|250px|Djarin probing fry cook Hugo Durant for information on Rotta the Hutt]] Once on the surface, Djarin bought food for Grogu from the [[Ardennian]] [[fry cook]] [[Hugo Durant]] and asked him for the location of a Hutt, offering a generous sum of credits. Durant was initially hesistant but took the credits once he mentioned he was searching for Rotta. He chuckled and remarked "everybody knows Rotta the Hutt. That guy's a monster" before pointing out a poster advertising a gladiator match he was participating in. Djarin and Grogu spectated Rotta's game, and found he was fit for a Hutt. Rotta dominated a human gladiator in battle before crushing him with his weight. Afterward, Djarin visited Rotta in his living quarters, a prison cell. Rotta explained he did not need rescuing as his next match was the last in his contract: after that, he would be free. Djarin asked Rotta who he was indebted to but Rotta ignored him and asked if he could feed Grogu. Djarin permitted him to and Rotta told him it was [[Lord]] [[Janu Coin|Janu]], leader of all syndicates on Shakari's moons. Rotta insisted, despite the cage, he was treated well and his battles had granted him a great following which he could use to make a living following his release. Grogu approached Rotta but the Mandalorian ordered him to heel. Rotta feed Grogu some more and reassured Djarin, telling him he was nothing like his father, [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure|Jabba the Hutt]], the infamous crime boss of Tatooine. He told Djarin that people feared Jabba but respected him for his prowess in battle and it was the first time he did not live in the shadow of his father. For these reasons, Rotta told Djarin he did not need to be rescued and the Mandalorian left with his apprentice. [[File:Salt_Bar.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Djarin and Grogu in the Salt Bar]] Djarin returned to Durant and asked him where to find Lord Janu. Durant closed his shop window but Djarin entered the stall and asked the worried fry cook again. Durant told the Mandalorian that nearly every vendor on the planet paid Janu protection and, when pressed for a collection location, Durant told him one of the many locations the protection money was collected at was the [[Salt Bar]] under [[Korvin Station]]. Djarin flicked him a credit, as Grogu had eaten some of his food, and travelled by train to the salt bar. Djarin met one of Janu's subordinates named [[Hogsbreth]] and asked for Janu. Hogsbreth encouraged him to walk away but Djarin did not relent, leading to a brawl in the bar between him and most others present. The Mandalorian emerged victorious, shooting off one of the [[Iktotchi]]'s [[horn]]s off and holding him at blasterpoint before Janu appeared and invited him into his office. Djarin asked to buy out Rotta's contract for a bag of New Republic credits but Janu refused. He told Djarin that he had gathered the creatures from [[Dejarik]], a holochess game where each of the pieces was a certain creature, and would pit them against Rotta in a match in Rotta's final match, in which he would surely perish. Janu gave the credits back and told Djarin to bet them on Rotta's death and gave him a chunk of [[salt]] to settle the bar fight. In exchange, he asked that the Mandalorian consider fighting for him, a prospect which would bring in many spectators. Djarin left his office, dunking and therefore dissolving the salt in Hogsbreth's drink. [[File:Rotta_v_Din_in_the_Pits.png|thumb|right|250px|Djarin fighting Rotta the Hutt in the Pits]] Djarin returned to Rotta and told him Janu would continue bringing in opponents in the match until Rotta was killed. Rotta asked why he should believe him, as he worked for the Twins. Rotta believed the Twins wanted him dead as he was heir to Jabba's throne, despite Rotta wishing to distance himself from the life of crime led by Jabba. He told Djarin that, initially, the crowds wanted him dead but soon began to cheer for him, recognising him as a skilled warrior and unlike his father in personality. Djarin told Grogu that fighting wasn't a sport but a last resort and opened the cell, asking Rotta to come with him. Rotta alerted the guards and gas was released into the cell block, rendering Djarin and Grogu unconscious. Grogu was taken as a pet by Janu and the Mandalorian would be put in a cell, forced to compete in the match. Djarin entered the arena and attempted to reason with Rotta but the Hutt attacked. Djarin took up arms but still tried to convince Rotta he was here to rescue him. Eventually, Djarin had Rotta at his mercy and, though the crowds cheered, encouraging him to kill the Hutt, Djarin dropped his weapon and yielded, letting Rotta win. Janu declared "Rotta the Hutt has won. Now he is free... to die!" before releasing the Dejarik creatures. Djarin threw Rotta an battle [[axe]] and proposed working together. He agreed and the two battled the creatures. Using a sword and axe, Djarin battled a [[Monnok]] gladiator, kicking the creature down before throwing his axe at a [[Ghhhk]] attacking Rotta, as Rotta defeated a [[Molator]] gladiator with Djarin pushing the Molator down. As Rotta fights a [[Kintan strider]], Djarin gets bitten by a Houjix who elecoluted him. Recovering from his bitten arm, a [[Ng'ok]] comes at him from behind and attempts to eat him but his beskar helmet protected him, with Rotta grabbing the Ng'ok when the Molator gladiator came and pinned him. Cutting the Molator's tentacle, the Kintan strider comes back and clubs him, but his armor protects him and a [[Mantellian Savrip]] grabs the Kintan strider and throws it to the ground. Battling the Monnok gladiator, Djarin stealing its [[staff]] and throws a sword at a charging Molator. Battling the Ng'ok gladiator, Djairn soon broke off the fight to help Rotta, dodging the Mantellian Savrip's attack and saving Rotta by running up the Hutt, Djarin uses the Monnok staff to choke hold the creature before the Kintan strider knocks them both down. to until Rotta threw a [[Houjix]], an electrified monster into an electric fence, short-circuiting the arena. Janu and Hogsbreth fled and the creatures began crawling into the stands. Djarin rescued Grogu from the cage Janu had imprisoned him in and they left the arena. [[File:Din_and_Grogu_on_the_streets_of_Shakari.png|thumb|left|250px|Djarin narrowly avoiding a Mantellian Savrip while he and Grogu chase Rotta the Hutt on the streets of Shakari]] On the city streets, the Dejarik creatures ran amok, causing havoc. Djarin shot a [[Molator]] before Rotta admitted the match was fixed and worked to find them a ride. The Hutt entered a speeder and apologised, telling Djarin he couldn't go back, before leaving without them. Djarin pursued him with his jetpack while Grogu followed behind using his high-speed hover pram. Rotta piloted his speeder onto the train tracks and reached the end of the line, stopped by Zeb in the Razor Crest. Djarin captured the Hutt in and secured him in a hammock in the ship. ====Capturing Commander Janu Coin==== {{Quote|Muster my personal security forces. We're going to hit the streets in full armour. I don't want to take any chances when it comes to the Mandalorian. I've heard many things about those monsters.''"
"''It's all true. Imperial Commander Janu Coin. I'm here on behalf of the New Republic to bring you to justice.''"
"''I'm afraid we're outside of your jurisdiction. Take him!|Janu Coin and Din Djarin|}} In the ship, Djarin told Rotta not to attempt to escape before letting him down from the hammock. Rotta again pleaded to be set free, explaining that the Twins had always been cruel to him and he would be killed if taken back to Nal Hutta. Djarin apologised and told him he was hired to do a job. Rotta asked how he slept at night, working for the Hutts. Djarin explained he was working for the New Republic, taking on a task from the Hutts in exchange for Commander Coin. Rotta told Djarin that Lord Janu and Commander Coin were one and the same, as he was an ex-Imperial and Rotta had once seen him with Stormtroopers. He told him if he did not take this opportunity, he may be gone forever. Djarin asked how he could believe him and Rotta asked him to look in his eyes and use his bounty hunter skills of discernment to tell. Djarin believed him and the four travelled to the beach where Janu Coin's compound was located. [[File:Scouting_Coins_compound.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Din Grogu and Djarin scouting Commander Janu Coin's beach compound on Shakari]] On a dune across from the compound, Djarin, Grogu, Zeb, and Rotta scouted out the building. Zeb noted there were many stormtroopers and Rotta confirmed this from when he was last there, telling Djarin he'd need backup to capture Coin. Djarin infiltrated the building while Coin held a meeting. He told his stormtroopers to patrol the streets in full armour, not wishing to take any chances as he'd heard many stories of the fighting prowess of the Mandalorians. Djarin remarked "it's all true" and outlined how he would apprehend him on behalf of the New Republic. Coin fled and Djarin battled his Stormtroopers. He defeated the troopers but was pinned under a table by Hogsbreath's rapid-fire blaster. He engaged in hand-to-hand combat but was grabbed by the Iktotchi and held against the wall. Djarin activated his flamethrower and left Hogsbreath writhing on the ground. At this moment, Zeb had finished off Coin's Stormtroopers and the two stopped the Imperial Commander from leaving. Djarin told him "I can bring you in warm, or I can bring you in cold" and the two apprehended him and fled the compound. Djarin and Zeb drove back to the Razor Crest in a speeder with the captured Coin, pursued by Stormtroopers in another speeder. Arriving back on Nevarro, Djarin flew near his cabin where he contacted the [[Anzellan Droidsmiths]] to help make modifications to his new gunship. Djarin also contacted a [[Smuggler|gunrunner]] to get Rotta away from his aunt and uncle. Later, Djarin had Rotta stay in his cabin until [[Unidentified gunrunner droid|the gunrunner droid]] landed, where he worked to make modifications on his new Razor Crest, which he also contacted the Anzellan Droidsmith's to help. Seeing a small speeder coming from Nevarro city, Djarin greeted the crew, but told Grogu to yield when he scared the crew, along with their new member [[Clang]]. Then a [[TR-TL3 Terrapin-class bulk tanker|TR-TL3 ''Terrapin''-class bulk tanker]] landed, and Djarin told Rotta he contacted a gunrunner to help get his away from his aunt and uncle, which Rotta thanked him for and warned him to lay low. Later, Djarin worked late at night to make modifications, when he saw his Blurrgs acting strange. Turning on the infrared from his helmet, he saw they were warning him to two intruders. Djarin woke Grogu and the four Anzellans, opening up a small trapdoor in the floor, telling Grogu to leave when he heard the signal. One of the strangers climbed up onto the roof, where Djarin signaled Grogu to leave with the Anzellans before he placed a grav charge on the roof. As the falling roof pieces landed, Djarin attempted to kill the intruder with his blaster. [[Embo]], the intruder, used his [[Kyuzo war shield|saucer hat]] to block the blaster fire before using a device that emitted a bright flash that disorientated Djarin, due to his helmet's thermal vision, and the intruder sprinting out of the front door. Recovering from the bright flash, Djarin chased after him, but upon hearing a cry, Djarin assumed it was Grogu but ran into a trap, where he was captured in a [[net]] and it electrified him unconscious. As Embo summoned his ship the [[Guillotine (starship)|''Guillotine'']] and contacted the Hutt Twins, who ordered Embo to bring Djarin to Nal Hutta, he dragged Djarin's unconscious body while his [[anooba]] [[Keibu]] arrived with one of the droidsmiths named [[Minch]]. As Embo flew through hyperspace to Nal Hutta, Djarin woke up in a cell and saw Keibu playing with Minch with her jaws. Thinking fast, Djarin pulled out one of Grogu's treats and enticed the female anooba to get it while he urged Minch to get into his cell to avoid Keibu. When Keibu noticed Minch running to the cell, she charged at him, but Djarin managed to pull the Anzellan inside, with Keibu growling in anger. This caught the attention of Embo, who came out of the cockpit. Noticing he was a [[Kyuzo]], Djarin asked who had hired him, but before Djarin could finish speaking, Embo pressed a button on the wall and shocked him unconscious. Arriving on Nal Hutta, Embo led Djarin to the throne room in the Hutt Palace where the twins paid Embo. After he and Keibu left, the Twins had one of their [[mercenary sentry droid]]s take off Djarin's helmet to sell the Mandalorian steel on the [[black market]] and shame him even further from the [[Mandalorian Creed]] for breaking their agreement. The twins further showed that Embo also delivered Rotta to them a few days earlier, which made Djarin realize Rotta was right that the twins were monsters. As the brother taunted Djarin that Grogu will be next, he attempted to kill them but the Hutt brother triggered a trapdoor. Djarin then fell into their pit, where he swam up and fought five [[Amani]] warriors, killing each of them with one of their [[spear]]s. A [[Hutt's dragonsnake|dragonsnake]] then emerged, and, despite managing to reclaim his helmet and injuring the snake's mouth, the [[dragonsnake]] injured him with its lethal [[poison]], with the Twins taunting him that even if he wins he will die from the poison bite. Grogu then used a grav charge to blow a hole that allowed them to escape. After escaping, Djarin asked how Grogu and the Anzellan got to Nal Hutta, which one of them told him they took their starship, which Djarin ran with the small aliens to where they parked their [[Anzellan Starship]]. Upon seeing the ship, Djarin quickly realized he couldn't fit in it, and decided to hold off the droids, but the dragonsnake injury worsened his condition, as he defeated a [[B-1 series mercenary sentry droid]] from a [[Single Trooper Aerial Platform]] and a [[B-2 series mercenary sentry droid]], taking one of their [[E-5 blaster rifle]]s. Upon seeing the Anzellan Starship take off, Djarin assumed Grogu and the Anzellans escaped, and collapsed due to the poison. Grogu stayed behind and created a small mudhut to protect Djarin from the droids as they scanned for his whereabouts in the jungle. During the next few days, Grogu met an [[Gatori's species|alien]] [[fisher]] named [[Gatori]], stealing one of the alien's [[Unidentified Nal Hutta fish|fish]] before returning the next night, but befriended the fisher, who was later visited by Embo and Keibu. While Grogu hid, Embo told Gatori that his target Djarin was bitten by a dragonsnake and after both Embo and Keibu left, Gatori mixed some [[Plant|herbs]] and created an [[antidote]] for the [[Dragonsnake venom antidote|dragonsnake venom]] but warned it might have been too late to save Djarin. ====The old protect the young==== Grogu returned to the mudhut and feed the antidote to Djarin. The next morning, Djarin woke up and recovered, which he thanked Grog for staying "The old protect the young, then the young protect the old. This is the Way." Finding a way off the planet, the two set off into the jungle where Grogu took him to the turtle tanker ship, which Djarin recognized as the same ship from the gunrunner he hired to get Rotta away from the Twins. Looking inside, he was soon attacked by several Amani warriors, but Djarin shot them with his blaster and stabbed the last ones with his vibroblade. Seeing the gunrunner droid's destroyed body and found out that the turtle tanker is still operational. Knowing the Twins would continue to hunt him and Grogu, the two agreed to fight the Hutts and save Rotta. Djarin then took several weapons from the shelves; two [[machete]]s, a blaster pack, vibroblades, and a new Amban [[disruptor rifle]] before piloting the Turtle Tanker out of the swamps and crashing into the Hutt Palace, despite the initial resistance from the HH-87 Starhoppers and [[turbolaser]] towers. Once inside the palace, Djarin flew on a [[Single Trooper Aerial Platform]], destroying several droids before heading to the throne room on foot where he threw a grav charge to misdirect a patrol and fought another patrol off. Once at the throne room, Djarin faced against two large droids [[Arges (droid)|Arges]] and [[Bullethead]]. Attempting to stun Arges with his disruptor rifle, Djarin managed to stun Bullethead with his rifle prongs but was flanged into a wall by Bullethead's [[club]]. After dodging Arges' fire, Djarin managed to take cover and fire back on Arges, but the droid was not stunned. Thanks to Grogu, Arges' [[wrist blaster]] malfunctioned and Bullethead threw several grenades which stunned Djarin. As Arges attempted to kill Djarin, Grogu managed to cause the droid to misfire again at Bullethead, allowing Djarin to activate Bullethead's grenades on its belt, destroying Bullethead and cutting Arges before stabbing it in the eye. After Grogu came out, Djarin used his flamethrower and broke into the throne room. Approaching the twins, the two Hutts begged Djarin to spare them due to their valuable intel, but Djarin has Grogu released Rotta and attempted to kill the twins with his new Amban disruptor rifle for seeing his face. Although Keibu caused him to misfire and he faced Embo, who wielded two [[sickle]]s. Attempting to shoot his attacker, the Kyuzo's hat protected him before throwing Djarin across the room. Pulling out two machetes, the two hunters dueled, with Djarin managing to knock Embo down despite his opponent's superior skill. As the fight continued, Rotta battled the Twins and Grogu [[Taming beasts|tamed]] Keibu with the Force, while Djarin was kicked in the head, protected by his beskar helmet but losing one of his swords in the process. Despite losing his last sword, Djarin managed to get Embo to lose one of his sickles, forcing the Kyuzo to use his saucer hat. Continuing to battle Embo, Djarin was hit in the chest by Embo's hat but he managed to overpower the Kyuzo, disarming him of his remaining sickle and pinning him to the ground. Seeing Rotta was destroying the trapdoor, Djarin abandoned his opponent and headed to his Amban rifle, using it to stun Embo, which caused Keibu to protect Embo's unconscious body. After Rotta caused the trapdoor to collapse, Grogu managed to save Rotta while both Embo and Keibu escaped through the same tunnel, Djarin escaped from, and the Twins were eaten by their own dragonsnake while Djarin watched. Hearing the throne room doors banging, Djarin had Rotta and Grogu find an exit while he held off the droids, shooting Arges in the head. Reloading his rifle, he shot several sentry droids before more Droid Gotra droids arrived. Pinned, Djarin received a comlink transmission from the Anzellans who came back for him with the Adelphi Rangers led by Colonel Ward. As Ward asked for his status, Djarin told her that he, Grogu, and Rotta were under attack and outnumbered. He directed her to his location to fire everything they had, which she reluctantly did while she was in range. Assuring her he and his allies would be out of the Hutt Palace by the time she arrived, she ordered Blue Squadron to ready their armaments. Fighting off the sentry droids, Djarin caught up to Rotta and Grogu, finding the two blocked by a wall. He then used his Amban rifle to blow a hole out. As Ward told Djarin her squadron was closing in fast, Djarin had Rotta and Grogu jump, despite the Hutt's reluctance. As the bombers destroyed the Hutt palace, Zeb picked up the trio in his U-Wing for a hot extraction and headed to the Adelphi Base. At the base, Ward joked how messy the mission was, with Djarin questioning why she came for him since it wasn't part of the mission. Ward tells him that he was right and Coin told them everything, that the Twins were playing them and feeding information to the Empire all along. Since they picked a side and took one of their own behind, it was a reason to rescue Mando. As Ward left, Djarin offered to take Rotta somewhere, but Rotta decided to stay and aid the New Republic, with Zeb offering a uniform and buying Rotta a drink. As they departed Adelphi in the new Razor Crest, Djarin gave Grogu permission to initiate the jump to hyperspace. ==Personality and traits== ===Mysterious warrior=== {{Quote|Greef Karga said you were coming.''"
"''What else did he say?''"
"''He said you were the best in the parsec. ''[…]'' He also said you were expensive. Very expensive.|audio=Client-Expensive.flac|The Client and Din Djarin|}} [[File:The_Mandalorian_First_Look.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Mysterious, weary from battle, and tight-lipped, Djarin was a lone gunfighter and a formidable Mandalorian bounty hunter.]] Din Djarin was a lone Mandalorian warrior whose past and identity were a mystery to others, and he remained battle-worn and laconic as a formidable bounty hunter in the galaxy. A human male, he had [[Color|dark]] [[hair]], brown [[eye]]s, and tan skin. A natural loner, Din Djarin was often aloof, tight-lipped, and generally silent. He rarely spoke unless spoken to, and had a tendency to let his action speak for themselves. However, under this cold exterior, laid a much softer side. While he was ruthless and unforgiving to members of the seedy underworld, he refrained from showing this side to the innocent and helpless. This softer side was the catalyst for his bond with Grogu. In addition to his softer side, Din Djarin was also extremely loyal to those that have helped him, and never forgot his allies. He insisted to pay Kuiil for his work when they restored the Razor Crest despite the Ugnaught's hesitation, helped Greef Karga rid Nevarro of the remaining Imperial Remnant free of charge, and refused payment when Boba Fett called upon him during Fett's war with the Pyke Syndicate, instead opting to assist Fett on goodwill alone. He refused to abandon Fett, even when Fett suggested that he should leave because their forces were drastically outnumbered. Djarin stated that it was against the Creed to go back on his word, and he was willing to stay even if it resulted in his death.{{BOBF|Chapter 7: In the Name of Honor}} When confronting the Mythrol, Djarin captured his target without hesitation and later froze the Mythrol upon seeing the target tinkering around in the ''Razor Crest''. As a hunter, he was considered one of the best by Karga of the Bounty Hunters' Guild, with his skills making him the galaxy's best hunter during his era.''[[The Mandalorian: A Clan of Two]]'' Karga viewed Djarin as his "most valuable partner" following the Mandalorian's successful capture of the Child. However, Djarin never celebrated his success, choosing to continue on to the next job. [[File:Mando3-textlessKenLashleycover.png|thumb|right|250px|Din Djarin: a warrior, devout Mandalorian, and father]] Djarin, despite his profession, does not care excessively about money, but sees it as a means of earning a living. For example he refused yet another commission from the Ishi Tib guild master despite not having paid him, since he was only looking for information about the [[Mandalorian covert]]. Djarin displayed a shy personality towards other individuals, such as Caben, Stoke, and people he had worked with before, like Xi'an and Malk. Djarin also rejected a life with the widowed Omera as he felt he did not belong at the village. During the standoff with Davan, Djarin was the only individual to holster his blaster, attempting to defuse the situation between the soldier and Mayfeld's team of mercenaries. On the contrary, Djarin was close to the Tribe, and had a special interest in the foundlings, as he had been one before. He ensured that they received any of his excess beskar. He took the Creed of his tribe to heart, following its traditions and ways to the letter, most notably his utter refusal of taking off his helmet in front of others regardless of the situation. However, Djarin came to care for Grogu so much that he broke this code. Djarin was glad to have become a Mandalorian, and was notably angered to see the discarded armor of his fellow Mandalorians, determined to stay behind at the sewers and fight the Imperials as revenge. Mandalorians that did not follow the Way were not Mandalorians in his eyes. Djarin was not used to being one of those who killed in cold blood, when he knew that there was a human guard in the New Republic prison, sparing his life while his companions refused. He also showed mercy to Doctor Penn Pershing, for experimenting with [[Din Grogu|Grogu]]. ===Attitude towards droids=== {{Quote|Sorry, gang. Come on. You know he doesn't like droids.''"
"''May as well let them have at it. The ''Crest'' needs a good once-over.''"
"''Oh! So he likes droids now.|Peli Motto, noticing Djarin's changing feelings about droids|}} Being a survivor of an attack on his home by battle droids during the Clone Wars, Djarin was left with a hatred of droids that he carried on with for most of his life, which he demonstrated at times such as when he rejected a brand-new speeder driven by a droid for a human-operated one. He made this behavior clear to various individuals, such as a Kubaz ferryman, Peli Motto, and Cara Dune. He was also greatly distrustful of IG-11 despite his reprogramming, insisting on keeping the droid away from Grogu at all costs. [[File:AtmosphericAnalysis-Chapter18.png|thumb|left|250px|Djarin employed R5-D4 as a companion in his travels.]] After witnessing IG-11 protect the infant with his life, however, Djarin's outlook on him changed, and he allowed the droid to take off the Mandalorian's helmet and heal his head injury. He was saddened when IG-11 chose to sacrifice himself for Grogu's safety. Following these events, his dislike of droids in general lessened; the brief friendship he had developed with IG-11 greatly improved his outlook on the mechanical beings. In fact, he even allowed Motto's DUM-series pit droids to conduct repairs on the ''Razor Crest'', although Motto ordered her droids to be careful, believing Djarin only barely trusted automatons. Later, when he constructed his N-1 starfighter with Motto, he allowed her droids to help them, and cooperated with her BD unit. When he searched for Grogu in Luke's academy, he called R2-D2 a "friend". ===Relationships=== ====Din Grogu==== {{Quote|If his parent gave permission, couldn't he then become a Mandalorian apprentice?''"
"''Yes, but his parents are far from here, if they are even alive.''"
"''Then I will adopt him as my own.|Din Djarin, and the Armourer|}} [[File:DinDjarinAndGrogu-CoverArt.png|thumb|left|250px|Din Djarin cared greatly for the foundling Grogu.]] Grogu became one of the few beings whom Din Djarin truly bonded with, which started from the beginning of his relationship with the small alien. Despite his cold demeanor, he did not allow Grogu to be killed—even when the Client allowed his termination for a smaller reward—and instead destroyed IG-11 before the droid could eliminate Grogu. Throughout his time on Arvala-7, he protected Grogu from various threats, and strictly refused to sell him to a tribe of Jawas. When he finally delivered Grogu to the Client, Djarin felt remorse upon powering up the ''Razor Crest'' to depart Nevarro, and returned to the Imperial facility to rescue him, even going close to death in an encounter with the Bounty Guild by shielding the infant from laser fire. Later, he showed his care for Grogu in searching for a place where they could happily reside away from bounty hunters, and was willing to leave Grogu behind in a remote village on Sorgan for the infant's sake. When dealing with Motto, Djarin specifically requested that her pit droids stay away from his ship, but later thanked the mechanic when he saw her taking care of Grogu. Upon being reminded of the Way of the Mandalore by the Armorer, which dictated that he had to be responsible for Grogu's welfare far more than just the infant's protection, he decided to search the galaxy for Grogu's species. A strong emotional bond existed between Djarin and Grogu, which Ahsoka Tano sensed through the Force. She described Djarin as a father figure to Grogu. He considered Grogu to be his closest friend,{{InsiderCite|213|A Certain Point of View}} and became his adopted [[Parent|father]]. Djarin went to great lengths to rescue Grogu after the Child was abducted by Moff Gideon, to the point of bending and breaking the rules of the Mandalorian creed that he was raised to uphold. [[File:WayoftheMandalore-TMH.png|thumb|right|250px|Grogu held by Din Djarin]] Despite his objection to removing his helmet in public, Djarin did so before giving Grogu to Luke Skywalker, allowing the Child to see his face for the first time. Before parting ways, he promised that they would see each other again. Later, he asked the Armorer to reforge his beskar spear into an armor for Grogu. He missed Grogu, and tried to visit him during Grogu's training, but was stopped by Ahsoka Tano. All the same, Grogu would chose to reunite with him, resulting in a joyous reunion during the chaos of the Battle for Mos Espa. With Grogu having chosen the Mandalorian people over the path of the Jedi, Djarin was eager for his foundling to prove himself and begin his formal training, with Bo-Katan Kryze comparing it to how her own father acted.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 20: The Foundling}} ====Greef Karga==== {{Quote|The people of Nevarro appreciate all you've done, Mando. I want to give you this deed to a cabin just outside of town where you can lay low with your new family if you choose so. Between adventures.|Greef Karga to Din Djarin|}} As magistrate of the bounty hunters guild on Nevarro, Greef Karga became a frequent employer of Din Djarin during the New Republic Era. Karga recognised his great track record, and consequently gave him a highly classified Imperial bounty for the alien Grogu. Unaware that his target was a child, Djarin agreed to the job and was ultimately successful. However, after forming a bond with the tiny creature, the Mandalorian returned to free Grogu from the clutches of the Empire, causing conflict with Karga, who brought many mercenaries with him to confront Djarin. Though Djarin ultimately escaped, his tarnished business relationship with Karga prevented him from accepting further formal employment. Greef Karga later struck a deal with the Empire to lure Djarin back to Nevarro under the story that he required assistance freeing the planet from Inperial presence, before killing him, and kidnapping the child. The Mandalorian soon arrived with his allies, and reluctantly followed along with the magistrate. However, after Karga likewise developed a care for Grogu, he betrayed his arrangement with the remnant and informed Djarin of what was happening. Together, Djarin and Karga returned to the Empire, pretending their plan to reclaim Grogu was successful. In the ensuing battle following the arrival of Moff Gideon, Djarin and Karga worked together to remove the imperial presence, and ultimately restore peace to the city by defeating the Warlord. With Karga now acting as magistrate of the town, the two developed an even greater respect for one another, and exchanged pleasantries before Djarin departed the planet with Grogu. ====Boba Fett==== {{Quote|I'm with you until we both fall.|Din Djarin to Boba Fett|}} [[File:Mando6-Andrewstextless.png|thumb|left|250px|Din Djarin and Boba Fett quickly became close friends.]] Boba Fett and Din Djarin had a strong relationship as friends{{DisneyGallery|Disney Gallery: The Book of Boba Fett|The Book of Boba Fett}} and brothers-in-arms.{{SideshowCite|set=Art Prints|pack=Brothers In Arms|link=collectibles/star-wars-brothers-in-arms-502506UL}} The two shared similarities including their their lifestyle and profession. Despite Fett initially threatening Djarin when the pair first met on Tython, they later became friends and grew a mutual trust and respect for one another. Their relationship began after the death of Fett's Tusken tribe, after which Fett decided to take over Jabba's Palace and become the new Daimyo of Tatooine.{{BOBF|Chapter 4: The Gathering Storm}} However, Fett first required his armor that he had lost after his escape from the Sarlaac Pit. Djarin was in possession of the armor, having been gifted it by Cobb Vanth for his aid defeating the Krayt Dragon that terrorized his town. During his travels, Djarin ventured to Tython, where he was unknowingly followed by Fett. Upon his arrival, the latter initially threatened Djarin for the armor, though soon changed his tune and decided to take a more peaceful approach. Fett agreed that in exchange for his armor, he would help protect Djarin's adopted son: Grogu. However, two Imperial transports were sent down from Moff Gideons light cruiser, and a skirmish ensued. Fett and Shand assisted Djarin in fending off the Imperial forces, however, Grogu was captured by Dark Troopers in the process. Fett agreed that he would help Djarin rescue Grogu, and would stay with him until Grogu was returned safely. Fett and Shand then assisted Djarin on his mission to Morak, and later on the attack on Gideon's cruiser. Eventually, Grogu was safe, and Fett headed to Tatooine to take over Jabba's Palace. During his reign as Daimyo, Fett learned of a war being planned by the Pyke Syndicate. Intent on keeping his new home safe, Fett and Shand asked Djarin for aid. Djarin agreed to help for free out of respect for Fett. After Shand realized the Fett Gotra had no foot soldiers, Djarin visited Freetown to ask for their support. Two Pyke Syndicate soldiers had destroyed the Sanctuary in Mos Espa, leading Fett, Shand and Djarin to investigate. However, in the midst of their investigation, Fett's old rival Cad Bane showed up to negotiate on behalf of the Pyke Syndicate. Djarin backed up his friend. After one of the sectors of Mos Espa fell under attack, Shand rushed off to give her support. [[File:MandoCombo-BoBFCh7.png|thumb|right|300px|Djarin and Fett fighting alongside one another.]] Despite being outnumbered by the Pyke forces, Djarin refused to abandon Fett, stating that he would be with him until they both fell. The two then fought off all the Pyke forces together. They were nearly defeated until the people of Freetown showed up to support them. Djarin and Fett then fought against two walkers together, before they realized they couldn't defeat them with their weapons. Fett asked Djarin to distract them while he returned to the Palace to collect his Rancor. When Fett returned, Djarin helped the foot soldiers while Fett faced the walkers and eventually Cad Bane. When the battle was over, Fett thanked Djarin for his service, before Djarin headed off to complete his quest on Mandalore. ==Equipment== {{Quote|I'm a Mandalorian, weapons are part of my religion. |Din Djarin, to Kuiil|}} [[File:TheMandalorian-Fathead.png|thumb|left|280px|Djarin originally wore armor composed of both beskar and durasteel pieces.]] Djarin was a warrior who initially wore a set of durasteel [[Din Djarin's armor|Mandalorian armor]] utilizing pieces made from beskar, which included a shoulder pauldron, helmet, and heartplate. The bounty hunter began replacing some of the damaged armor pieces with his payment of beskar from the Client; eventually, he achieved a full beskar body suit of a helmet; plated vest; two pauldrons, with one later bearing his signet, the mudhorn; two [[Mandalorian vambrace|vambraces]];, two gauntlets; two greaves; and two boots. He also earned a [[JTZ-18 jetpack]] made from beskar, which could be controlled remotely when he was not wearing it. Djarin's final suit also included non-beskar components, including [[bandolier]]s, a [[cape]], and a belt with a pistol [[holster]]. His helmet was capable of tracking heat signatures and long-range audio, and could detect recent footprints left on the ground by using his left vambrace. His left vambrace was equipped with a [[whistling bird]] launcher that could shoot twelve explosive projectiles. However, he lost the whistling bird launcher during the [[Liberation of Mandalore]].{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-mandalorian-and-grogu-trivia|text=''Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu'' Behind-the-Scenes Facts and Trivia|author=StarWars.com Team|date=2026-05-25}} Both vambraces contained a [[flamethrower]] and a [[whipcord launcher]]. He usually carried an [[IB-94 blaster|IB-94]] [[The Mandalorian's IB-94 blaster pistol|blaster pistol]] holstered in his belt, a [[Vibroknife|vibro-knife]] [[sheath]]ed in his boot, and an [[Amban phase-pulse blaster]], which he carried ammunition for in one of his bandoliers. He also carried [[flash charge]]s, [[grav charge]]s, and [[Smoke grenade|smoke bombs]]. [[File:BeskarSpear-TMCh13.png|thumb|right|250px|Din Djarin in his full beskar armor while carrying the beskar spear he was gifted by Ahsoka Tano.]] The ''Razor Crest'' itself had an arsenal of weapons in a locker aboard the Razor Crest, such as a [[Relby-v10 micro grenade launcher]], an [[EE-3 carbine rifle]], a [[DL-21 blaster pistol]], and a [[M-32 light repeating blaster rifle|drum blaster]]. While on Tatooine, Djarin made use of a [[Zephyr-J speeder bike]] that had previously belonged to Toro Calican. Djarin also has a smaller [[hold-out blaster]] which he briefly placed along with all of his remaining weapons in a checked cargo box in order to board a transport ship to Tatooine. He also collected the weapons and armor of Mandalorian design, although he did not generally carry and use them: a [[Boba Fett's armor|vest]], [[Z-6 jetpack|jetpack]] with [[Missile|single-shot missile]] launcher, and [[helmet]] with [[Rangefinder|aiming device for the missile launcher]] collected on Tatooine, which was later recovered by Boba Fett on Tython and a [[beskar spear]] collected on Corvus. After defeating Moff Gideon in combat, Djarin acquired the [[Darksaber]]. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|A mysterious lone gunfighter…with a questionable moral character…and he's a badass.|Pedro Pascal, on Din Djarin|}} Din Djarin is the protagonist of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' television series ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'', created by [[Jon Favreau]]. The first picture of the Mandalorian warrior was revealed on [[October 4]], [[2018]].{{SW|url=news/the-mandalorian-revealed|text=''The Mandalorian'' First Image, Directors Revealed}} On [[November 13]], 2018, [[Pedro Pascal]] was reported to be in negotiations to play the lead role in the series,{{WebCite|url=https://io9.gizmodo.com/the-mandalorian-picks-up-game-of-thrones-pedro-pascal-a-1830414626|text=''The Mandalorian'' Picks Up ''Game of Thrones''{{'s}} Pedro Pascal as Its Lead|author=Lussier, Germain|date=2018-11-13|work=[[Wikipedia:Gizmodo|''Gizmodo'']]|archivedate=20191102030157}} and on [[December 12]], 2018, it was officially announced that Pascal would portray the titular character of the series.{{SW|url=news/pedro-pascal-revealed-as-the-mandalorian|text=Pedro Pascal Revealed as ''The Mandalorian''}} [[File:The_Mandalorian_DF_sketch.png|thumb|left|220px|Dave Filoni's sketches of the Mandalorian]] After [[Lucasfilm]] president [[Kathleen Kennedy]] turned to Favreau to work on something for the release of [[Disney+]], he said he had interest and an idea. By the time Favreau was officially hired, he had written the first four episodes about a Mandalorian. In a meeting between Favreau and [[Dave Filoni]], they exchanged ideas and drawings for a Mandalorian show. Filoni combined his knowledge of Mandalorian history with Favreau's concept of a lone gunslinger.{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2022/05/star-wars-cover-the-rebellion-will-be-televised|text=''Star Wars:'' The Rebellion Will Be Televised|author=Breznican, Anthony|date=2022-05-17|work=[[Wikipedia:Vanity Fair (magazine)|''Vanity Fair'']]|archivedate=20220517110251}} After being recruited by Favreau, Pascal prepared for the role by watching classic [[Wikipedia:Clint Eastwood|Clint Eastwood]] Westerns and [[Wikipedia:Akira Kurosawa|Akira Kurosawa's]] [[Wikipedia:Samurai|samurai]] films. In an interview with [[Wikipedia:USA Today|''USA Today'']], he stated, "Any time I had a question or a physical doubt about a moment, I was always like, 'What would Clint do? How would he shrug this off? How would he walk away from this?{{' "}}{{WebCite|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/tv/2019/11/11/what-to-know-disney-star-wars-spinoff-the-mandalorian/2532565001|text='The Mandalorian': How Disney+ 'Star Wars' spinoff amps up Western grit with guns and droids|author=Keveney, Bill|date=2019-11-11|work=[[Wikipedia:USA Today|''USA Today'']]|archivedate=20191226052613}} While Pascal served as the voice of the titular character for the majority of the season,{{WebCite|url=https://www.syfy.com/syfywire/pedro-pascal-under-helmet-the-mandalorian|text=The Mandalorian: Pedro Pascal isn't always under the helmet — It's sometimes John Wayne's grandson|author=Weiss, Josh|date=2019-12-10|work=[[Wikipedia:Syfy#Syfy_Wire|Syfy Wire]]|archivedate=20200103105747}} [[Brendan Wayne]], [[Lateef Crowder]], and [[Barry Lowin]] served as stunt doubles. [[Aidan Bertola]] portrayed the character as a young boy in flashbacks. [[Stephen Jackson]] served as a stand-in in "[[Chapter 5: The Gunslinger]]." As of [[February]] [[2024]], according to ''Mandalorian'' actress [[Emily Swallow]], Wayne is the main suit actor for Djarin—crediting Djarin's cowboy-like walk to Wayne's heritage as John Wayne's grandson—and Pascal only does the character's voice. The third major player in bringing Djarin to life according to Swallow is [[Lateef Crowder]], whom she described as a "fighting machine." That the three were able to work so well together and bring Djarin to life is an art in-and-of-itself in Swallow's eyes.{{YouTube|video=F2jmWi-f144|text=THE MANDALORIAN Star Emily Swallow On Her Journey Into The STAR WARS Universe! | Ep 52|channel=BrotherlyLovePod|name=Brotherly Love Pod}} [[File:MandoSunset.jpg|thumb|right—|220px|Din Djarin]] At the beginning, Pascal established Djarin's physical specificity in some ways. He observed and picked up from what Crowder and Wayne did when they were wearing the armor.{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/tv/pedro-pascal-the-mandalorian-star-wars-celebration-interview|text=Pedro Pascal praises his ''Mandalorian'' doubles: 'They do the heavy lifting'|author=Coggan, Devan|date=2022-07-29|archivedate=20220729223558}} Pascal said that wearing the armor was "like putting on a head-to-toe glove with weights on it." He said wearing the helmet is like going blind due to the lack of peripheral vision and his breath fogging up the narrow slit. Despite this, Pascal felt powerful and like a protector when he wore the armor. Over the course of ''The Mandalorian'' and ''[[Star Wars: The Book of Boba Fett]]'', the costume was finessed and made more comfortable, but there were still problems seeing in the helmet.{{WebCite|url=https://www.empireonline.com/tv/news/pedro-pascal-cant-see-shit-in-mandalorian-armour|text=Pedro Pascal ‘Can't See Shit' In The Mandalorian Armour: ‘If There's A Hole, I'm Gonna Fall Into It'|author=Travis, Ben|date=2023-02-13|work=[[Wikipedia:Empire (magazine)|''Empire'']]|archivedate=20230213122319}} The real name of the titular character was revealed by Pascal in an interview conducted by ScreenSlam released on the same day as [[Chapter 1: The Mandalorian|Chapter 1]] of the [[The Mandalorian Season One|first season]], with the website spelling the name "Dyn Jarren."{{YouTube|video=11wor2uDnkA|text=The Mandalorian: Pedro Pascal Official TV Interview - Disney Plus|channel=channel/UCJ3P8KTy3e_dqYk5inEYOMw|name=ScreenSlam}} He was finally named in the show in the [[Chapter 8: Redemption|eighth chapter]] of the first season, with the subtitles spelling "Din Djarin." [[File:LegoMando.png|thumb|left|250px|LEGO Din Djarin]] A Mandalorian helmet that heavily resembles{{GEAttr|Dok-Ondar's Den of Antiquities}} the one worn by Djarin is in [[Dok-Ondar's Den of Antiquities]] in the [[Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge|''Star Wars'': Galaxy's Edge]] theme park. The helmet is hung next to an Amban phase-pulse blaster, the same blaster model Djarin used. However, after a fan suggested a timeline as to how the Mandalorian's gear ended up at the Den of Antiquities, [[Matt Martin]] of the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] stated he did not believe it was Djarin's helmet.{{Twitter|missingwords|status/1165074204884008961|[[Matt Martin]]|quote=Not bad, although I'd assume that's not THE Mandalorian's helmet in Dok's.}} At Disney's [[Wikipedia:D23 (Disney)|D23 Expo]] in [[2022]], it was announced that Djarin and Grogu would be included as characters at Galaxy's Edge. On [[December 2]], 2020, Djarin was added as an outfit in ''[[Fortnite]]''{{'s}} fifth season of its second chapter, alongside cosmetics based on both Grogu and the ''Razor Crest''. The outfit features Djarin's beskar armor. Additionally, eliminating an NPC player of Djarin in-game rewarded the player with Djarin's amban phase-pulse blaster, as well as his jetpack.{{SW|url=news/the-mandalorian-joins-fortnite|text=The Mandalorian Joins the Hunt in a New Season of ''Fortnite''}} "[[The Journey of Din Djarin]]," an article by [[Kristin Baver]] in [[Star Wars Insider 216|''Star Wars Insider'' 216]], stated that Djarin became Grogu's adopted [[Parent|father]] prior to the events of [[The Mandalorian Season Three|''The Mandalorian'' Season Three]]. However "[[Chapter 24: The Return]]" featured Djarin formally adopting Grogu during Season Three, not before. Season Three.{{Twitter|starwarsjapan|status/1630583179944837120|Star Wars Japan|date=2023-02-28|quote=@moku_favorite ご参加ありがとうございます✨『マンダロリアン』シーズン3を より楽しむためのキーワードは… ＜ボ＝カターン・クライズ＞ 3/1(水)
